Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef using two forks. Discard herb sprigs and bay leaves.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with a generous amount of beef ragu.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: 7 Up Brined Crispy Chicken Bites
recipes.visual_description: A casual sharing platter presents an inviting arrangement of golden-brown crispy chicken bites. The chicken chunks are irregularly cut, approximately 3 cm, showcasing a crunchy, textured coating. A light scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. Several bright yellow lemon wedges are positioned alongside the chicken, ready for squeezing. The chicken pieces are piled loosely, not geometrically, allowing for a natural, approachable look. The platter, made of clean white porcelain, rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, appealing glow without harsh shadows. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the food's inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a variety of dipping sauces such as honey mustard, ranch, or a spicy barbecue sauce.
Offer alongside a simple coleslaw or potato salad for a complete casual meal.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm irregular chunks.
Combine 7 Up, 5 g salt, 2 g black pepper, 2 g garlic powder, 2 g onion powder, and 2 g smoked paprika in a bowl. Stir well.
Add chicken chunks to the 7 Up mixture. Ensure chicken is submerged. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Prepare dredging stations. In a shallow bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, remaining 5 g salt, 3 g black pepper, 3 g garlic powder, 3 g onion powder, and 3 g smoked paprika.
In a second shallow bowl, whisk eggs and milk until combined.
Drain chicken from brine. Do not rinse. Shake off excess liquid.
Dredge each chicken chunk first in the flour mixture, coating completely. Shake off excess flour.
Dip floured chicken into the egg wash, allowing excess to drip off.
Return chicken to the flour mixture for a second dredge, pressing to ensure a thick, even coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C.
Carefully add chicken chunks to the hot oil in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry chicken for 6-8 minutes, or until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Use a meat thermometer.
Remove fried chicken with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack set over paper towels to drain excess oil.
Immediately season hot chicken with a pinch of salt.
Arrange crispy chicken bites on a serving platter. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Tomato Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Bell Pepper & Tomato Mediterranean Chickpea Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Diced red, yellow, and green bell peppers are brightly interspersed with diced red Roma tomatoes and crisp diced cucumber. Thinly sliced red onion rings and dark, halved Kalamata olives provide contrasting colors and textures. Creamy, beige chickpeas are artfully distributed throughout the vibrant mixture, ensuring every forkful offers varied elements. The ingredients are lightly coated with a glistening lemon-oregano vinaigrette, with a few drops visible on the plate's surface. A generous scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a final pop of color and freshness. The salad is arranged in a gentle mound, showcasing its diverse components without overcrowding. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with natural, even lighting illuminating the fresh ingredients. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate, and a small, rustic ceramic bowl containing a few extra Kalamata olives is subtly positioned in the background, hinting at the Mediterranean theme. The entire composition feels fresh, inviting, and authentically casual.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread or pita.
instructions: Dice red and yellow bell peppers into small cubes.
Dice Roma tomatoes into small cubes.
Dice cucumber into small cubes.
Thinly slice red onion.
Halve pitted Kalamata olives.
Rinse and drain canned chickpeas.
Chop fresh parsley.
In a large bowl, combine diced bell peppers, diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, thinly sliced red onion, halved Kalamata olives, and chickpeas.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, dried oregano, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef & Fermented Mushroom Ragout with Root Puree
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, organic presentation on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. A smooth mound of creamy, off-white root vegetable puree forms the base. Nestled off-center is a rich, dark brown Slow-Braised Beef & Fermented Mushroom Ragout. The beef chunks are deep mahogany, tender, and unsliced. Mixed mushrooms are plump and glossy. The sauce is thick and unctuous. Thin slices of quick-pickled button mushrooms are artfully placed atop, with a scattering of chopped fresh parsley. Earthy browns, creamy off-white, and subtle greens dominate. Textures contrast smooth puree with tender beef and meaty mushrooms. Ample negative space highlights natural forms. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood table. An undyed linen napkin sits beside it. Soft, natural light enhances textures. A clean, minimalist background with a hint of green plant and artisanal flatware complete the sustainable dining experience.
instructions: Prepare mushroom stock: Combine reserved mushroom stems, 500ml water, and any vegetable scraps in a pot. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain.

Prepare quick pickled mushrooms: Slice button mushrooms thinly. Combine apple cider vinegar, 50ml water, 10g sugar, 5g salt in a small saucepan. Bring to boil. Add sliced mushrooms. Simmer 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool in liquid. Add fresh dill or parsley.
Sear beef: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the same pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes more.
Deglaze: Pour in red wine (if using) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce liquid slightly.

Combine and braise: Return beef to the pot. Add mushroom stock, lacto-fermented brine, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to an oven preheated to 160°C. Braise for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add mushrooms: Add fresh mixed mushrooms to the ragout. Cook for another 30 minutes, uncovered, until mushrooms are tender and the sauce thickens slightly.

Prepare root puree: While ragout finishes, boil potato and parsnip chunks in salted water until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Mash with vegetable stock and butter (if using) until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and white pepper.
Finish ragout: Adjust seasoning of the ragout to taste. Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf.

Plate: Ladle a portion of the smooth root puree onto each plate. Top with a generous serving of the Slow-Braised Beef & Fermented Mushroom Ragout. Garnish with a few thin slices of quick-pickled button mushrooms and a scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley or dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Broccoli, and Cheddar Bake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting individual portion of Creamy Chicken, Broccoli, and Cheddar Bake is served on a round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features a golden-brown, bubbly top crust of melted cheddar cheese, revealing hearty 2-3 cm chunks of cooked chicken, tender bright green small broccoli florets, and thinly sliced 2-3 mm potato rounds beneath. Small 0.5 cm diced carrots and sautéed mushrooms are interspersed throughout the creamy, rich sauce. The components are naturally layered, with some sauce and melted cheese pooling slightly at the edges. The scene is set on a well-used, rustic wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, inviting light. A simple, casually folded linen napkin and a silver fork rest beside the plate, emphasizing a homely, family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the comforting, hearty meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes (2-3 cm). Cook until lightly browned, 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion and small diced carrots to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until tender. Stir in diced tomatoes.
Melt butter in a separate large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth until smooth and thickened. Bring to a simmer.
Remove from heat. Stir in 150g grated cheddar until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Combine cooked chicken, sautéed vegetables, and blanched broccoli with the cheese sauce.
Arrange half of the thinly sliced potatoes (2-3 mm thick) in a single layer at the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Spoon half of the chicken and vegetable mixture over the potatoes.
Repeat layers: remaining potatoes, then remaining chicken and vegetable mixture.
Top evenly with the remaining 50g grated cheddar.
Bake for 30-40 minutes. Potatoes should be tender. Top should be golden brown. Sauce should be bubbly. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Lobster Fish Cakes
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of golden-brown Thai Lobster Fish Cakes, irregular in shape, are casually arranged on a simple, round, light-colored ceramic plate. The exterior of the fish cakes appears crispy, revealing tender, subtly red-orange diced lobster meat and thin slices of green beans within. Alongside, a small, clear glass or ceramic bowl holds the vibrant sweet chili cucumber dipping sauce (Ajat), brimming with thin slices of red bird's eye chilies, small diced cucumber, and translucent shallot rings. Fresh cilantro sprigs are naturally scattered around the plate, adding a pop of green. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table under warm, cozy lighting, evoking a relaxed, homestyle Thai snack experience. The dish is presented for sharing, inviting casual eating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a shared appetizer or snack.
Accompany with a traditional sweet chili cucumber relish (Ajat).
instructions: If using raw lobster, poach or steam until cooked. Cool lobster. Dice lobster into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine diced lobster, red curry paste, thinly sliced green beans, finely diced onion, egg, fish sauce, palm sugar, and thinly sliced kaffir lime leaves.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly by hand until well combined and slightly sticky.
Sprinkle in cornstarch. Mix until fully incorporated.
Form the mixture into small, flat patties. Aim for about 2-3 cm thick and 5-6 cm wide.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to 175°C (350°F).
Carefully place fish cakes into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove fish cakes with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Prepare dipping sauce: Combine white vinegar, water, granulated sugar, and fish sauce in a small saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Let cool completely.
Stir sliced red bird's eye chilies, small diced cucumber, sliced shallots, and chopped cilantro into the cooled sauce.
Serve hot fish cakes immediately with the sweet chili cucumber dipping sauce.
traditional_techniques: Pounding ingredients (for curry paste, if homemade)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Skillet is presented on an off-white ceramic plate with a subtle, rustic rim, resting on a well-worn wooden dining table. Generous chunks of pan-seared chicken, cooked to a golden brown exterior, are nestled among vibrant green broccoli florets and whole, tender-crisp green beans. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, coated in a rich, creamy white sauce that pools gently on the plate. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the plate, with a casually folded cloth napkin. The scene is lit by warm, ambient kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a lived-in kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet or plated individually.
Commonly accompanied by steamed rice or egg noodles.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to skillet. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Trim green beans. Add broccoli florets and green beans to the simmering broth.
Cook vegetables for 5-7 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Whisk cornstarch with water in a small bowl until smooth.
Stir cornstarch mixture into the simmering broth in the skillet. Cook until the sauce thickens.
Stir in heavy cream. Return cooked chicken to the skillet.
Heat gently for 2 minutes until warmed through. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Chicken thighs can be used instead of breast for a richer flavor.
Adjust vegetable cooking time based on desired tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Corn Succotash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Corn Succotash is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pan-seared chicken breast, cut into thick, irregular chunks, displays a beautiful golden-brown crust with tender, moist interior visible. These chicken pieces are arranged organically to one side of the plate. Adjacent to the chicken is a vibrant mound of succotash, featuring bright yellow corn kernels and deep green small broccoli florets, intermingled with translucent diced onion and flecks of red chili. The vegetables are tender-crisp, maintaining their distinct shapes and colors. A light sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley or chives garnishes both the chicken and the succotash, adding a fresh contrast. The plate is centered on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and finely diced chili. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add corn kernels and broccoli florets to the pan. Cook 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in butter until melted. Season succotash with salt and pepper.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick chunks or medallions.
Divide succotash evenly among 4 plates. Arrange chicken chunks beside the succotash.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Pisto Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Pisto Skillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown pan-seared chicken thighs, moist and tender, rest atop a vibrant, rustic mound of Pisto. The Pisto features clearly defined 2cm cubes of red and yellow bell peppers and deep purple eggplant, all softened and glistening with a rich tomato-based sauce. Finely diced onions and minced garlic are visible within the colorful vegetable medley. A generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin sits beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful pisto sauce
Pair with a glass of dry Spanish red wine
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken; set aside.
Dice red and yellow bell peppers into 2cm cubes. Dice eggplant into 2cm cubes. Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced bell peppers and eggplant to the skillet. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and red wine vinegar. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Submerge partially in the vegetable mixture. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender. Stir occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Chop fresh parsley.
Serve chicken and pisto immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Medallions with Smoky Chocolate Chili Sauce and Apple Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork Medallions with Smoky Chocolate Chili Sauce is elegantly presented on a clean white round porcelain dinner plate. Three to four thick, golden-brown pork medallions are neatly arranged, showcasing their tender, juicy interior. A rich, dark brown Smoky Chocolate Chili Sauce is generously spooned beneath and partially over the pork, creating a glossy, appealing sheen. Beside the pork, a vibrant, crisp mound of Apple Salsa provides a striking contrast. The salsa features finely diced Granny Smith apples, small cubes of red onion, and bright green flecks of chopped fresh cilantro, adding fresh color and texture. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the focal point. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its colors and textures in a professional, approachable manner, suitable for a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Place dried ancho and guajillo chilies in a small bowl. Cover with boiling water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving 50ml of the soaking liquid.
In a blender, combine rehydrated chilies, reserved soaking liquid, onion, garlic, apple cider vinegar, honey, cumin, coriander, oregano, and cinnamon stick (if using). Blend until very smooth.
Pat pork tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

Transfer the pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, or 75°C (167°F) for well-done. Let pork rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes before slicing.

While pork roasts, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Pour in the blended chili mixture. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and sauce thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes. If sauce is too thick, add a splash of chicken broth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small bowl, combine finely diced Granny Smith apple, finely diced red onion, chopped fresh cilantro, and lime juice. Stir gently to combine.

Slice rested pork tenderloin into 2-3 cm thick medallions. Arrange pork medallions on serving plates. Spoon a generous amount of smoky chocolate chili sauce over and around the pork. Place a mound of fresh apple salsa beside the pork.
notes: Adjust chili quantity for desired spice level. For milder sauce, use fewer chilies or remove more seeds.
The cinnamon stick in the sauce adds subtle warmth; omit if preferred.
Ensure the dark chocolate is unsweetened or very low in sugar for a savory application.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Caramelized Onion Puree, Garlic Confit, Parmesan Tuile
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a singular, artistic composition on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. The plate rests on a cool, veined white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, emphasizing depth and texture. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the plate. The centerpiece is a perfectly seared, thick chunk of beef tenderloin, exhibiting a deep mahogany crust and a promise of succulent medium-rare interior. Adjacent to the beef, a delicate, crescent-shaped swoosh of pale lavender-beige caramelized onion puree provides a soft, elegant contrast. Two to three glossy, golden garlic confit cloves are artfully placed, their rounded forms offering a textural counterpoint. A thin, irregular shard of golden-brown parmesan tuile stands gracefully, adding architectural height and crispness. A few minimalist dots of creamy white mozzarella emulsion are strategically placed around the elements, adding a subtle touch of richness. The composition is clean, uncluttered, and features abundant negative space, allowing each element to shine. A single, vibrant green micro-herb sprig is precisely positioned on the beef or puree for a final touch of color and freshness. The overall presentation is one of refined simplicity, showcasing masterful technique and premium ingredients.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 1 whole head (for confit), 2 cloves (for beef seasoning)

ingredients.name: Fresh Mozzarella (bufala or fior di latte)

instructions: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Place in a vacuum-sealable bag with 2 thyme sprigs and 1 tbsp olive oil. Seal bag.
Set water bath to 54°C (129°F) for medium-rare. Cook beef for 2 hours.

Peel remaining whole garlic head cloves. Place cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with 100 ml olive oil and 1 thyme sprig. Cook over very low heat (barely simmering) for 45-60 minutes, until cloves are very soft and golden. Do not brown. Strain oil (reserve for other uses). Set garlic cloves aside.

Peel and thinly slice onions. Melt 20g butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Add 50 ml beef demi-glace (if using) and a pinch of salt. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smoothness. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grate parmesan cheese finely. Spread thin, even circles (approx. 5-7 cm diameter) of grated cheese on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Remove from oven. Let cool slightly on sheet, then transfer to a wire rack to fully crisp. Break into irregular shards.

Dice fresh mozzarella. In a small saucepan, combine diced mozzarella with 2 tbsp water and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Heat gently over low heat, stirring, until mozzarella melts into a smooth, creamy sauce. If too thick, add a tiny bit more water. Blend with an immersion blender until emulsified and smooth. Keep warm.

Remove beef from sous vide bag. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 30g butter in a cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear beef tenderloin on all sides for 2-3 minutes total, until a deep golden-brown crust forms. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Slice beef into 4 equal, thick chunks. Place one beef chunk slightly off-center on each plate. Create a small, elegant swoosh or dot of caramelized onion puree beside the beef. Arrange 2-3 garlic confit cloves artfully near the puree. Place 1-2 parmesan tuile shards leaning against the beef or puree. Drizzle or dot a small amount of mozzarella emulsion around the plate, or directly onto the beef. Garnish with a few microgreens or finely snipped chives for a pop of color.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken Thighs is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A large, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, with crispy skin and tender meat, is positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, several soft, caramelized red onion wedges and whole, roasted garlic cloves are artfully arranged. Two vibrant yellow lemon wedges provide a bright contrast. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures are varied: crispy chicken skin, succulent chicken, soft onions, and creamy garlic. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. A silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate, with a folded white cotton napkin nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. The background is minimalistic, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to absorb pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Cut red onions into thick wedges. Leave garlic cloves unpeeled.
In a large roasting pan, toss chicken thighs, onion wedges, and whole garlic cloves with olive oil.
Arrange ingredients in a single layer, skin-side up for chicken.
Cut lemon into wedges. Add lemon wedges to the pan.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Zuppa di Pomodoro Fresco
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Zuppa di Pomodoro Fresco is presented in a clean, white porcelain soup bowl. The soup exhibits a vibrant, deep red-orange hue, indicative of ripe tomatoes. It has a visually appealing, rustic texture with small, soft pieces of diced tomato and onion visible, showcasing its partial blending. A generous swirl of bright green extra virgin olive oil adorns the surface. A few fresh, whole basil leaves are gently placed on top as a garnish. The bowl rests on a simple, light wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded light-colored cotton napkin and a polished silver soup spoon are placed beside the bowl. A small, rustic piece of toasted crusty Italian bread is placed on a small side plate beside the bowl, ready for dipping. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Dice the onion and tomatoes. Mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add diced tomatoes and sugar. Stir well.
Add dried oregano. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup. Leave some texture.
Season with salt and black pepper. Adjust sweetness if needed.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chicken and Vegetable Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of vibrant Spiced Chicken and Vegetable Curry is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl. Diced, golden-seared chicken chunks are nestled among bright green broccoli florets and tender orange carrot pieces. The ingredients are coated in a rich, reddish-brown, creamy curry sauce with visible spice flecks. Fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander is generously sprinkled over the top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl is placed on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a small portion of fluffy white basmati rice and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm basmati rice.
Offer with fresh naan bread or roti.
Accompany with a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip).
Serve with mango chutney or pickled lime.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, skinless, diced into 3 cm cubes

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Stir well. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, coconut milk, and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add diced carrots. Stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F) and carrots are tender.
Stir in broccoli florets. Cook for an additional 5-7 minutes, uncovered, until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Stir in garam masala and salt. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander before serving.
notes: Adjust cayenne pepper for desired spice level.
For a thicker curry, simmer uncovered for a longer period.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple-Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of pan-seared chicken breast and apple-potato gratin. The chicken breast is golden-brown with a crisp crust, resting as a whole piece on the plate. Beside it, a generous mound of the gratin features tender, slightly caramelized potato wedges and apple slices, interspersed with al dente noodles. The gratin is topped with a light golden-brown breadcrumb crust, showing hints of melted cheese if used. Colors are warm browns, golden yellows, and creamy whites, with the occasional pop of green from fresh thyme sprigs scattered over the dish. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. A cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its textures. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, maintaining focus on the dish.

ingredients.name: Noodles (e.g., egg noodles or thin spaghetti, broken)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 1 cm thick rounds or wedges.
Core apples. Cut into 1 cm thick slices or wedges, similar to potatoes.
Mince garlic cloves.
Cook noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
In a large oven-safe skillet or baking dish, combine potatoes, apples, cooked noodles, minced garlic, half the chicken stock, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to combine.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
While gratin bakes, prepare chicken. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown.
Transfer chicken to oven with gratin for final 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
If desired, sprinkle breadcrumbs and Parmesan over gratin for the last 10 minutes of baking.
Remove chicken and gratin from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Serve one chicken breast with a generous portion of apple-potato gratin. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Beef Stir-fry with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Peruvian Beef Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. The seared beef strips, cut into 1cm thick pieces, are prominently arranged alongside vibrant, sautéed red onion and bell pepper strips, with golden corn kernels interspersed. The vegetables are crisp-tender, showcasing their natural colors. Roasted potato wedges, golden brown with slightly crispy edges, are neatly arranged beside the stir-fry. A mound of fluffy white rice completes the plate. The entire dish is lightly coated in a glossy, savory sauce. Freshly chopped green cilantro is sprinkled over the beef and vegetables, providing a bright color contrast. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting includes a woven placemat and a simple fork, reflecting a casual bistro atmosphere. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 1.5cm thick wedges. Toss with 30ml vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip halfway.

Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water. Combine rice with 600ml cold water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Slice beef sirloin against the grain into 1cm thick strips. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Slice red onion into thick 1.5cm strips. Slice bell peppers into similar 1.5cm strips. Mince garlic.
Heat remaining 30ml vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add beef strips to the hot pan in a single layer. Sear quickly for 1-2 minutes per side until browned. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove beef from pan and set aside.
Add red onion and bell peppers to the same pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp. Add minced garlic and corn kernels. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared beef to the pan. Add soy sauce, red wine vinegar, Aji Amarillo paste, cumin, and oregano. Toss quickly to coat all ingredients. Cook for 1 minute, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Remove from heat immediately. Stir in half of the chopped fresh cilantro.
Serve the Peruvian beef stir-fry alongside the roasted potato wedges and fluffed white rice. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Herring with Creamy Dill Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Herring with Creamy Dill Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a light wooden table surface. Two golden-brown, crispy-skinned herring fillets, whole and unsliced, are neatly arranged on the plate. Beside them, a generous dollop of creamy, off-white mashed potatoes, studded with vibrant green flecks of fresh dill, sits invitingly. A small, artfully arranged pile of translucent, thinly sliced quick pickled cucumbers adds a refreshing contrast, their pale green edges visible. Fresh dill sprigs are delicately scattered over the potatoes and herring, providing a final touch of color and aroma. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. A simple cotton napkin and classic silver cutlery are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Prepare quick pickled cucumbers: Thinly slice the cucumber into rounds. In a small bowl, whisk together white wine vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add cucumber slices. Let sit for at least 15 minutes.
Boil potatoes: Peel and cut potatoes into uniform chunks. Place in a large pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Prepare creamy dill potatoes: Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot. Add cream, butter, and half of the chopped fresh dill. Mash or crush until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare herring: Pat herring fillets very dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge each fillet in all-purpose flour, shaking off excess.

Pan-sear herring: Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, carefully place herring fillets skin-side down in the pan. Do not overcrowd. Sear for 3-4 minutes until golden-brown and crispy. Flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes until cooked through and flaky.

Plate the dish: Place a portion of creamy dill potatoes on one side of a plate. Arrange 2-3 pan-seared herring fillets next to the potatoes. Drain and place a small portion of quick pickled cucumbers on the plate. Garnish with remaining fresh dill sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Rockfish with Ginger-Scallion Sauce and Bok Choy
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. A single portion of pan-seared rockfish sits prominently, its skin deeply golden and crispy, contrasting with the tender, flaky white flesh. The fish is a whole, unsliced fillet. Alongside the rockfish, vibrant green bok choy halves are arranged neatly, their leaves slightly wilted but still holding shape. A rich, aromatic ginger-scallion sauce, glistening with hot oil, is generously spooned over the rockfish, showcasing finely julienned fresh ginger and thinly sliced green onions. The colors are natural and appealing: golden-brown fish, verdant bok choy, and the amber-toned sauce with flecks of green and white. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. A set of elegant dark wood chopsticks rests beside the plate, accompanied by a small white rice bowl. A simple white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a relaxed restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice on the side.
Offer a small bowl of chili oil for those who prefer more heat.

ingredients.name: Bok choy
ingredients.quantity: 2 large heads, or 4-6 baby bok choy

instructions: Prepare Ginger-Scallion Sauce: Finely julienne 40g ginger. Thinly slice green onions, separating white and green parts. Combine julienned ginger, white parts of green onions, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar in a small bowl. Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a small saucepan until shimmering. Pour hot oil over ginger-scallion mixture. Stir well. Add remaining green parts of scallions. Set aside.
Prepare Rockfish: Pat rockfish fillets dry with paper towels. Season skin side with salt and pepper. Lightly score fish skin a few times to prevent curling.

Sear Rockfish: Heat a large non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 15ml vegetable oil. Once hot, place rockfish fillets skin-side down. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until fish is opaque and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63
R
C (145
R
F). Remove fish from pan. Set aside.

Cook Bok Choy: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml vegetable oil. Add remaining 20g julienned ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds. Add bok choy, cut in half lengthwise if large. Pour in 120ml water or fish stock. Cover and steam for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with a pinch of salt.
Plate Dish: Place cooked bok choy on one side of a plate. Arrange a pan-seared rockfish fillet next to bok choy. Spoon generous amount of ginger-scallion sauce over rockfish. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure fish skin is very dry for maximum crispiness.
Adjust sauce sweetness and saltiness to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Duck Legs with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, crispy duck leg rests on an everyday round ceramic plate. The skin is deeply golden brown, visibly crisp, and slightly puckered from rendering. Surrounding the duck are generous portions of roasted root vegetables: golden potato wedges, bright orange carrot chunks, and tender, slightly charred onion wedges. A few smashed garlic cloves and sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme are nestled among the vegetables. The arrangement is natural and slightly asymmetrical, as if just served from a communal pan. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, with a simple, casually folded cloth napkin to the side. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the comfort food. The overall scene is homely and inviting, reflecting a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: carrots, peeled, cut into 2.5 cm thick chunks
onions, peeled, cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Score duck skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat.
Season duck legs generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck legs skin-side down in a large, cold oven-safe skillet or roasting pan.
Turn heat to medium. Render fat for 10-15 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip duck legs. Cook for 5 minutes on the other side.
Remove duck legs from pan. Pour off most rendered fat into a heatproof container, leaving about 30ml in the pan.
Add potato wedges, carrot chunks, onion wedges, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme to the pan with the duck fat. Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place duck legs on top of the vegetables in the pan.
Roast in preheated oven for 45-60 minutes, or until duck is cooked through and vegetables are tender and caramelized. Internal temperature of duck should reach 75°C (167°F).
Rest duck legs for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Save rendered duck fat for roasting potatoes or other vegetables later.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Roasted Red Pepper Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared cod fillet rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The cod, golden-brown and flaky, is presented as a whole piece. A vibrant, smooth roasted red pepper and tomato sauce pools elegantly beneath and around the cod, its rich red contrasting beautifully with the fish. Alongside, a neat cluster of bright green, tender-crisp asparagus spears provides a fresh counterpoint. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh basil and parsley garnishes the dish, adding specks of green. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits at the plate's edge. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh textures and colors against a softly blurred, modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on baking tray. Roast 25 minutes until skin blisters.
Transfer roasted peppers to a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap 10 minutes. Peel off skins.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté diced shallots 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes to saucepan. Simmer 10 minutes. Break down tomatoes with a spoon.
Combine peeled roasted peppers, tomato mixture, and vegetable broth in a blender. Blend until smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add asparagus. Blanch 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Pat cod fillets very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 45ml olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Place cod fillets presentation-side down. Sear 4-5 minutes until golden brown and a crust forms.
Flip cod. Cook 3-4 minutes until opaque and flakes easily.
Plate each cod fillet on a white porcelain dinner plate. Spoon generous amount of warm red pepper sauce around and under the cod. Arrange blanched asparagus spears beside the cod.
Garnish with chopped fresh basil and parsley. Add a lemon wedge to the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Pork and Vegetable Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Hearty Pork and Vegetable Pasta is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The pasta, likely rigatoni or penne, is coated generously in a rich, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce. Interspersed throughout are substantial 2cm cubes of seared pork, tender and slightly browned, nestled among vibrant 1.5cm diced pieces of red bell pepper, softened yellow onion, and green zucchini. The ingredients are naturally mixed and slightly overlap, creating an inviting, unpretentious appearance. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color. The bowl rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. A simple, casually folded cloth napkin and a fork lie beside the bowl, completing the homely scene.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced pork (2cm cubes). Sear pork until browned on all sides. Remove pork from skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion (1.5cm pieces) to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add diced bell pepper (1.5cm pieces) and diced squash (1.5cm pieces). Cook for 7-8 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared pork to the skillet.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until pork is tender. Stir occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the pork and vegetable sauce. Toss to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Buckwheat & Quinoa Pilaf with Roasted Chickpeas and Date-Verjus Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Middle Eastern Buckwheat & Quinoa Pilaf is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pilaf forms a gentle, organic mound, showcasing the fluffy texture of the golden-brown grains, subtly flecked with finely diced red onion and green herbs. Crispy, golden-brown roasted chickpeas are artfully scattered over and around the pilaf, providing textural contrast. A glistening amber-colored date-verjus dressing is drizzled elegantly over the top, creating delicate streaks. Freshly chopped bright green parsley and mint are sprinkled as a vibrant garnish, along with a scattering of toasted slivered almonds for added crunch and warmth. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's earthy colors and varied textures. The background is minimal, reflecting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and inviting composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread for scooping.
Offer a side of simple cucumber and yogurt salad (Tzatziki or Labneh with cucumber) to balance richness.
Accompany with a small bowl of mixed olives or pickled vegetables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Drain and rinse chickpeas. Toss chickpeas with 15 ml olive oil, 2 g cumin, 2 g coriander, 3 g smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until crispy. Set aside.
Rinse buckwheat and quinoa thoroughly. Combine in a fine-mesh sieve.
Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, remaining cumin, and coriander. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed buckwheat and quinoa to the pot. Stir to coat grains with spices and oil. Toast for 2 minutes.

Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and grains are tender. Do not overcook. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

While grains cook, prepare date-verjus dressing. Roughly chop pitted dates. Combine chopped dates, verjus, and remaining 15 ml olive oil in a small blender or food processor. Blend until smooth. Add a tablespoon of hot water if needed for consistency.
Roughly chop fresh parsley and mint.
Gently fold half of the roasted chickpeas and most of the chopped herbs into the pilaf.
Serve pilaf in individual portions. Top with remaining roasted chickpeas. Drizzle generously with date-verjus dressing. Garnish with remaining fresh herbs and toasted slivered almonds.
notes: For enhanced flavor, lightly toast buckwheat and quinoa in a dry pan before rinsing.
Adjust the sweetness of the dressing by adding more dates or a touch of water as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Curry with Cucumber Raita
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Chicken and Potato Curry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic Indian curry bowl. The rich, reddish-brown curry fills the bowl, showcasing tender chicken chunks and soft potato cubes. A swirl of cream from the yogurt is visible. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh cilantro garnishes the top. Beside the curry bowl, a smaller white porcelain bowl holds the crisp, white cucumber raita, dotted with green chili and cilantro flecks. Chicken is cut into 4cm chunks. Potatoes are cut into 3cm cubes. Onions are finely diced. Cucumber is grated. The curry boasts deep, earthy reds and browns, contrasted by the white of the chicken and potatoes. Textures are tender and yielding. The raita is creamy white with fresh green accents. The bowls are placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the main bowl. A small, unadorned metal spoon for the curry and a smaller spoon for the raita are positioned appropriately. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere with warm, natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly cooked Basmati rice
Serve with warm naan bread or roti
Offer a side of pickled onions or mango chutney

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast
Green Chili
ingredients.quantity: 1, deseeded and finely chopped (optional, for raita)

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onions. Cook until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, coriander, and red chili powder. Cook 30 seconds.
Add pureed tomatoes. Cook until oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add chicken chunks. Sear on all sides until lightly browned.
Add potato cubes and water. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 20-25 minutes, or until chicken and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat. Stir in yogurt until well combined. Do not boil after adding yogurt.
Add garam masala and half of the chopped cilantro. Season with salt.
For raita: Combine grated cucumber, remaining yogurt, cumin seeds, green chili (if using), and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix well.
Serve curry hot, garnished with remaining fresh cilantro. Serve with cucumber raita on the side.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not boil the curry after adding yogurt to prevent curdling.
traditional_techniques: Tempering spices for curry base (bhunao technique)
Adding yogurt off heat to prevent curdling

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Beer Braised Beef with Kidney Beans
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rich stew is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table. Several substantial chunks of fork-tender, dark brown braised beef are nestled amongst vibrant orange carrot rounds and softened celery slices. The deep, glossy dark brown sauce, thickened from the beer reduction, coats the ingredients beautifully. Scattered throughout are plump, dark red kidney beans, adding textural contrast. A neat pile of creamy mashed potatoes sits beside the stew. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley. The presentation is professional yet approachable, reflecting a simple restaurant style. Natural, even lighting illuminates the warm, inviting color palette of deep browns, rich reds, and green accents. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of creamy mashed potatoes.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Dark beer (e.g., stout or Belgian dubbel)

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add diced onions, carrots cut into 1cm rounds, and celery cut into 1cm slices to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Gradually whisk in dark beer and beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Stir in Dijon mustard.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover pot.
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Stir in drained and rinsed kidney beans. Cook for 10-15 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use a good quality dark beer like a Belgian dubbel or a robust stout.
Browning the beef well is crucial for deep flavor development.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken & Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mexican Chicken & Rice Bowl presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. A generous base of fluffy, pale green cilantro-lime rice anchors the dish. Arranged neatly on the rice are irregular, golden-brown seared chicken chunks, showing a slight char. Beside the chicken, a rich, dark mound of smoky black beans, some lightly mashed for texture. Opposite, a bright pile of roasted corn kernels, interspersed with finely diced, vibrant green roasted jalapeno and fresh cilantro flecks. The colors are natural and balanced: verdant greens, deep blacks, sunny yellows, and warm browns. Garnished with a few fresh cilantro sprigs and a bright lime wedge on the rim. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the bowl, and a small stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and freshness.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer lime wedges for additional zest.
A small side of Mexican crema or crumbled Cotija cheese can be offered.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, 5g cumin, and 5g chili powder.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest 5 minutes. Dice into 2 cm chunks.

Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rice, 500ml water, juice of 1 lime, and 5g salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand covered 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped cilantro.

Dice half the onion and 2 cloves garlic. Finely mince 1 jalapeno (remove seeds for less heat). Heat 15ml olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté diced onion, garlic, and minced jalapeno 5 minutes until softened.

Add drained black beans, 250ml chicken broth, 5g cumin, 5g chili powder, smoked paprika, and oregano to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Lightly mash about one-third of the beans with a fork for creaminess. Season with salt and pepper.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Spread frozen corn kernels and the remaining whole jalapeno on a baking sheet. Roast 15-20 minutes, or until corn is lightly charred and jalapeno skin is blistered. Remove from oven.
Dice roasted jalapeno (remove stem and seeds if desired). In a small bowl, combine roasted corn, diced roasted jalapeno, juice of 1 lime, and remaining chopped cilantro. Season with salt.

Divide cilantro-lime rice among four large bowls. Arrange diced seared chicken chunks on one side of the rice. Spoon black beans next to the chicken. Place corn-jalapeno salsa on the remaining side. Garnish each bowl with a few fresh cilantro sprigs and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken & Corn Bake
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mexican Chicken & Corn Bake is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table. The dish features tender, seared chicken chunks interspersed with bright diced red and green bell peppers, sweet corn kernels, and roasted broccoli florets, all coated in a rich, savory tomato sauce. Melted, bubbly shredded cheddar cheese and sliced black olives form a golden-brown crust on top, adding texture and color. Freshly chopped cilantro is scattered generously, providing a pop of green. A vibrant lime wedge sits on the rim of the bowl. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. In the background, a small rustic basket holds warm corn tortillas, suggesting a complete, authentic meal. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Lime wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 10ml olive oil, 1g salt, and 0.5g pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with 2g salt and 1g pepper. Add to hot pan. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 10ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion and bell peppers. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, drained corn, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Stir to combine.
Transfer chicken and vegetable mixture to a 2L baking dish if not using an oven-safe pan.
Scatter roasted broccoli florets over the mixture.
Top evenly with shredded cheddar cheese and sliced black olives.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken & Sausage Galantine, Olive Fluid Gel, Oregano Oil
recipes.visual_description: Plated on a pristine white bone china rectangular platter, 8-10 perfectly circular medallions of pale golden-brown chicken and rich pink Italian sausage galantine are arranged with deliberate, generous negative space. Each galantine slice, approximately 1.5 cm thick, is precisely positioned. Adjacent to each medallion, a delicate, glossy teardrop of deep purple Kalamata olive fluid gel glistens. A few tiny, vibrant green drops of oregano oil are artfully dotted around the base, adding a fresh aromatic accent. Vertically inserted into each galantine is a fragile, irregular shard of golden-brown crispy chicken skin tuile, providing textural contrast. The setting features a cool grey veined marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in the corner. Dramatic, soft professional lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated minimalism.
instructions: Butterfly chicken breasts open. Pound gently to uniform 5mm thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Reserve chicken skin.
Sauté shallots in butter until translucent. Add sausage, break up, cook until browned. Deglaze with white wine, reduce. Stir in chopped oregano. Cool completely.

Lay plastic wrap on a clean surface. Arrange pounded chicken breasts, slightly overlapping, to form a rectangle. Spread cooled sausage mixture evenly over chicken. Roll tightly into a cylinder using plastic wrap. Twist ends to secure.

Poach galantine in simmering chicken stock or water for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from liquid. Chill completely in an ice bath, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Blend pitted olives with water until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Combine olive liquid and agar-agar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes.
Once set, blend the gel in a high-speed blender with extra virgin olive oil until smooth and fluid. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.
Blanch 50g oregano leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain and squeeze dry.
Blend blanched oregano with neutral oil and a pinch of salt until very smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth to remove solids. Store in a squeeze bottle.

Scrape any fat from reserved chicken skin. Season lightly with salt. Place skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Place a baking sheet on top to press it flat. Bake at 160°C for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and very crisp. Remove, cool, break into small, irregular shards.

Unwrap chilled galantine. Slice into 1.5cm thick medallions. Arrange 8-12 galantine medallions artistically on a platter. Place a small, precise dot or line of Kalamata Olive Fluid Gel next to each galantine piece. Drizzle a few tiny drops of Oregano Oil around the galantine or on the fluid gel. Garnish each piece with a delicate, irregular shard of Crispy Chicken Skin Tuile. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Eastern European Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Eastern European Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim. Golden-brown seared chicken thigh pieces are nestled amongst tender, irregular potato chunks and fluffy rice, all coated in a rich, reddish-orange tomato and paprika sauce. The chicken skin is crisp; the potato chunks are soft. Green flecks of fresh dill are scattered over the top. A halved hard-boiled egg rests on the side of the dish. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, slightly scratched. A simple, dark-colored cloth napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. A small, dark rye bread slice is placed nearby on the table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a slice of dark rye bread.
A dollop of sour cream or plain yogurt on the side.
Pickled vegetables (e.g., dill pickles) as an accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring liquid to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Add potato chunks. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, or until potatoes are fork-tender and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Stir in rinsed rice. Cover and continue to simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is cooked and most liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
While stew cooks, hard-boil eggs. Peel and halve.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with half a hard-boiled egg and fresh chopped dill.
notes: This is a hearty, warming dish perfect for family meals.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Manchego & Thyme Pasta Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, oblong pasta croquettes, approximately 6-7 cm long, are artfully arranged on a clean, rectangular white porcelain plate. Each croquette showcases a visibly crispy, textured Panko breadcrumb crust. Some croquettes are lightly stacked or laid diagonally, revealing glimpses of their creamy, cheesy interior with distinct flecks of finely diced orange carrot and vibrant green thyme. A small, white ceramic ramekin, placed beside the croquettes, holds a rich, rustic roasted tomato dip. The dip’s surface is slightly textured from the blended tomatoes, adorned with a subtle swirl of olive oil and a few fresh thyme leaves. The presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the dish, creating an inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a tapas spread
Pair with a dry sherry or light red wine

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.quantity: 45 mL (30 mL for dip, 15 mL for croquettes)

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme leaves
ingredients.quantity: 15 g (5 g for dip, 10 g for croquettes)

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.quantity: 80 g (30 g for mixture, 50 g for breading)

ingredients.name: Neutral oil for deep frying (e.g., sunflower, canola)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss tomato halves, 2 garlic cloves, 30 mL olive oil, 5 g thyme, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes until tomatoes are softened and slightly caramelized.
Transfer roasted mixture to a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth. Adjust seasoning. Set aside.
Bring chicken stock to a boil in a saucepan. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta well. Reserve 50 mL cooking liquid.
Heat 15 mL olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced carrot and onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add 1 minced garlic clove. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.

Add cooked pasta to the skillet with mirepoix. Stir in grated Manchego cheese, 10 g chopped thyme, and the reserved 50 mL chicken stock. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until cheese melts and mixture thickens. Remove from heat.
Let mixture cool slightly. Stir in 1 beaten egg and 30 g flour. Mix well to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Form mixture into oblong croquettes, about 6-7 cm long and 2-3 cm thick. (Yields approx. 16 croquettes).
Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with 50 g flour, one with 2 beaten eggs, one with Panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Roll in Panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat neutral oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C.
Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Arrange warm croquettes on a serving platter or individual plates. Serve immediately with the roasted tomato dip.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Carrot Arancini with Garlic Aioli
recipes.visual_description: Six golden-brown arancini are artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each arancino is perfectly spherical, showcasing a crisp, textured panko crust. A small, elegant white ramekin holds a dollop of creamy, off-white garlic aioli, positioned subtly to the side. The interior of one arancino is partially visible, revealing creamy risotto with flecks of shredded chicken and bright orange, finely diced carrot. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and a casually placed cotton napkin, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an antipasto or a street food snack.
Offer alongside a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Cook chicken breast: Boil or poach chicken breast until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Shred chicken finely. Set aside.
Prepare vegetables: Finely dice the onion and carrot. Mince 1 garlic clove.
Start risotto: In a large saucepan, sauté diced onion in a tablespoon of olive oil until translucent. Add minced garlic and diced carrot. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add rice: Stir in Arborio rice. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Cook until fully absorbed.
Add broth: Begin adding warm chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be absorbed before adding the next.

Finish risotto: Continue adding broth for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente. Stir in shredded chicken, Parmesan cheese, and half of the chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Spread risotto on a baking sheet. Cool completely in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.

Prepare aioli: Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. In a bowl, whisk egg yolk, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and minced garlic. Slowly drizzle in olive oil while continuously whisking until thick and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
Form arancini: Take cooled risotto. Form 40-50 g balls. Press a small cube of diced mozzarella into the center of each ball. Reshape into a tight sphere.
Bread arancini: Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with panko breadcrumbs. Roll each arancino first in flour, then in egg, then thoroughly coat in panko.
Fry arancini: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 175°C (350°F). Fry arancini in batches for 4-6 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Use a slotted spoon to remove. Drain on paper towels.
Serve: Arrange arancini on a serving platter. Serve immediately with garlic aioli and remaining fresh parsley for garnish.
notes: Ensure the risotto is completely cold before forming the arancini; this prevents them from falling apart during frying.
Do not overcrowd the fryer; fry in small batches to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: Four vibrant bell peppers, halved lengthwise, are baked until tender, holding their shape on a rustic ceramic baking dish. Each half is generously filled with a hearty, rustic mixture of cooked white rice and brown lentils, mixed with diced red onion, minced garlic, and diced mushrooms. The rich red of the crushed tomatoes and the fresh green of chopped basil, oregano, and parsley are visible within the filling. A golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella cheese and crisp breadcrumbs tops each pepper. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with an everyday ceramic plate. A casually folded cloth napkin and simple cutlery complete the homely, comforting scene. Natural, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the modest, satisfying portions, highlighting the dish's inviting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in any remaining sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in rinsed lentils and rice. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, until most liquid is absorbed and lentils/rice are partially cooked.
Stir in chopped basil, oregano, parsley, and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling generously into each bell pepper half.
Top each filled pepper with shredded mozzarella and breadcrumbs.
Add 100 ml water to the bottom of the baking dish to prevent sticking.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is golden and bubbly.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle with Beef and Chicken Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A generous swirl of golden Pappardelle pasta forms the base on a round, clean white porcelain plate. It is abundantly topped with a rich, deep red-brown beef and chicken ragu. Visible within the thick sauce are tender, slow-cooked beef chunks and smaller pieces of chicken. Brightly colored diced red and yellow bell peppers are interspersed, alongside wilted, roughly chopped dark green swiss chard leaves and finely chopped stems, adding vibrant color and soft texture. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese covers the ragu, with a scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley for garnish. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a silver fork and knife beside the plate and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the ragu.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3-4 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm pieces. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery finely for soffritto.
Mince garlic.
Remove Swiss chard stems. Finely chop stems. Roughly chop leaves.
Dice red and yellow bell peppers into 1.5 cm pieces.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While beef simmers, heat a separate pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken pieces until browned and cooked through, reaching 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Set aside.
After beef is tender, add chopped Swiss chard stems and diced bell peppers to the ragu. Cook 15 minutes.
Add seared chicken pieces and chopped Swiss chard leaves to the ragu. Cook 5-7 minutes until chard leaves wilt.
Season ragu with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Serve immediately with a generous amount of ragu. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Black Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a simple, everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table in a cozy family kitchen. Diced red, yellow, and green bell peppers, along with vibrant black beans and golden corn kernels, are casually mounded on the plate, creating a colorful and inviting display. Minced green chili and finely diced red onion are interspersed throughout, adding subtle texture and color. A generous sprinkling of fresh, chopped cilantro leaves garnishes the top, providing a fresh green accent. The components are naturally mixed and slightly overlapping, reflecting a comforting, unpretentious home-style preparation. The dressing lightly coats all ingredients, giving them a slight sheen. The plate is adequately filled but not overcrowded, allowing for some negative space.
