Repeat layers: remaining sliced potatoes, remaining rice mixture, remaining diced tomatoes.
Top generously with the remaining grated cheese.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender, rice is cooked through, and cheese is bubbly and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use a firm, waxy potato variety that holds its shape well when sliced.
The deep caramelization of the onions is key for rich flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Rosemary, Thyme, and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, a rustic scattering of roasted onion chunks (2 cm pieces), whole pitted black olives, and golden-brown smashed garlic cloves from the pan. A light sheen of savory pan sauce pools subtly at the base. Fresh green torn basil leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a vibrant contrast. Shavings of pale yellow Parmesan cheese are elegantly draped over the chicken and some of the vegetables. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. The plate sits on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Traditional Italian flatware rests beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes.
Flip chicken. Add chopped onion, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs to the skillet.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring onions and garlic, until fragrant.
Add pitted olives and chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove skillet from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh basil.
Serve chicken with pan sauce, onions, garlic, and olives. Garnish with shaved Parmesan and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef & Fermented Tomato Ragu with Hand-Rolled Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked beef and fermented tomato ragu is plated on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone. The wide, hand-rolled pappardelle pasta is naturally intertwined with generous chunks of tender, dark-brown braised beef and rich, deep red fermented tomato sauce. Diced carrots and celery are visibly softened within the sauce, adding natural orange and green flecks. The dish presents a rustic, organic texture with the substantial pasta strands and irregular beef pieces. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered artfully on top, providing a vibrant green contrast. The plating is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural textures and deep, savory colors of the dish to be the focal point. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple undyed linen napkin and a single, unpolished metal fork. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the authentic, wholesome quality of the meal.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3-4 cm chunks.
Dice onions, carrots, and celery into small cubes. Mince garlic.

For pasta: Combine flour, eggs, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix until dough forms. Knead on a floured surface for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef chunks. Sear until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Return browned beef to the pot. Add fermented tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary sprigs, and bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring ragu to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Cook for 2-3 hours, or until beef is very tender and easily pulls apart with a fork. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

While ragu simmers, roll pasta dough. Divide dough into portions. Pass each portion through a pasta machine, gradually decreasing thickness, or roll thinly by hand. Cut into wide pappardelle strips (approximately 2-3 cm wide). Dust with extra flour to prevent sticking.
Just before serving, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fresh pappardelle. Cook for 2-3 minutes until al dente.
Drain pasta. Transfer cooked pasta directly into the ragu. Toss gently to coat all the pasta strands with sauce.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh basil or parsley leaves.
notes: To ferment tomatoes: Roughly chop ripe tomatoes. Place in a clean jar. Add 2% salt by weight of tomatoes (e.g., 20g salt per 1kg tomatoes). Cover with non-chlorinated water if needed to submerge. Weigh down. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess, burping daily.
Save vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends) to make a flavorful stock for future recipes, contributing to a zero-waste kitchen.

recipes.recipe_name: Gnocchi di Patate con Crema di Piselli e Cipolle Caramellate
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Potato Gnocchi with Pea Cream and Caramelized Onions is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The soft, irregularly shaped potato gnocchi are coated in a vibrant, smooth pea cream, exhibiting a natural light green hue. Scattered throughout are tender, deep amber caramelized onion slices and small, golden-brown cubes of crispy pancetta. A generous dusting of freshly grated white Parmigiano Reggiano lightly covers the dish, with a few small, vibrant green fresh mint leaves placed artfully on top for color contrast. The dish is centrally composed with moderate negative space, showcasing the textures of the pillowy gnocchi and the creamy sauce. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a classic silver fork and knife beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish without harsh shadows, maintaining a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Boil potatoes in their skins until very tender, about 25-30 minutes. Drain well. Peel hot potatoes and pass through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly until no lumps remain. Spread riced potato on a clean surface to cool slightly for 10 minutes.
Form a well in the center of the riced potato. Add flour, egg, a pinch of nutmeg, and salt. Gently mix with hands until a soft, cohesive dough forms. Do not over-knead.

Divide dough into several portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, about 1.5 cm thick. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Gently roll each piece against the tines of a fork or a gnocchi board to create ridges. Place finished gnocchi on a lightly floured tray.

For the sauce, thinly slice the yellow onions. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Set aside.
If using pancetta, cook diced pancetta in the same skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pan.
Add minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add green peas and broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until peas are tender.

Transfer two-thirds of the pea mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Return blended pea cream and remaining whole peas to the skillet. Stir in caramelized onions and cooked pancetta (if using). Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until they float to the surface. Remove gnocchi with a slotted spoon.
Add cooked gnocchi directly to the sauce. Add butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Gently toss to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes to allow gnocchi to absorb sauce.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish generously with fresh Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh mint or basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang Chicken with Mango & Coconut
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Panang Chicken with Mango & Coconut is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The rich, creamy, reddish-orange curry sauce coats tender 3cm chicken chunks and soft diced mango pieces. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered generously over the curry, complemented by a few delicate, thinly sliced red chili rings and finely grated lime zest for a pop of color and aroma. The jasmine rice is served in a separate, small white porcelain bowl beside the main curry bowl. The overall plating is professional, balanced, and organized, allowing moderate negative space around the elements. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, suggestive of a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the inviting textures and colors. A traditional Thai-style serving spoon is placed beside the curry bowl, maintaining cultural authenticity within a contemporary dining context. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the culinary presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies) on the side for additional seasoning.
instructions: Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat.
Add Panang curry paste. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Cook, stirring, until chicken is browned on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk. Add kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
Stir in diced mango. Cook for 2 minutes.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in fresh lime juice and yogurt until well combined.
Serve Panang chicken curry over steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh basil leaves, thinly sliced red chili, and a sprinkle of lime zest.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the five fundamental flavors: sweet, sour, salty, spicy, and umami.
Stir-frying curry paste to release aromatics before adding liquid.

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Matar Paneer with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Indian Aloo Matar Paneer curry is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple, light wooden table. The curry features tender 2cm cubed potatoes, bright green peas, and creamy 2cm cubed paneer, bathed in a rich, golden-orange gravy. The sauce is medium-thick with visible spice flecks. Scattered throughout and atop are deep golden-brown, thinly sliced caramelized onions. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped coriander leaves provides a vibrant green garnish. The bowl rests on a clean white cotton napkin. Adjacent, fluffy Basmati rice is served on a flat white dinner plate. A small, polished stainless steel katori holds cool white raita. Soft, natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting. The entire plate and accompaniments are visible, showcasing a single, refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with Basmati rice.
Accompany with freshly made naan bread or roti.
Offer a side of raita (yogurt dip) or mango pickle.
instructions: Heat 30ml ghee/oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring frequently, until onions are deep golden brown and caramelized. This takes 15-20 minutes. Remove onions from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml ghee/oil to the same pot. Add cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pureed tomatoes. Cook, stirring, until oil separates from the mixture (about 5-7 minutes).
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chilli powder. Stir well. Cook for 2 minutes, adding a splash of water if spices stick.
Add cubed potatoes. Stir to coat with spices. Add 250ml water and salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until potatoes are almost tender.
Add green peas and paneer cubes to the pot. Stir gently. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, until peas are tender and paneer is heated through.
Stir in garam masala. Add most of the caramelized onions. Reserve some for garnish.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander and remaining caramelized onions. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust green chillies and red chilli powder to desired spice level.
Paneer can be lightly fried before adding to prevent breaking and enhance texture.
Consistency of gravy can be adjusted by adding more water or simmering longer.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper Pasta with Mint & Creamy Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of pasta coated in a vibrant, creamy roasted bell pepper sauce. The pasta, such as rigatoni, is evenly coated in the warm, orange-hued sauce. Bright green peas are interspersed throughout, providing pops of contrasting color and texture. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley adds a verdant touch on top. Grated Pecorino Romano cheese rests lightly over the pasta, adding a subtle visual texture. The sauce has a smooth, rich consistency, clinging well to the pasta. The overall presentation is inviting and rustic yet refined, with moderate negative space on the plate. The table setting features a simple wooden surface, a cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard flatware, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Fresh Parsley
ingredients.quantity: A small bunch, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve and deseed bell peppers. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin is blistered and charred. Transfer to a bowl, cover with cling film for 10 minutes. Peel off skin.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add peeled roasted bell peppers, dried mint, smoked paprika, and pul biber to the pan. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer bell pepper mixture to a blender. Add ricotta, sour cream, and 100ml reserved pasta water. Blend until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper.
Return the sauce to the pan. Add frozen green peas. Simmer gently for 3-4 minutes until peas are tender and heated through.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add grated Pecorino Romano. Toss to coat evenly. Add more reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, if sauce is too thick.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and extra grated Pecorino.
notes: This dish blends Italian pasta tradition with Turkish-inspired spices and creamy elements, creating a unique and flavorful main course. The roasting of the bell peppers deepens their flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beer-Braised Chicken with Herbed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of spicy beer-braised chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of fluffy, white long-grain rice, subtly mixed with finely chopped fresh parsley, forms the base. A golden-brown, whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, tender from braising, rests centrally. The chicken skin is visibly crisp. A rich, reddish-brown braising sauce, glossy and viscous, pools around the chicken and lightly coats the rice. The composition is neat, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors. A fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The dish appears refined yet approachable, showcasing quality ingredients and professional plating.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes.
Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook for 3-5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer and hot sauce. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 30 minutes. Check internal temperature. Cook until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, prepare the rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rinsed rice and chicken broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Remove chicken from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
To serve, spoon a portion of herbed rice onto a white porcelain plate. Place one braised chicken thigh on top of the rice.
Spoon some braising liquid over the chicken and rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Garlic Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown confit chicken thigh rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The chicken skin is visibly crisp, showcasing its rich texture. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, vibrant mound of red-orange fermented tomato-garlic relish provides a pop of color and natural texture. A few delicate, fresh green thyme sprigs are thoughtfully placed near the chicken, providing a touch of organic green. The plating is minimalistic, emphasizing white space and the inherent beauty of each ingredient. The setting is an eco-conscious light bamboo surface with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, and the background is clean and unobtrusive, featuring subtle hints of natural elements or plants, enhancing the sustainable aesthetic. No artificial garnishes or elaborate arrangements are present; the focus is on pure, ingredient-focused presentation.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs with bone and skin

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with sea salt.
Place chicken in a deep, oven-safe pot. Add 5 thyme sprigs and 1 head of garlic (unpeeled, halved).
Pour oil over chicken until fully submerged. Cook in oven at 140°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from oil. Strain and reserve oil for future use. Discard used garlic and thyme.
For relish: Dice tomatoes finely. Mince 4 garlic cloves. Combine tomatoes, minced garlic, cayenne pepper, and 1 tablespoon sea salt in a clean jar.
Stir relish ingredients. Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or until desired tanginess. Stir daily. Refrigerate after fermentation.
To serve: Crisp chicken skin in a hot pan if desired. Warm chicken gently.
Plate one chicken thigh. Spoon a small portion of fermented tomato-garlic relish beside chicken. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Rendered chicken fat from the confit process can be strained and stored in the refrigerator for future cooking. It adds rich flavor to roasted vegetables or potatoes.
Leftover chicken bones can be used to make nutritious chicken stock. Tomato scraps (cores, skins) can be added to vegetable stock.
The fermented relish can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks, deepening in flavor over time.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sumac Halloumi with Bulgur and Tahini
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Sumac Halloumi with Bulgur and Tahini is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. The plate features a neat mound of fluffy, golden-brown bulgur pilaf at its base. Three to four golden-crusted, pan-seared halloumi slabs are arranged artfully on top of the bulgur, showcasing their crispy exterior. Beside the halloumi and bulgur, a vibrant pile of small-cubed green cucumber and chopped fresh parsley and mint provides a fresh contrast. A creamy, off-white lemon-tahini sauce is drizzled elegantly over the halloumi and bulgur, creating soft, flowing lines. A light dusting of reddish-purple sumac powder adorns the halloumi and a few fresh mint leaves are placed strategically for garnish. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A simple silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. The setting is a modern bistro with natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Rinse bulgur under cold water. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add bulgur. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Add 400 ml vegetable broth or water to bulgur. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and bulgur is tender. Fluff with a fork. Season with salt and pepper.
While bulgur cooks, prepare the cucumber salad. Dice cucumbers into small cubes (approximately 0.5 cm). Finely chop fresh parsley and mint.

In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber, chopped parsley, and chopped mint. Add 1 teaspoon sumac, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and juice from half a lemon. Toss gently to combine. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Prepare the tahini sauce. In a small bowl, whisk tahini with juice from the remaining half lemon. Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to tahini mixture. Gradually whisk in 80-100 ml cold water until the sauce reaches a smooth, pourable consistency. Season with salt.
Slice halloumi cheese into 1.5 cm thick rectangular slabs or medallions. Pat dry with paper towels.
Sprinkle halloumi slices evenly with 1 teaspoon sumac and a pinch of black pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add halloumi slices to the hot skillet in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
To plate, spoon a generous portion of bulgur pilaf onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Arrange 3-4 pieces of pan-seared halloumi on top of or beside the bulgur.

Place a spoonful of the cucumber-herb salad alongside the halloumi and bulgur. Drizzle the tahini sauce generously over the halloumi and bulgur. Garnish with an extra sprinkle of sumac and a few fresh mint leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic-Herb Potatoes and Seasonal Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef medallions, thick-cut and perfectly seared to a rich brown crust with a rosy interior, anchors a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Alongside, a generous serving of golden-brown roasted potato wedges, tender inside, are arranged neatly. A vibrant medley of crisp-tender green beans, bright yellow corn kernels, and plump green peas is thoughtfully placed, showcasing their natural colors. A glossy, rich Worcestershire-infused beef jus is spooned artfully over the beef. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley for a pop of color and freshness. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, presented on a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin and modern flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors in a casual bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut into wedges. In a bowl, toss potato wedges with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper, chopped rosemary, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden-brown. Turn halfway.
Bring a pot of salted water to boil. Blanch green beans for 2-3 minutes. Drain and immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Finely dice red onion. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion and sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add corn kernels and green peas to the pan. Sauté for 3 minutes. Add blanched green beans. Season vegetables with salt and pepper. Cook for 2 more minutes. Keep warm.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat a separate heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Add a drizzle of olive oil.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary.
Remove beef from pan. Place on a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Return the pan to medium heat. Deglaze with beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Bring to a simmer. Stir in unsalted butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens. Taste and adjust seasoning.

To plate, arrange roasted potato wedges and sautéed seasonal vegetables on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Place one pan-seared beef medallion beside them. Spoon the rich pan sauce over the beef. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thai Basil Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A neat mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies one side. Adjacent, a generous portion of spicy Thai basil chicken (Pad Krapow Gai) is artfully placed, featuring finely diced chicken pieces wok-fried to a light golden-brown, intermingled with vibrant green holy basil leaves, thinly sliced red bird's eye chilies, and minced garlic. The chicken has a glossy, rich brown sauce clinging to it, indicating proper caramelization and seasoning. Scattered around the chicken are bright red halved cherry tomatoes, adding a fresh, juicy contrast. A few fresh basil leaves garnish the top. The overall presentation is clean and balanced, showcasing the vibrant colors and varied textures. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate on a light wooden table surface, under natural, even lighting, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies and a squeeze of lime).

ingredients.name: Thai Bird's Eye Chilies, thinly sliced

instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package instructions. Keep warm.
Combine soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and water/stock in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves. This is the stir-fry sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince to the wok. Break up the chicken with a spatula. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the stir-fry sauce over the chicken. Stir well to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Add holy basil leaves to the wok. Stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds until basil wilts. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve the spicy basil chicken directly alongside a portion of warm jasmine rice. Garnish with halved cherry tomatoes and a few fresh basil leaves.
notes: Holy basil (krapow) is traditional for this dish. If unavailable, Thai basil or sweet basil can be used as a substitute, though the flavor will be slightly different.
Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Strawberry Peanut Butter Almond Crumble
recipes.visual_description: The Strawberry Peanut Butter Almond Crumble is presented warm in a rustic, deep ceramic baking dish (approx. 20x20 cm), its golden-brown, textured topping still gently bubbling at the edges. The surface shows a mix of crisp oats, finely integrated flour, and visible, roughly chopped almond pieces and irregular clusters of baked peanut butter. Peeking from beneath are soft, glossy, bright red strawberries. A single, modest portion is scooped into a simple, cream-colored ceramic bowl placed beside the main dish. A generous, irregular dollop of thick, white plain yogurt melts slightly onto the warm crumble in the bowl. The setting is a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, with natural, soft light coming from a nearby window or overhead kitchen fixture. A folded, plain linen napkin is casually placed. The overall scene is inviting and unpretentious, capturing the essence of a comforting homemade dessert ready to be shared.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Combine hulled and halved or quartered strawberries with 50g granulated sugar in a large bowl. Mix gently to coat.
Pour sweetened strawberries into a 20x20 cm (or similar size) baking dish.
In a separate large bowl, combine flour, rolled oats, brown sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Add cold cubed butter to the dry ingredients. Use fingertips to rub butter into the mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Add peanut butter and roughly chopped almonds to the crumble mixture. Mix until well combined and crumbly.
Evenly sprinkle the crumble topping over the strawberries in the baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes. The crumble should be golden brown. The strawberries should be bubbling at the edges.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm with a generous spoonful of plain yogurt on top.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna, Masa Crisp, Ancho-Garlic Fluid Gel, Avocado Puree
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, large white bone china plate with abundant negative space, intended as an individual elegant portion of a shared snack. Three to four perfectly seared tuna cubes, showing a deep pink rare center and a thin seared crust, are artfully arranged. Adjacent to the tuna are two to three irregularly shaped, golden-brown masa crisps, showcasing their delicate texture. Vibrant green avocado puree is applied in small, elegant dots or a delicate, organic swoosh. Dark, glossy drops of ancho-garlic fluid gel are precisely placed to create visual contrast. A few delicate sprigs of micro cilantro are used as a final, minimalist garnish. The composition is natural and flowing, avoiding rigid geometric shapes. The setting features a premium white Carrara marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows, creating an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare Ancho-Garlic Fluid Gel: Rehydrate ancho chiles in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain. Roast garlic cloves until tender. Blend rehydrated chiles, roasted garlic, 150 ml water, and a pinch of salt until very smooth. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Whisk in xanthan gum until a smooth fluid gel forms. Set aside.
Prepare Avocado Puree: Scoop avocado flesh into a blender. Add lime juice and a pinch of salt. Blend until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smooth consistency. Set aside.

Prepare Masa Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut corn tortillas into irregular shards or small rectangles. Lightly brush with olive oil and sprinkle with salt. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and very crisp. Cool completely.

Sear Tuna: Pat tuna loin dry. Season generously with sea salt. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over high heat until smoking. Sear tuna loin for 45-60 seconds per side for rare center. Remove from heat. Rest tuna for 5 minutes. Cut tuna into 1.5 cm thick cubes or small rectangular blocks.

Assemble Dish: On a large white bone china plate, arrange 3-4 pieces of seared tuna. Place 2-3 masa crisps around the tuna. Create small dots or a delicate swoosh of avocado puree. Add 3-4 precise drops of ancho-garlic fluid gel. Garnish sparingly with micro cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Lean Beef and Mushroom Ragu with Whole Wheat Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lean Beef and Mushroom Ragu with Whole Wheat Rigatoni is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. The robust, rich red-brown ragu generously coats the al dente rigatoni, with visible tender chunks of lean beef and earthy slices of browned mushrooms interspersed throughout. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The pasta is arranged naturally, allowing the sauce to pool slightly at the bottom of the bowl. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl, and a silver fork rests invitingly. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual dining atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, ensuring the dish remains the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light green salad dressed simply with olive oil and lemon.
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese on the side for individual preference.
Accompany with a glass of light-bodied red wine, such as a Chianti.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add lean beef mince. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and no pink remains. Drain any excess fat. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-8 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return browned beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, dried oregano, and bay leaf. Stir well.
Bring the ragu to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 30 minutes, or up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Remove bay leaf before serving.
While ragu simmers, cook whole wheat rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml of pasta water before draining.
Add drained pasta to the ragu. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in half of the fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: This recipe uses lean beef mince and whole wheat pasta to create a lower calorie and higher protein profile.
The rich flavor comes from slow-simmered vegetables and herbs, reducing reliance on heavy fats.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Medallions with Roasted Red Pepper Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast medallions is centrally plated on a round white porcelain dish. The chicken, cooked to a tender finish, exhibits a delicate crust. Beneath and around the chicken, a vibrant, smooth roasted red pepper coulis creates a striking red base, artfully swirled or spooned. A drizzle of bright green basil oil provides a contrasting color and aromatic accent. Small fresh basil leaves are scattered thoughtfully as a garnish. The dish presents a balanced composition with moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and even natural light.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Slice each breast horizontally into 2-3 medallions, about 1.5 cm thick. Season medallions with salt and black pepper.

Roast peppers: Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds and stems. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 20-25 minutes until skins are blistered and slightly charred. Transfer roasted peppers to a bowl, cover tightly with plastic wrap, and let cool for 10 minutes. Peel off the skins and discard.

Make coulis: Heat 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 3-5 minutes. Add the peeled roasted peppers and chicken stock. Simmer for 5 minutes. Transfer mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep coulis warm.

Make basil oil: Combine fresh basil leaves with 3 tablespoons (45 ml) olive oil in a small blender or food processor. Blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a clearer oil, if desired.

Sear chicken: Heat remaining 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken medallions to the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

Plate: Spoon roasted red pepper coulis onto the center of individual white porcelain plates. Arrange pan-seared chicken medallions elegantly over the coulis. Drizzle with basil oil. Garnish with a few small fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Spiced Apple-Cherry Chutney and Savory Oat Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut medallion of pan-seared pork tenderloin rests off-center on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Beside it, a neat quenelle of deep red and amber apple-cherry chutney. Golden-brown savory oat crumble sprinkles generously over the pork and around the plate, providing textural contrast. The pork shows a rich golden crust and tender pink interior. The chutney offers vibrant reds and soft yellows from finely diced apples. The oat crumble is toasted golden-brown with green herb hints. A small fresh thyme sprig garnishes the plate. The plate rests on a warm wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and simple flatware complete the setting. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. For the Savory Oat Crumble: Melt 50g butter in a small pan. Add oats, half of the minced garlic, and 1 teaspoon of chopped fresh rosemary. Cook until fragrant. Spread mixture on a baking sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.

For the Spiced Apple-Cherry Chutney: Melt 20g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallot and remaining minced garlic. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add diced apples, dried cherries, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, and chicken stock. Add 1 sprig of fresh thyme. Bring to a simmer. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are tender and liquid reduces to a chutney consistency. Remove thyme sprig. Season with salt and pepper.

For the Pork Tenderloin: Pat pork dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F).
Remove pork from oven. Rest 5 minutes on a cutting board. Slice pork into thick medallions (approximately 3-4 cm thick).

Assemble: Place one or two pork medallions on each plate. Spoon a quenelle of warm apple-cherry chutney next to the pork. Sprinkle a generous amount of savory oat crumble over the pork and around the plate. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Bell Pepper Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and robust single portion of Spicy Chicken and Bell Pepper Rice is presented centrally on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among fluffy, reddish-orange rice. The rice is studded with brightly colored diced red and yellow bell peppers and small pieces of onion and chili. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The texture is a mix of tender chicken, soft rice, and slightly firm-tender vegetables. The dish is served on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a lime wedge on the plate, a cotton napkin beside it, and a clean fork and knife set. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of fresh salsa or pico de gallo.
Provide extra lime wedges for squeezing.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and bell peppers (2cm dice) to the same skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, finely diced jalapeño, cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in rice until well coated.
Pour in hot chicken broth and canned diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet, nestling it into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Mincemeat Loaf with Roasted Potato Wedges
recipes.visual_description: A thick, substantial slice of golden-brown mincemeat loaf rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The loaf exhibits a glossy, caramelized ketchup glaze topped with melted, bubbly sharp cheddar, showing a slight crispness on its edges. Roasted potato wedges, golden and slightly charred with a visible crispy exterior, are artfully arranged around the meatloaf, creating a balanced composition. A small, elegant ramekin or a delicate spoon holds a vibrant red tomato-onion relish, its chunky texture visible. A creamy, pale orange swirl of mayonnaise-ketchup sauce is drizzled artistically beside the loaf. Fresh, finely chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a soft cotton napkin, and standard flatware, all illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating an inviting modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Accompany with a side of steamed green beans or buttered corn.
Pair with cornbread.

ingredients.name: Large potatoes (e.g., Russet or Maris Piper)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crispy.
For the meatloaf, finely dice half of the onion. Mince garlic. Soak bread in milk for 5 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid.
In a large bowl, combine mincemeat, diced onion, minced garlic, soaked bread, egg, 50g grated cheddar, 15ml ketchup, 2g oregano, salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into an oblong loaf shape on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake meatloaf for 40 minutes. Meanwhile, dice the remaining half onion and both tomatoes.

Prepare the tomato-onion relish: Heat 15ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add diced tomatoes, 50ml ketchup, 3g oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 10-15 minutes until thickened.
After 40 minutes, remove meatloaf from oven. Spread remaining 15ml ketchup evenly over the top. Sprinkle remaining 50g grated cheddar over the ketchup.
Return meatloaf to oven and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and internal temperature reaches 70°C.
Prepare the special sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise and 15ml ketchup.

Let meatloaf rest for 5 minutes before slicing into thick portions. Serve each portion with roasted potato wedges, a spoonful of tomato-onion relish, and a drizzle of the special sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheek with Saffron Risotto, Roasted Bell Pepper Gel, and Confit Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, artfully arranged portion presented on a pristine, oversized white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern. The plate rests on a cool white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and abundant negative space. The focal point is a single, richly browned, irregularly shaped piece of braised beef cheek, its surface glossy with reduced jus. Adjacent, a creamy, vibrant golden Saffron Risotto forms an organic, flowing crescent, its individual grains distinct yet tender. Beside the beef, a precise placement of two or three translucent, glistening confit pearl onions adds a sweet, delicate counterpoint. A few artfully placed, jewel-toned cubes of bright red roasted bell pepper gel provide a vibrant color contrast and textural pop. The rich, dark beef jus is meticulously spooned, creating a glossy, abstract pool that anchors the beef. The composition is minimalist yet impactful, showcasing sophisticated simplicity, precise knife work on the gel, and the luxurious textures of each component. No elements are fanned out; each component is presented in its natural, refined form.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads, steeped in 30ml hot water

instructions: Pat beef cheeks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return beef cheeks to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C. Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef cheeks from braising liquid. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids.
Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat until it forms a glossy, thick jus. Season to taste. Keep warm.
For the Saffron Risotto: Heat a separate saucepan over medium heat. Add a small amount of olive oil. Sauté minced shallot until translucent.
Add Arborio rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze with white wine. Cook until absorbed.
Begin adding hot vegetable stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each ladle to be absorbed before adding the next.
After 15 minutes, add steeped saffron with its liquid. Continue adding stock and stirring.
Cook until rice is al dente, creamy but with a slight bite, about 18-20 minutes total. Remove from heat.
Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan until melted and risotto is creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the Roasted Bell Pepper Gel: Roast red bell pepper whole over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred and blistered. Place in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let steam for 10 minutes.
Peel, deseed, and coarsely chop the roasted bell pepper. Blend with a splash of water until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Heat bell pepper puree in a small saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil and simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Pour onto a shallow plate or tray. Chill until set.
Once set, cut the gel into small cubes or re-blend until smooth for a gel consistency. Keep chilled.
For the Confit Pearl Onions: Peel pearl onions. Place in a small saucepan. Cover with extra virgin olive oil. Add a thyme sprig.
Gently heat over very low heat. Confit for 25-30 minutes, or until onions are tender and translucent. Do not brown. Drain and keep warm.
To Plate: Place a generous, organic smear or crescent of Saffron Risotto slightly off-center on each plate. Place one piece of braised beef cheek gently beside the risotto.
Artistically spoon a small amount of the Bell Pepper Gel onto the plate, near the beef or risotto. Arrange 2-3 confit pearl onions elegantly around the beef.
Spoon a generous drizzle of the reduced beef jus over and around the beef cheek. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chai-Spiced Oat & Apple Savory Squares
recipes.visual_description: A collection of 12 Chai-Spiced Oat & Apple Savory Squares are casually arranged on a rustic, well-used wooden cutting board. The small, golden-brown squares are approximately 4cm x 4cm, showcasing a slightly irregular, homely appearance. Each square reveals visible specks of grated apple and vibrant purple blueberries, interspersed with green flecks of fresh thyme and melted cheddar. The texture appears hearty and comforting, with a tender crumb. The squares are placed close together, some gently overlapping, creating an inviting, natural cluster. A simple, off-white linen napkin is loosely draped to one side. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, emphasizing the natural colors and comforting texture of the canapes, suitable for a family kitchen table setting.

ingredients.name: Ground chai spices (cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, clove, black pepper)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm x 20cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine oats, flour, baking powder, chai spices, salt, and pepper. Whisk well.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg, milk, and melted butter.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in grated apple, fresh blueberries, and chopped thyme. Add shredded cheddar cheese. Mix gently.
Pour batter into the prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cool in the dish for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Once cooled, cut the baked square into 12 small squares for canapes.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni al Pomodoro Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni al Pomodoro Confit is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a vibrant, rustic red sauce, showcasing the tender, burst slow-roasted cherry tomatoes and golden, soft confit garlic cloves. Freshly torn bright green basil leaves are scattered throughout, providing a striking color contrast and aromatic garnish. A light sheen from the olive oil gives the dish an appealing luster. The pasta is arranged in a natural, slightly mounded pile with moderate negative space around it. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is arranged neatly. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping the flavorful sauce.
Pair with a light green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Place cherry tomatoes in a baking dish. Add 50 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place whole garlic cloves in a small oven-safe dish. Cover with 100 ml olive oil. Ensure cloves are submerged.
Roast tomatoes and garlic confit in the preheated oven for 60-75 minutes. Tomatoes should be soft and slightly shriveled. Garlic should be golden and tender.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add rigatoni pasta to boiling water. Cook according to package instructions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, gently crush roasted tomatoes in their juices with a fork. Add confit garlic cloves and a few tablespoons of their oil to the tomato sauce. Stir gently.
Reserve 125 ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the tomato and garlic sauce.
Add torn fresh basil leaves. Toss well, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a smooth, glossy sauce that coats the pasta.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sirloin with Garlic Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared sirloin steak, cut into thick, juicy medallions, rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. The steak, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, displays a rich brown crust. Piled generously beside and slightly over the beef are golden-brown sautéed cremini mushrooms, some whole, some sliced, glistening with a light, savory pan sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a natural pop of color. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy home kitchen. Standard silver flatware is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere with minimal background clutter.
instructions: Pat sirloin steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.
Heat a large skillet or cast iron pan over high heat until very hot. Add 5ml olive oil.
Sear steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness.
Remove steaks from pan. Let rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 10ml olive oil to the pan. Add sliced mushrooms.
Sauté mushrooms for 5-7 minutes until browned and softened.
Add minced garlic to the pan with mushrooms. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes until broth slightly reduces.
Slice the rested sirloin into thick chunks or medallions.
Serve sliced sirloin immediately, topped with the garlic mushrooms and pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Sausage and Potato Roast
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Sheet Pan Sausage and Potato Roast sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features golden-brown roasted potato chunks, tender-crisp large red bell pepper pieces, and caramelized red onion wedges. Hearty, browned sausage chunks are interspersed throughout the vegetables. All components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, unpretentious mound. The textures are varied: crisp potato exteriors, soft interiors, tender vegetables, and savory sausage. A scattering of roughly chopped fresh green parsley adds a pop of natural color. The plate is centered on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin is placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting nature of the meal. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen atmosphere, perhaps a water glass or salt shaker slightly out of focus. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, typical of a family dinner.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut sausages into 3 cm thick chunks.
Cut potatoes into rough 2-3 cm chunks.
Cut bell peppers into large 3-4 cm chunks.
Cut red onion into thick wedges.
In a large bowl, combine sausage, potatoes, bell peppers, and onion.
Drizzle with olive oil. Toss to coat evenly.
Add dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Toss again.
Spread ingredients in a single layer on a large sheet pan.
Roast for 30-35 minutes. Turn ingredients halfway through cooking.
Ensure potatoes are tender and browned. Sausage should be cooked through.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sirloin with Mushrooms and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: Two thick-cut, pan-seared sirloin medallions, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, showcasing a deep golden-brown crust. They are positioned slightly offset on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Beside the beef, a generous portion of rustic quartered cremini mushrooms, deeply caramelized, is neatly arranged. Vibrant green, crisp-tender asparagus spears, lightly steamed, are laid alongside the mushrooms. A glossy, dark beef jus, made with shallots and red wine, is gently pooled beneath and around the beef. The dish is garnished with a small sprig of fresh rosemary and thyme. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Cook to internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare.
Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 5-10 minutes.
Add remaining 5ml olive oil to the same pan. Add quartered cremini mushrooms. Sauté over medium-high heat until deeply caramelized and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms from pan.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Steam or blanch asparagus until crisp-tender, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt.
For the sauce: Add finely diced shallot to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half, about 1 minute.

Pour in beef broth. Add 1 sprig thyme and 1 sprig rosemary. Bring to a simmer. Reduce sauce by one-third, about 3-5 minutes, until slightly thickened. Strain sauce if desired. Discard herbs. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Plate rested beef medallions alongside sautéed mushrooms and steamed asparagus. Spoon beef jus over and around the beef. Garnish with a fresh sprig of rosemary or thyme. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Stroganoff with Buttered Egg Noodles and Wild Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Beef Stroganoff is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Tender 2.5 cm beef chunks, seared to a rich brown, are nestled within a creamy, savory mushroom sauce. Sliced cremini mushrooms, sautéed until tender, blend seamlessly with the sauce. Golden, buttered medium egg noodles form a comforting base beneath the saucy beef and mushrooms. Adjacent to the bowl, on the pristine white plate, a small, neat mound of multi-colored wild rice pilaf provides a textural contrast. The dish is generously garnished with vibrant, freshly chopped parsley, adding a pop of bright green. The rich browns and creams of the stroganoff are complemented by the varied hues of the rice and the fresh herb. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. Served on a simple wooden table with standard cutlery and a folded cotton napkin.
instructions: Cut beef sirloin into 2.5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 20g butter to the pan. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the pan. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Mince garlic and add to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Return seared beef to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

While stroganoff simmers, cook wild rice blend according to package directions. Typically, combine rice with 2.5 parts water, bring to boil, then simmer covered until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add egg noodles and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir remaining 30g butter into the drained egg noodles.
Remove stroganoff from heat. Stir in sour cream until fully incorporated. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Chop fresh parsley for garnish.
Serve beef stroganoff over buttered egg noodles. Serve a portion of wild rice pilaf alongside. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Steak Sandwich with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish features an open-faced seared beef steak sandwich presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, rustic slice of golden-toasted sourdough bread forms the base. It is generously spread with a creamy, pale off-white blue cheese aioli. A mound of deeply caramelized, glossy amber onions is piled atop the aioli. On the onions, thick, juicy chunks of medium-rare beef steak are arranged, showcasing a rich brown crust and a vibrant pink interior. The steak pieces are irregular, substantial cuts, not fanned slices. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, reflecting a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting. The overall presentation is professional, approachable, and balanced, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crispy seasoned potato wedges or a simple green salad.
Offer extra blue cheese aioli or a steak sauce on the side.
instructions: Slice onions thinly. Heat 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Add a splash of beef broth if needed to deglaze. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, crumbled blue cheese, minced garlic, and Dijon mustard. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat steak dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.

Heat remaining 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until smoking. Add steak. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Transfer steak to a cutting board. Tent with foil. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Lightly toast bread slices in the same pan or a toaster until golden.

Spread a generous layer of blue cheese aioli on each toasted bread slice. Top with a portion of caramelized onions. Slice steak into thick chunks against the grain. Place steak chunks on top of onions. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Resting the steak is essential for tenderness and juiciness.
Adjust blue cheese quantity in aioli to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Creamy Parmesan Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. The dish features two thick, dark brown, fork-tender beef short rib chunks, showcasing their rich, slow-cooked texture. They rest atop a generous, free-flowing pool of creamy, pale yellow Parmesan polenta, which maintains a fluid consistency. A vibrant green gremolata, finely chopped, is sprinkled over the beef, providing a fresh, zesty contrast. The braising liquid, reduced to a glossy, deep brown sauce, is drizzled over the beef and polenta, adding shine and depth. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Standard European flatware is placed neatly beside the plate on a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a subtly blurred bistro-style background creating an approachable restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust red wine, such as a Chianti or Barolo.
Offer crusty bread on the side for soaking up the rich sauce.
Traditionally enjoyed as a hearty main course, often in cooler months.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return short ribs to the pot. Add beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the Dutch oven tightly.
Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove short ribs from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and reduce until slightly thickened.
While sauce reduces, prepare polenta. Bring water or milk to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Cook polenta, stirring frequently, for 3-5 minutes until creamy and smooth.
Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and fully incorporated. Season with salt to taste.
For the gremolata, combine finely chopped parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic in a small bowl.
Serve braised short ribs over creamy Parmesan polenta. Spoon reduced braising liquid over the ribs. Garnish generously with gremolata.
notes: For best flavor, braise the short ribs a day in advance. The flavors deepen overnight, and fat is easier to skim when cold.
Adjust the consistency of the polenta by adding more hot liquid if it becomes too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Beef with Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Beef with Saffron Rice is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rich, dark brown braised beef chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled on one side, generously coated in a glossy, thick red wine and tomato sauce. The sauce contains tender, small-diced red bell pepper and onion pieces. Adjacent to the beef, a mound of vibrant yellow saffron rice is neatly mounded. The rice grains are separate and fluffy, showing the characteristic golden hue from saffron. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a bright green contrast over both the beef and rice. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a dark cotton napkin folded casually beside it. The background suggests a modern bistro, softly blurred to keep focus on the dish. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its textures and rich colors. Traditional simple flatware is placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat beef dry. Dice beef into 4-5 cm chunks. Season beef with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into small pieces. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to pot. Add diced onion and red bell pepper. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic and smoked paprika to pot. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pot. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef to pot. Add diced tomatoes and beef broth.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C.
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
While beef braises, prepare saffron rice. Warm 100 ml water or broth. Add saffron threads to warm liquid. Let steep 10 minutes.
Heat a separate medium pot over medium heat. Add Arborio rice. Stir 1 minute.
Add saffron liquid and 650 ml hot water or broth to rice. Season with salt.
Bring to a simmer. Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook 18-20 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove rice from heat. Let rest 5 minutes, covered. Fluff with a fork.
Taste braised beef stew. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve braised beef and its rich sauce alongside a portion of saffron rice. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef and Red Wine Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion of rich, creamy Braised Beef and Red Wine Risotto. The risotto is fluid and free-flowing, reflecting its al dente consistency. Deep crimson hues from the red wine braising liquid infuse the Arborio rice. Irregularly shaped, tender chunks of braised beef are interspersed with vibrant, roasted bell pepper pieces in shades of red and yellow, their edges slightly caramelized. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The surface glistens with melted Parmesan and butter, indicating its luxurious texture. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface beside a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up any remaining sauce.
Pair with a glass of the red wine used in the recipe.

ingredients.name: Boneless beef short rib or chuck roast

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss bell pepper pieces with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.

Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 20g butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 20g butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes until wine reduces by half.

Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in enough hot beef broth to just cover the beef (about 500ml). Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender. Remove beef from liquid and set aside. Strain braising liquid and reserve.
In a separate large saucepan, melt 20g butter over medium heat. Add Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in a ladleful of the reserved hot beef braising liquid. Stir until absorbed.
Add hot beef broth one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.

Gently stir the cooked beef chunks and roasted bell peppers into the risotto. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20g butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Ladle immediately into warm bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mushroom and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Hearty Mushroom and Potato Soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The soup features substantial chunks of tender, light brown sliced cremini mushrooms and soft, off-white diced potatoes, suspended in a rich, clear, dark amber broth. Some mushroom pieces are beautifully browned from searing, adding depth. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the surface. The arrangement is natural and unforced, filling the bowl without overcrowding. A simple, silver-colored spoon rests beside the bowl. The background is a blurred, warm-toned homely family kitchen, suggesting a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere with soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and thyme sprigs to the pot.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs.
Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: German Style Bratwurst and Cheese Tart
recipes.visual_description: The German Style Bratwurst and Cheese Tart sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, golden-brown shortcrust pastry shell, lightly fluted at the edges, encases the rich filling. The top of the tart is a deep golden-yellow, indicating a perfectly set egg custard. Visible through the custard are generous chunks of browned, crumbled bratwurst sausage and softened, diced onion pieces, adding rustic texture. Melted, bubbly Emmental cheese peeks through, creating small pockets of golden-brown crust. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The tart is presented as a generous wedge, revealing the layered interior of savory sausage, sweet onion, and creamy, cheesy custard. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and hearty appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sharp German mustard.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer traditional German rye bread or pumpernickel alongside.
Pair with a crisp German white wine or a light lager.
instructions: Combine flour and a pinch of salt in a large bowl. Add cold butter cubes. Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add ice water, mixing until dough just comes together. Form dough into a disc. Wrap in plastic film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Remove casings from bratwurst sausages. Crumble sausage meat.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add crumbled bratwurst. Brown until cooked through, breaking up meat with a spoon. Drain excess fat. Remove bratwurst from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).

On a lightly floured surface, roll out chilled pastry dough into a 30 cm circle. Carefully transfer dough to a 24 cm tart tin. Press into place. Trim excess pastry. Prick the bottom of the pastry with a fork.
Spread half of the grated cheese evenly over the pastry base.
Distribute cooked bratwurst and sautéed onion-garlic mixture over the cheese. Sprinkle remaining cheese over the filling.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, heavy cream, milk, Dijon mustard, grated nutmeg, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Pour custard mixture carefully over the tart filling.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the custard is set and lightly golden. The internal temperature of the filling should reach 75°C (167°F).
Let the tart cool in the tin for 10 minutes before carefully removing and slicing into wedges.
Garnish each slice with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the tart custard is fully set for optimal slicing and texture.
For best results, use good quality bratwurst and a flavorful, meltable cheese like Emmental or Gruyere.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Saffron Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Braised Beef with Saffron Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, dark brown chunk of fork-tender braised beef, showcasing its rich, slow-cooked texture, rests prominently on one side. Beside it, a golden-yellow pool of creamy saffron risotto flows naturally, reflecting its fluid, al dente consistency. A glossy, deep red-brown braising sauce, reduced to perfection, is artfully spooned over the beef, creating a glistening sheen. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of vibrant green finely chopped fresh parsley over the beef and a few delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese atop the risotto. The composition is balanced and elegant, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded linen napkin and traditional European flatware, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich braising sauce.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 60 g, grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat beef chunks dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Add bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme. Return seared beef to the pot. Liquid should mostly cover the beef. If not, add more broth.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Check internal temperature. Beef must reach 75°C (167°F).
Once beef is tender, remove from oven. Carefully remove beef chunks from the pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids and herbs.
