Remove rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped Italian parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Black Garlic Purée, Confit Tomato, Beef Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef tenderloin chunk, boasting a deep mahogany crust and a vibrant pink interior, anchors the pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent, a deliberate, elongated swirl of glossy, charcoal-black garlic purée offers a striking contrast. Scattered artfully are three to four glistening, ruby-red confit cherry tomatoes, their skins delicately softened. A rich, dark beef jus is precisely spooned around the beef, creating a reflective pool. The dish is finished with a few delicate sprigs of bright green micro-chervil, adding a touch of freshness and color. Abundant negative space surrounds the minimalist composition, emphasizing the architectural precision and premium ingredients. The plate rests on a cool, veined white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by simple, elegant silver flatware and a crisply folded white linen napkin, bathed in dramatic, focused lighting.
instructions: Prepare Beef Jus: Finely chop shallots. Sauté shallots in a small pot until softened. Add beef stock, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by two-thirds until thick and flavorful. Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
Prepare Black Garlic Purée: Peel black garlic cloves. Blend cloves with a tablespoon of warm water or reserved beef jus until perfectly smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Confit Cherry Tomatoes: Place cherry tomatoes and peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover completely with 100ml olive oil. Cook gently over very low heat for 20-25 minutes until tomatoes are slightly softened and garlic is tender. Carefully remove tomatoes and garlic from oil; set aside.

Cook Beef Tenderloin: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat beef tenderloin dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat 30ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef in pan. Sear on all sides for 2-3 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. Add butter, remaining thyme, and rosemary to the pan. Baste beef continuously for 2 minutes. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 55°C for medium-rare. Remove beef from oven. Rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes before cutting into two thick chunks per serving.

Plate Dish: Spoon an elongated swirl of black garlic purée onto one side of each plate. Carefully place two seared beef tenderloin chunks next to the purée. Artfully arrange 3-4 confit cherry tomatoes and a confit garlic clove near the beef. Drizzle the rich beef jus elegantly around the beef and purée. Garnish sparingly with a few sprigs of micro-chervil.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Chicken Paprika Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Hungarian Chicken Paprika Stew is presented in a clean white porcelain shallow bowl. The stew features rich reddish-brown chicken chunks, roughly cut potatoes, carrots, and vibrant red bell pepper pieces. The chicken is seared golden-brown before simmering, showcasing a tender, succulent texture. Vegetables are soft but hold their shape. A creamy swirl of white sour cream is artfully incorporated into the stew, adding a subtle contrast. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, freshly chopped parsley. The overall composition is balanced and appealing, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's warm colors and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional Hungarian nokedli (small dumplings).
Offer crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Present with a side of pickled cucumbers or cabbage.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Dice onions. Chop garlic finely.
Peel potatoes and carrots. Cut potatoes, carrots, and bell pepper into 2-3 cm rough pieces.
Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add chopped garlic, sweet paprika, and smoked paprika. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn the paprika.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add chopped potatoes, carrots, and bell pepper. Stir well.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and vegetables are cooked through.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Stir in sour cream until fully incorporated. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure paprika does not burn when sautéing, as it can become bitter.
Do not boil the stew after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
traditional_techniques: Pörkölt preparation (meat stew with paprika and onions)

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Tomato and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rich Braised Beef with Tomato and Garlic is meticulously plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three substantial, irregular chunks of dark, fork-tender braised beef, showcasing a deep mahogany crust, are centrally arranged. They are partially submerged in a glossy, thick, reddish-brown sauce, studded with small, tender diced pieces of tomato, onion, and carrot. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a bright green contrast over the beef and sauce. The dish is presented on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded off-white cotton napkin beside the plate. A polished silver fork and knife rest to the right. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, inviting bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
Accompany with creamy mashed potatoes or polenta
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Stir well.
Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours.
Cook until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf before serving.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot.
notes: For best flavor, braise the beef a day ahead and gently reheat. Flavors deepen overnight.
Ensure beef is very tender; cooking time may vary based on beef cut and thickness.
Use a good quality dry red wine that you would enjoy drinking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Creamy Corn Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef medallions with creamy corn risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The golden-yellow risotto forms a free-flowing base, showcasing visible whole corn kernels. Two thick, seared beef medallions, with a rich, dark brown crust and tender interior, are placed slightly overlapping on the risotto. A small pool of glistening garlic-herb butter with delicate thyme leaves is drizzled over the beef. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is scattered across the dish. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A folded grey linen napkin and standard silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat beef dry. Cut into 8 equal medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Finely dice onion and mince 4 garlic cloves.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and 30 g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until liquid is mostly absorbed before adding more. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 15 minutes, stir in corn kernels.
Once rice is creamy and al dente, remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Cover and let rest 2 minutes.
While risotto rests, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary.
Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Melt remaining 30 g butter in a small saucepan. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Add to butter with fresh thyme sprigs. Simmer gently for 2 minutes.

To plate, spoon creamy risotto onto each white porcelain plate. Arrange two seared beef medallions slightly overlapping on top of the risotto. Drizzle garlic-herb butter over beef and risotto. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Use high-quality beef for best results. Adjust cooking time for beef based on thickness and desired doneness.
Risotto should be creamy and flow slightly, not stiff or dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon and Cheese Gratinéed Toast
recipes.visual_description: A single individual starter portion of Bacon and Cheese Gratinéed Toast is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The thick-cut white toast is generously covered with a creamy, rich béchamel sauce. Crispy, small diced bacon pieces are visible beneath the melted American cheese, which is golden-brown and bubbling, showing slight caramelization at the edges. The cheese drapes naturally over the sides of the toast. The colors are warm, ranging from the golden toast to the creamy white sauce, the reddish-brown bacon, and the vibrant golden cheese. The texture is a contrast of soft bread, creamy sauce, crisp bacon, and gooey melted cheese. A simple white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
Accompanied by a small glass of a light, dry white wine or water.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook diced bacon in a skillet over medium heat. Cook until crispy. Drain bacon on paper towels. Set aside.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add flour. Whisk for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Continue whisking until sauce thickens and is smooth. This is your béchamel sauce.
Season béchamel with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Remove from heat.
Lightly toast bread slices. Spread a generous layer of béchamel sauce on each slice.
Scatter cooked bacon pieces evenly over the béchamel. Place two slices of American cheese on top of each toast, covering the bacon.
Place toasts on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and edges are golden. Alternatively, broil for 2-3 minutes until cheese is golden brown.
Serve immediately as a warm starter.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Paccheri with Fermented Onion & Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of paccheri pasta forms a gentle mound on a matte cream-beige ceramic plate. The pasta is richly coated in a rustic, reddish-brown tomato sauce, showcasing slow-cooked passata and caramelized fermented onions. Small, irregularly diced, crispy bacon pieces are thoughtfully scattered on top, offering dark brown hues and crunch. Vibrant green, torn basil leaves are sparingly placed for color. Emerald green basil stem oil subtly drizzled around the base, adding a glossy finish. Plating emphasizes natural beauty with ample white space. The scene rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface. An undyed natural linen napkin is beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light highlights textures. A subtle green plant, out of focus, reinforces the eco-conscious theme. Simple traditional silver flatware completes the clean, uncluttered composition, focusing solely on pure ingredient beauty.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of dry Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Enjoy as a shared family meal, with portions served from a central bowl.

ingredients.name: Fresh Basil
ingredients.quantity: 1 large bunch (approx. 50g), leaves picked, stems reserved

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.quantity: 50 ml, plus extra for basil oil

instructions: Prepare Basil Oil: Wash basil stems thoroughly. Combine reserved basil stems with 50 ml extra virgin olive oil in a small saucepan. Gently heat over low flame for 10 minutes. Do not fry. Remove from heat. Let steep for 30 minutes. Strain oil, discard stems. Set aside.
Cook Bacon: Place diced bacon in a cold large pan. Render bacon over medium-low heat until crispy. Remove crispy bacon bits with a slotted spoon. Reserve bacon fat in the pan.

Sauté Onions and Garlic: Add fermented onions to the reserved bacon fat in the pan. Cook over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Add sliced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Simmer Sauce: Pour in tomato passata and 200 ml water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and black pepper.

Cook Pasta: While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add paccheri pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Combine and Finish: Add drained pasta directly to the sauce. Add grated parmesan cheese and half of the fresh basil leaves (torn). Stir well to coat pasta. Add reserved pasta water gradually, if needed, to achieve a fluid sauce consistency.

Serve: Divide pasta among plates. Garnish with reserved crispy bacon bits and remaining fresh basil leaves. Drizzle generously with basil oil. Serve immediately with extra grated parmesan on the side.
notes: Fermented onions provide a complex, tangy, and deeply savory flavor profile. Begin fermentation 3-5 days in advance.
This recipe utilizes bacon fat and basil stems, minimizing food waste.
The sauce benefits from slow simmering, allowing flavors to meld.
Adjust pasta water to achieve desired sauce consistency; Italian pasta sauces should coat the pasta without being overly thick or dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple "Ravioli" with Strawberry Fluid Gel and Lime Caviar
recipes.visual_description: A Michelin-starred dessert, elegantly plated on a pristine white bone china plate set on a white Carrara marble surface. Two to three translucent, paper-thin apple "ravioli" with a creamy vanilla-lime mascarpone filling are arranged in a delicate, organic curve, showcasing their precise round shape. A vibrant ruby-red strawberry fluid gel forms a flowing line or several artful dots beside the apple, contrasting with its pale hue. Small clusters of luminous, clear-green lime caviar spheres are strategically placed to add a burst of acidity and visual interest. A few tiny, dark green micro basil leaves provide a final touch of color and freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist and sophisticated composition. The setting features a precisely folded white linen napkin and a single elegant silver dessert fork, all under dramatic professional lighting that casts subtle shadows.
instructions: Prepare Apple "Ravioli" Filling: Combine mascarpone, vanilla bean paste, lime zest, and powdered sugar in a bowl. Mix until smooth. Chill.

Prepare Strawberry Fluid Gel: Wash and hull strawberries. Blend until smooth. Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve. In a saucepan, combine sieved puree, 30g granulated sugar, 15ml lime juice, and agar-agar. Bring to a boil, whisking, for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set (30 minutes). Cut into chunks. Blend in a high-speed blender until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Store in a squeeze bottle.

Prepare Lime Caviar: Dissolve calcium lactate in 500ml distilled water in a tall glass for the calcium bath. In a separate bowl, whisk sodium alginate into 100ml lime juice, 50ml water, and 20g granulated sugar until dissolved. Let lime base rest for 1 hour to remove air bubbles. Using a syringe, slowly drip lime base into the calcium bath. Let caviar sit for 1-2 minutes. Strain caviar. Rinse briefly with fresh water. Store in a small amount of water.

Prepare Apple Sheets: Wash apples. Using a mandoline, slice apples into paper-thin sheets. Use a 6-7 cm round cutter to cut uniform apple circles. Keep circles in lightly acidulated water to prevent browning. Pat dry before use.

Assemble "Ravioli": Lay out half of the apple circles. Place a small dollop (5g) of mascarpone filling in the center of each. Top with another apple circle. Gently press edges to seal. Prepare 2-3 "ravioli" per serving.

Plating: On each dessert plate, artfully arrange 2-3 apple "ravioli". Squeeze small, precise dots or a flowing line of strawberry fluid gel alongside the "ravioli". Carefully spoon small clusters of lime caviar onto the plate. Garnish with a few delicate micro basil or mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Saffron Risotto with White Bean Puree and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a minimalist, premium bone china plate with abundant white space. A golden, fluid pool of Saffron Risotto forms the base, its creamy texture evident. Nestled within the risotto is a smooth, pristine white dollop of White Bean Puree, offering a soft contrast. Vibrant, slow-roasted cherry tomato halves, their skins slightly wrinkled and caramelized, are artfully placed on and around the puree, providing bursts of intense red. A scattering of delicate, golden-brown crispy shallot rings adds textural crunch. Fresh green basil leaves provide a final touch of color and freshness. The composition is organic and flowing, avoiding rigid shapes. The plate rests on a white Carrara marble surface with a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's elegant simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Prepare Saffron Broth: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Add saffron threads. Keep warm.

Prepare Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 140°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small baking dish. Add 50 ml olive oil, 1 crushed garlic clove, salt, pepper. Roast for 45 minutes until tender. Set aside.

Prepare Crispy Shallots: Thinly slice 2 shallots into rings. Heat frying oil in a small saucepan to 170°C. Fry shallot rings in batches until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Prepare White Bean Puree: Finely dice 1 shallot and 1 garlic clove. Sauté in 15 ml olive oil until translucent. Add cannellini beans and 150 ml vegetable broth. Simmer 5 minutes. Transfer to a blender. Blend until ultra-smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Saffron Risotto: In a wide, heavy-bottomed pan, heat 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter. Add remaining finely diced shallot. Sauté until translucent. Add Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine evaporates. Begin adding warm saffron broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until liquid is absorbed before adding more broth. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 40 g butter and Parmigiano Reggiano. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Cover and let rest 2 minutes (mantecatura). Risotto should be fluid.

To Serve: Ladle a generous portion of Saffron Risotto onto the center of each plate, allowing it to spread naturally. Create a small well in the risotto. Spoon a dollop of White Bean Puree into the well. Arrange a few Tomato Confit halves elegantly on and around the puree. Garnish with a sprinkle of Crispy Shallots and 2-3 fresh basil leaves. Drizzle lightly with extra virgin olive oil.
notes: Ensure risotto is al dente and has a fluid, wavy consistency.
Blend the bean puree until exceptionally smooth and velvety.
For the tomato confit, avoid over-roasting; they should remain plump.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Noodles
recipes.special_requests: less calories, no broccoli, translate to German
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of spicy beef noodles fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Thick, dark brown noodles are coated in a glossy, savory sauce. Tender, irregularly cut chunks of seared beef, displaying a deep brown crust, are interspersed throughout. Thinly sliced white onion and vibrant red chili pieces add color and texture. Freshly sliced green onions are scattered casually over the top for contrast. The noodles are artfully tangled, appearing scooped from a pan, overlapping the beef and vegetables. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. Dark wooden chopsticks rest beside it. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed. Warm, soft light illuminates the cozy family kitchen scene. The plate is adequately filled, showcasing the homely, comforting nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with chopsticks
Often accompanied by a small side of pickled vegetables or a clear broth
instructions: Slice beef sirloin into thin strips. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, beef stock, and sesame oil. Set aside.
In another small bowl, mix cornstarch with water to create a slurry. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add beef strips. Sear until browned on all sides, about 3-4 minutes. Remove beef from skillet.
Add sliced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the skillet.
Pour in the soy sauce mixture. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens, about 1-2 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook noodles according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Add cooked noodles to the skillet with the beef and sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in deep bowls. Garnish with sliced green onions.
notes: This dish is best served hot immediately after preparation.
Adjust chili quantity to preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Tartare, Aged Cheddar Tuile, Pickled Shallot
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly formed, small cylindrical mound of finely diced beef tartare, glistening with olive oil and studded with vibrant green chives and tiny capers. Adjacent to the tartare, a delicate, irregularly shaped, golden-brown aged cheddar tuile stands upright, offering a textural contrast. A few translucent, thinly sliced pickled shallot rings are artfully scattered around the base of the tartare. The composition is set slightly off-center on a pristine, large, round bone china plate with subtle, almost imperceptible patterns, leaving abundant negative space. The plate rests on a cool, grey-veined marble surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits to the side. The overall presentation is one of extreme restraint and sophisticated simplicity, showcasing flawless execution of each element.
instructions: Prepare pickled shallots: Thinly slice shallots into rings. Combine white wine vinegar, water, and sugar in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over shallot rings. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare cheddar tuiles: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Grate aged cheddar. Spread thin, even circles of cheddar onto the parchment. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool on a wire rack.

Prepare beef tartare: Finely dice beef tenderloin into small cubes (2-3 mm). Place in a chilled bowl. Add chopped capers, cornichons, Dijon mustard, olive oil, and most of the minced chives. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Gently mix until just combined.

Assemble and plate: Using a ring mold, place a small cylindrical mound of beef tartare on a large, bone china plate. Remove the mold carefully. Arrange one delicate, irregularly shaped cheddar tuile upright beside the tartare. Artfully scatter a few pickled shallot rings around the base of the tartare. Garnish with remaining minced chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Noodle Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spicy Beef Noodle Stir-fry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, reflecting a homely setting. Thin, brown beef strips are naturally arranged amidst a tangle of golden-yellow egg noodles. Interspersed throughout are translucent slices of red onion, vibrant green pieces of chopped green onion, and fiery red chili slices, offering pops of color. The noodles are coated in a glossy, dark savory sauce, indicating a rich flavor. The dish has a slightly moist, inviting texture. The beef shows caramelized edges from searing. The presentation is casual and natural, with ingredients overlapping and touching, as if served directly from the wok onto a family dining table. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden table, accompanied by a pair of simple wooden chopsticks. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of chili oil or sriracha on the side for extra heat.
Offer extra soy sauce for individual seasoning.
Serve alongside a simple clear broth soup.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin
ingredients.quantity: 500 grams, thinly sliced against the grain into 5 cm strips

instructions: In a bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, cornstarch, and water or broth. Whisk well. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add egg noodles and cook according to package instructions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.

Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until smoking. Add beef strips in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes until browned on one side. Flip and sear for another 1-2 minutes. Remove beef from wok and set aside. Do not overcrowd the wok; cook in batches if necessary.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add sliced red onion and stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced red chili. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the wok. Add cooked noodles.
Stir the prepared sauce mixture and pour over the noodles and beef. Toss everything quickly for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately.
For chicken, cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Vegetable Noodle Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A modest, comforting single portion of spicy beef and vegetable noodles rests on a simple, well-used ceramic plate. The plate, an everyday off-white or light blue, sits on a warm wooden dining table. Thinly sliced beef strips are interwoven with tender egg noodles, creating a natural, flowing mound. Vibrant green broccoli florets, bright red bell pepper strips, and julienned orange carrots are generously mixed throughout, providing bursts of natural color and varied textures. Minced garlic and chili bits cling to the ingredients, hinting at the savory heat. The sauce coats everything with a glossy, inviting sheen. A sprinkle of freshly chopped green spring onions adds a final touch of freshness. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, suggesting a relaxed family meal. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests casually beside the plate. The overall presentation is unpretentious and homely, focused on the hearty, natural appeal of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with an extra side of chili oil for those who prefer more heat.
Offer soy sauce on the side.
Serve with chopsticks and a small ceramic bowl.
instructions: Slice beef thinly against the grain. In a bowl, toss beef with 5g cornstarch, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Cook noodles according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Heat 10ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add beef. Stir-fry quickly until browned. Remove beef. Set aside.
Add remaining 5ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add thinly sliced onion, minced garlic, and thinly sliced chili. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add broccoli florets and julienned carrots. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add bell pepper strips. Stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, remaining 5g cornstarch, and 60ml water.
Return beef to the wok. Add cooked noodles. Pour sauce mixture over noodles and beef.
Toss everything together until sauce thickens and coats ingredients. This takes about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped spring onions.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to personal spice preference.
For a vegetarian option, replace beef with firm tofu and oyster sauce with vegetarian mushroom sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beef and Beer Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Belgian Beef and Beer Stew is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a rich, deep mahogany-brown stew. Large, tender chunks of braised beef are nestled within the thick, glossy sauce, which has a subtle sheen from the dark beer reduction. Small, golden-brown sautéed mushroom halves are scattered within the stew, adding earthy notes. Beside the stew, a neat cluster of vibrant, crisp-tender blanched green bean batons provides a contrasting splash of emerald green. Nearby, several creamy, irregular chunks of boiled potato are carefully placed. The entire dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley and a few scattered pieces of crispy, golden-brown bacon lardons, adding texture and a smoky aroma. The plate is well-proportioned with moderate negative space, appearing inviting and comforting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
Traditionally, Carbonnade is often served with Belgian fries (frites) or boiled potatoes.
A glass of the same dark Belgian beer used in the stew is a traditional accompaniment.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon and set aside, leaving rendered fat.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, Dijon mustard, brown sugar, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While beef braises, prepare potatoes, mushrooms, and green beans.
Boil or steam potato chunks until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Sauté halved mushrooms in a separate pan with a touch of olive oil until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain.
Once beef is tender, remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves from the stew.
Taste and adjust seasoning. The stew should be rich and slightly thickened.
To serve, spoon a portion of the beef stew onto each plate.
Arrange boiled potato chunks, sautéed mushrooms, and blanched green bean batons neatly beside or around the stew.
Garnish the stew with reserved crispy bacon lardons and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The stew benefits from being made a day ahead, allowing flavors to deepen. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
Adjust the sweetness and tanginess with brown sugar and mustard to your preference.
Ensure the beer is a good quality dark Belgian ale, as its flavor is central to the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Roasted Apricot, Strawberry-Cherry Sorbet, Apricot Crémeux
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, allowing for abundant negative space. An elegant, organic swirl of smooth, pale orange apricot crémeux forms the base. Two honey-roasted apricot halves, their cut sides slightly caramelized and golden, are artfully nestled beside the crémeux. A small, vibrant crimson scoop of strawberry-cherry sorbet, intensely colored and icy, provides a striking temperature and color contrast. A delicate, golden-amber honey tuile stands upright, offering an architectural crispness. The arrangement is flowing and natural, avoiding rigid shapes. A few tiny, bright green mint microgreens are precisely placed, enhancing color and freshness. The setting features a premium white Carrara marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and professional, dramatic lighting casting soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Apricot Crémeux: Bloom gelatin. Combine apricot puree, sugar, egg yolks, milk, and cream in a saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill thoroughly for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set.

Prepare Strawberry-Cherry Sorbet: Combine sugar and water in a saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Cool completely to make simple syrup. Blend strawberries, cherries, simple syrup, and lemon juice until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds and pulp. Churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer's instructions. Freeze until firm.

Prepare Honey-Roasted Apricots: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Arrange apricot halves, cut-side up, on a baking sheet. Drizzle with melted butter and honey. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool slightly.

Prepare Honey Tuiles: Preheat oven to 170°C (340°F). Whisk melted butter, icing sugar, flour, honey, and egg white until smooth. Spread very thin layers of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment paper in desired shapes (e.g., irregular shards or delicate discs). Bake for 5-8 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Immediately remove from oven and, if desired, mold over a rolling pin or form into curves while warm. Let cool completely to harden.

Assemble the Dish: On each chilled plate, place a quenelle or elegant swirl of Apricot Crémeux slightly off-center. Arrange two warm honey-roasted apricot halves artfully beside the crémeux. Place a small scoop of Strawberry-Cherry Sorbet next to the apricots, allowing its vibrant color to contrast. Carefully place a Honey Tuile upright or leaning against a component for height and texture. Garnish sparingly with a few fresh mint microgreens for a touch of green and freshness. Ensure ample negative space on the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Spicy Beef Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Thai Spicy Beef Noodles is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. Thinly sliced, seared beef chunks are interspersed with broad, glistening rice noodles. Bright green broccoli florets and crisp red bell pepper strips add pops of color. The dish is generously garnished with fresh, aromatic holy basil leaves, adding a deep green contrast. A light sheen of savory sauce coats all ingredients, indicating proper stir-frying technique. The composition is organic and flowing, with elements naturally distributed, avoiding overcrowding. The plate sits on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a cotton napkin and a set of chopsticks, suggesting an authentic Thai dining experience. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies (Prik Nam Pla) for extra heat.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Best eaten immediately after preparation.
instructions: Prepare sauce: Combine oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, white pepper, and water in a small bowl. Mix well.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until smoking.
Add beef slices. Stir-fry quickly until browned, about 2-3 minutes. Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and chilies. Stir-fry until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add thinly sliced onion, broccoli florets, and bell pepper strips. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add fresh wide rice noodles to the wok. Pour sauce over noodles and vegetables. Toss vigorously to coat everything evenly.
Return beef to the wok. Add holy basil leaves.
Continue to stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until basil wilts and noodles are heated through. Ensure beef is cooked to 75°C.
Serve immediately.
notes: For less calories, use lean beef and limit oil.
Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.
Fresh wide rice noodles are preferred for texture.
traditional_techniques: Balancing of sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Apricot Honey Crémeux, Cherry Sphere, Strawberry Sorbet
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly composed dessert portion rests off-center on a pristine white bone china plate with subtle, organic texture. A vibrant red quenelle of strawberry sorbet, its surface subtly glistening with fine ice crystals, anchors the composition. Adjacent to it, an irregular, smooth dollop of pale apricot-honey crémeux, creamy and inviting, offers a soft textural contrast. Two perfectly formed, jewel-like cherry spheres, a deep ruby red, are nestled near the crémeux, promising a burst of liquid flavor. A delicate, golden-amber honey tuile shard stands tall, providing an architectural element and crisp texture. A few tiny, bright green micro-basil leaves are precisely placed for a hint of color and freshness. The plate is surrounded by abundant negative space, highlighting the deliberate placement of each element. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and dramatic, professional lighting creating soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated minimalism and refined artistry.
instructions: Prepare Sodium Alginate Bath: Whisk sodium alginate into distilled water. Use an immersion blender. Blend until smooth. Refrigerate for 12 hours to remove air bubbles. This is crucial.
Prepare Cherry Sphere Liquid: Whisk calcium lactate gluconate into cherry juice. Blend until smooth. Refrigerate for 1 hour.

Prepare Apricot Honey Crémeux: Bloom gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, combine apricot puree, honey, egg yolks, and sugar. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and reaches 82°C. Do not boil.

Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Let cool to 40°C. Gradually whisk in cold cubed butter until smooth and emulsified. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into shallow dishes. Chill until firm, at least 4 hours.

Prepare Strawberry Sorbet: In a small saucepan, combine sugar and water. Heat until sugar dissolves. Let cool. Combine cooled syrup, hulled strawberries, and lemon juice in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer instructions. Transfer to a freezer-safe container. Freeze until firm.

Prepare Honey Tuile: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat. Whisk melted butter, powdered sugar, honey, flour, and egg white until smooth. Spread very thin layers of batter onto the silicone mat using an offset spatula. Create irregular, delicate shapes. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Immediately drape over a rolling pin or other curved surface to shape as they cool. Store in an airtight container.

Assemble Cherry Spheres: Using a spherification spoon or syringe, carefully drop small amounts of cherry liquid into the sodium alginate bath. Let spheres form for 1-2 minutes. Gently remove spheres with a slotted spoon. Rinse thoroughly in a clean water bath. Place on a plate lined with parchment paper. Refrigerate until serving.

To Plate: Spoon a quenelle of chilled strawberry sorbet slightly off-center on a white, minimalist dessert plate. Place a small, irregular dollop of apricot honey crémeux next to the sorbet. Gently place one or two cherry spheres near the crémeux. Artistically place a honey tuile shard upright to add height and texture. Garnish with a few micro-basil or micro-mint leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure all spherification ingredients are precisely measured for best results.
Work quickly when shaping tuiles as they cool and harden fast.
The alginate bath can be reused for several batches of spheres.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey Vanilla Panna Cotta with Summer Berry Compote and Roasted Apricots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Honey Vanilla Panna Cotta is elegantly centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The panna cotta forms a smooth, creamy white dome, reflecting light gently. Beside it, a vibrant ruby-red summer berry compote is artfully spooned, showcasing diced strawberries and halved cherries, with a slight natural sheen. Two golden-orange roasted apricot halves, tender and slightly caramelized at their edges, are arranged thoughtfully around the panna cotta, adding warmth and depth. A few small, fresh mint leaves provide a bright green contrast. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver dessert spoon and a neatly folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Bloom gelatine sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes. Set aside.
Split vanilla bean lengthwise. Scrape seeds into a medium saucepan. Add bean pod, heavy cream, whole milk, and 80g honey to the saucepan.
Heat mixture over medium heat until simmering gently. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Discard vanilla bean pod.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatine sheets. Whisk gelatine into hot cream mixture until fully dissolved.
Pour mixture evenly into 4 individual ramekins or molds (approx. 150ml each).
Chill panna cotta in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until set.
For the berry compote: Wash and hull strawberries. Dice strawberries into small cubes. Pit cherries and halve them.
Combine diced strawberries, halved cherries, optional 20g sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and mixture thickens slightly. Cool completely.
For the roasted apricots: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Halve apricots and remove pits. Toss apricot halves with remaining 15g honey.
Place apricots cut-side up on a small baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Cool slightly.
To serve: Briefly dip the bottom of each ramekin in hot water to loosen. Invert panna cotta onto the center of individual white porcelain plates.
Spoon a generous amount of berry compote beside each panna cotta.
Arrange 2 roasted apricot halves artfully around the panna cotta.
Garnish each plate with a few fresh mint leaves for color and aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Guisado con Frijoles y Maíz
recipes.visual_description: The Annatto Chicken, Bean, and Corn Skillet is presented as a comforting, rustic single portion on an earthy, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, suggesting handmade quality. Large, irregular chunks of seared chicken, each about 4-5 cm, are nestled amongst vibrant red-orange diced tomatoes, golden corn kernels, and dark black beans. The chicken has a rich, deep orange hue from the annatto, with visible caramelized edges from searing. The diced onions are softened and integrated into the saucy base, which has a moderate viscosity, allowing the individual ingredients to be distinct yet cohesive. A generous sprinkling of roughly chopped fresh cilantro provides a bright green contrast across the top. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, filling the plate adequately but not overflowing, leaving some negative space around the edges. The dish is placed on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen. Beside the plate, a small stack of warm, soft corn tortillas is casually placed, along with two bright green lime wedges. A simple, rustic metal spoon rests beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural colors and textures of the homely meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Serve with a simple side of white rice.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4-5 cm chunks
can black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in achiote paste until dissolved.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F).
Stir in rinsed black beans and corn kernels. Cook for 5 minutes more, or until heated through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Beef Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single serving of Spicy Korean Beef Noodles is centrally mounded on a clean, round white porcelain bowl. The dish features glossy, translucent sweet potato starch noodles intertwined with thinly sliced, seared beef chunks that display a slight char. Brightly colored julienned red bell peppers and carrots provide crisp contrast, alongside wilted green spinach leaves and green onion pieces. The entire composition is lightly coated in a rich, reddish-brown sauce, indicating the spicy gochugaru. A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and fresh chopped green onions garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks resting beside it. A small white ceramic dish holding a vibrant red kimchi and another with yellow pickled radish (danmuji) are placed nearby, enhancing the cultural authenticity. A folded light grey cotton napkin is positioned neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors against a subtly blurred, modern bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional Korean side dishes (banchan) like kimchi and pickled radish (danmuji).
Enjoy with a clear, light broth on the side.
Eat using chopsticks.

ingredients.name: Green Onions
ingredients.quantity: 3, cut into 5 cm lengths, plus extra for garnish

ingredients.name: Gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, for beef marinade)
Water or Beef Broth (for noodle sauce)

instructions: Prepare beef: Slice beef thinly against the grain. Combine with all marinade ingredients in a bowl. Mix well. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Cook noodles: Boil Korean sweet potato noodles according to package directions until tender but chewy. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Drain again thoroughly.
Prepare vegetables: Julienne bell pepper and carrot. Thinly slice onion. Cut green onions into 5 cm lengths. Mince garlic.

Stir-fry vegetables: Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add sliced onion, julienned carrot, and julienned bell pepper. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Add spinach and green onions. Stir-fry for 1 minute until spinach wilts. Remove vegetables from pan. Set aside.

Cook beef: Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the hot pan. Add marinated beef in a single layer. Stir-fry quickly for 2-3 minutes until beef is browned and cooked through. Ensure no pink remains. Cook beef to 75°C (167°F). Remove beef from pan. Set aside.
Combine: Add cooked noodles to the pan. Add all Noodle Sauce ingredients. Toss well to coat noodles evenly.
Return cooked beef and vegetables to the pan with the noodles. Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Heat through for 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish with extra green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: For a milder dish, reduce the amount of gochugaru.
Use lean cuts of beef to keep the dish light.
Ensure noodles are thoroughly drained to prevent a watery sauce.
traditional_techniques: High-heat stir-frying (bokkeum) to achieve tender-crisp vegetables and seared beef.
Proper noodle preparation for chewy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fresh Tomato-Basil Passata
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, presented whole, rests elegantly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously draped with a vibrant, rustic fresh tomato-basil passata, showcasing the rich red of ripe tomatoes and flecks of bright green basil. Around the chicken, glistening, slightly charred roasted cherry tomato halves add bursts of color. Fresh whole basil leaves and delicate Parmigiano Reggiano shavings complete the garnish. The dish presents a contrast of tender chicken, smooth yet chunky sauce, and soft roasted tomatoes. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware, creating a modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting. The background is clean and unobtrusive.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or Chicken stock

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until deeply golden and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced red onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine (or chicken stock), scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Add roughly chopped plum tomatoes to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and sauce thickens slightly.

While sauce simmers, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss halved cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a small baking tray. Roast for 10-15 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

Remove sauce from heat. Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves. Season the passata with salt and pepper to taste. For a smoother sauce, lightly crush the tomatoes with a spoon or potato masher, or pulse briefly with an immersion blender.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan with the tomato-basil passata. Simmer gently for 2-3 minutes to warm through and allow flavors to meld.
Plate each chicken thigh with a generous portion of the fresh tomato-basil passata. Garnish with roasted cherry tomatoes, a few fresh whole basil leaves, and optional Parmigiano Reggiano shavings.
traditional_techniques: Building a simple tomato sauce (passata style)

recipes.recipe_name: Blackberry and Cherry Frangipane Tart
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Blackberry and Cherry Frangipane Tart rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The pastry crust is a delicate golden-brown, crisp at the edges. The creamy, baked frangipane filling is a rich, light tan, slightly puffed. Scattered across the frangipane are plump, glossy blackberries and deep red, pitted cherries, some slightly sunken into the filling, others peeking out. Their vibrant colors create a beautiful contrast against the neutral frangipane. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly covers the fruit and tart edges. The tart slice is presented neatly, occupying the center-left of the plate, leaving ample negative space. The setting is a rustic wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, illuminated by soft, natural light, creating a simple, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a quenelle of crème fraîche
Serve with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Combine 125g flour, 40g powdered sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in 60g cold butter until pea-sized crumbs form.
Add egg yolk; mix until dough just comes together. Add cold water if too dry.
Form dough into a disc, wrap, and chill 30 minutes.
Roll chilled dough to 3 mm thickness. Line a 20 cm tart pan. Trim edges.
Prick bottom with fork. Chill 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Line crust with parchment paper, fill with pie weights. Blind bake 15 minutes.
Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 minutes more until lightly golden. Cool crust.
Cream 75g softened butter and 75g granulated sugar until light.
Beat in 1 large egg and vanilla extract.
Fold in almond flour and 5g all-purpose flour until combined.
Wash blackberries. Pit cherries.
Spread frangipane evenly into the cooled, blind-baked tart shell.
Arrange blackberries and pitted cherries over the frangipane.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 35-45 minutes, or until frangipane is golden brown and set. A skewer inserted should come out clean.
Cool tart completely on a wire rack.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Panna Cotta with Blackberry Cherry Compote
recipes.visual_description: The Lemon Panna Cotta is elegantly presented as a single, perfectly molded dome on a pristine white porcelain plate. Its surface is smooth and creamy, a delicate off-white hue. Adjacent to the panna cotta, a vibrant, rich compote of cooked blackberries and pitted cherries pools naturally. The compote showcases softened fruit pieces, some slightly burst, revealing their deep red and purple tones. A few fine curls of bright yellow lemon zest are scattered over the panna cotta, providing a subtle color contrast. A small, fresh green mint sprig rests delicately beside the compote. The composition is clean and balanced, with ample negative space. The dish is set on a light wooden table, accompanied by a polished silver dessert spoon and a folded white cotton napkin, bathed in soft, even natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve well chilled for optimal texture and refreshing taste.
instructions: Soak gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until softened.
In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, 70 g granulated sugar, and lemon zest. Heat over medium heat until sugar dissolves and cream is warm, just before simmering. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin sheets. Stir softened gelatin into the warm cream mixture until fully dissolved.
Stir in 30 ml fresh lemon juice.
Pour mixture evenly into 4 individual molds or ramekins. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until set.
For the compote, combine blackberries, pitted cherries, 50 g granulated sugar, and 15 ml fresh lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Cook until fruits soften and release their juices, forming a slightly thickened sauce. Some fruit pieces should remain intact.
Remove from heat. Let compote cool completely.
To serve, carefully unmold each panna cotta onto a clean white porcelain plate. Dip molds briefly in hot water if needed to loosen.
Spoon a generous amount of blackberry cherry compote next to or over the panna cotta.
Garnish each plate with a fresh mint sprig and a few fine lemon zest curls.
notes: For easy unmolding, lightly grease molds with a neutral oil before pouring in the panna cotta mixture, or dip the bottom of the mold in hot water for a few seconds.
Adjust sugar in compote to your preference, depending on fruit sweetness.
Panna cotta can be made a day in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta with Blackberry Cherry Compote and Candied Lemon Peel
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy vanilla bean panna cotta is perfectly unmolded, standing as a pristine, smooth white dome on a clean white porcelain plate. Its surface has a subtle sheen, indicating a delicate wobble. Beside the panna cotta, a vibrant pool of blackberry and cherry compote bursts with rich reds and deep purples, showcasing soft, intact fruit pieces. The compote is casually spooned, creating an organic shape that complements the panna cotta's form. A few thin, translucent strips of golden candied lemon peel are delicately placed on top of the panna cotta, adding a touch of bright yellow and a subtle architectural element. The overall presentation is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the contrasting colors and textures. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its fresh, inviting appearance.
instructions: Prepare Candied Lemon Peel:
Wash lemon thoroughly. Peel lemon, avoiding white pith. Cut peels into thin strips (julienne).
Blanch lemon strips in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Repeat blanching two more times.
Combine 100g sugar and 100ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Dissolve sugar.
Add blanched lemon strips to syrup. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until translucent.
Remove strips with a fork. Place on parchment paper to dry.
Prepare Panna Cotta:
If using gelatin sheets, soak in cold water for 5-10 minutes until soft. Squeeze out excess water.
In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, 80g sugar, and vanilla bean seeds and pod.
Heat over medium heat until simmering gently. Do not boil. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat. Discard vanilla pod.
Stir in softened gelatin. Stir until fully dissolved.
Pour panna cotta mixture into four 150ml molds or ramekins.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set.
Prepare Blackberry Cherry Compote:
Combine blackberries, pitted cherries, 50g sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Cook until fruits soften and mixture thickens slightly. Some fruit pieces should remain.
Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Assemble and Serve:
To unmold panna cotta, briefly dip bottom of mold in hot water. Invert onto serving plates.
Spoon a generous amount of blackberry cherry compote beside or over panna cotta.
Garnish with a few pieces of candied lemon peel. Serve immediately.
notes: Prepare panna cotta and compote ahead of time for best results and chilling.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Vanilla Panna Cotta with Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Vanilla Panna Cotta is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The panna cotta, a smooth, pale ivory dome, sits off-center. Its surface is perfectly set and glossy. Alongside it, a vibrant mound of mixed berry compote gleams, showcasing whole and halved blackberries and cherries in a rich, slightly thickened ruby-purple sauce. A delicate sprig of fresh mint leaves rests on the panna cotta, and a thin, curled strip of bright yellow lemon zest is placed beside the compote. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the contrasting colors and textures. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly arranged beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refreshing dessert.
Can be paired with a light sparkling wine.
instructions: Prepare Gelatin: Sprinkle gelatin powder over cold water in a small bowl. Let bloom for 5 minutes.

Infuse Cream: Combine heavy cream, milk, 70g sugar, vanilla bean seeds and pod, and lemon zest in a saucepan. Heat gently over medium-low heat until sugar dissolves and mixture is warm. Do not boil. Remove from heat.
Dissolve Gelatin: Remove vanilla pod from cream mixture. Add bloomed gelatin. Stir until completely dissolved.
Chill Panna Cotta: Pour mixture into four 150 ml ramekins or molds. Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until set.

Make Berry Compote: Combine blackberries, halved cherries, 30g sugar, and 15ml lemon juice in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and sauce thickens slightly. Cool to room temperature.

Serve: To unmold panna cotta, briefly dip bottom of mold in warm water. Invert onto a chilled plate. Spoon berry compote alongside or over the panna cotta. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig and a lemon zest curl.
notes: For best results, prepare panna cotta the day before serving.
Adjust sugar in compote based on the sweetness of your berries.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Penne with Roasted Garlic and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Baked Penne with Roasted Garlic and Mozzarella is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The penne pasta, perfectly al dente, is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Throughout the dish, irregular, melted chunks of fresh mozzarella create inviting, golden-brown pools and gooey strands, contrasting with the pasta. Soft, whole roasted garlic cloves are nestled among the pasta, adding a subtle visual texture. The dish is garnished with several fresh, bright green basil leaves, providing a pop of color and freshness. A light drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on the surface. The presentation is organized but naturally flowing, showcasing the ingredients' textures and colors. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface with standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut tops off garlic heads. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast for 40 minutes until soft.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
While pasta cooks, mince 3 garlic cloves.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
Once roasted garlic is cool enough to handle, squeeze cloves from skin into the sauce. Mash gently with a fork. Stir well.
Tear fresh mozzarella into irregular, medium-sized pieces.
In a large baking dish, combine drained penne, tomato sauce, and half of the mozzarella pieces. Stir gently to combine.
Top with remaining mozzarella pieces.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and bubbly, and slightly golden.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: This dish is best served immediately for optimal cheese texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Nectarine and Cherry Galette
recipes.visual_description: A single wedge of Nectarine and Cherry Galette rests elegantly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The galette features a golden-brown, rustic pastry crust, lightly crimped at the edges, folded inwards to cradle a vibrant filling. Thinly sliced, pale orange nectarines are arranged amongst deep red, halved cherries, their natural juices creating a glistening, tender fruit layer. A small, perfectly spherical scoop of creamy vanilla bean ice cream is positioned beside the galette, offering a cool contrast. The plate showcases moderate negative space, emphasizing the dessert. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light-toned wooden table surface, with a silver fork and a neatly folded white cotton napkin placed to the left of the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, creating soft shadows and highlighting the dessert's inviting textures and colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with vanilla bean ice cream or crème fraîche.

ingredients.name: Vanilla bean ice cream or crème fraîche (for serving)

instructions: Combine flour, 15g sugar, and salt in a food processor. Pulse briefly.
Add cold butter. Pulse until mixture resembles coarse crumbs with pea-sized butter pieces.
Gradually add iced water, 15ml at a time. Pulse until dough just comes together.
Form dough into a flat disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Halve nectarines. Slice thinly, about 5mm thick. Pit cherries. Halve large cherries.
In a bowl, combine sliced nectarines, cherries, 50g sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and vanilla extract. Mix gently.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out dough into a 30cm circle.
Carefully transfer dough to the prepared baking sheet.
Spread almond meal over the dough, leaving a 5cm border free.
Arrange the fruit mixture evenly over the almond meal, leaving the border clear.
Fold the dough border over the fruit, crimping gently to secure.
Whisk egg yolk and 5ml water for egg wash. Brush egg wash over the folded crust.
Sprinkle turbinado sugar over the egg-washed crust.
B Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and fruit is tender and bubbly.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes.
Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream or a dollop of crème fraîche.

recipes.recipe_name: Nectarine and Cherry Frangipane Tart
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Nectarine and Cherry Frangipane Tart sits on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. The golden-brown pâte sucrée crust is crisp. The creamy, pale frangipane filling holds roasted nectarine wedges and halved dark red cherries, slightly caramelized at their edges, showcasing their tender texture. A delicate dusting of white icing sugar covers the tart, lightly spilling onto the plate. A small, vibrant green mint sprig rests neatly beside the tart slice. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface. A silver dessert fork is placed to the right, and a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is to the left. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a clean, inviting dessert presentation with ample negative space.
instructions: For the Pâte Sucrée: Sift flour and salt into a bowl. Add cold diced butter. Rub butter into flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Stir in icing sugar. Add egg yolk and mix until dough just comes together. Form into a disc, wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 22 cm tart tin with a removable base.
Roll out chilled dough on a lightly floured surface to 3 mm thickness. Line the tart tin. Trim excess dough. Prick base with a fork. Chill for 15 minutes.
Blind bake the pastry shell: Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until light golden. Cool on a wire rack.

For the Frangipane: Cream softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Stir in almond meal and vanilla extract. Mix until smooth.
Prepare fruit: Wash nectarines. Cut into 1 cm thick wedges. Halve and pit cherries.
Assemble tart: Spread frangipane evenly into the cooled pastry shell. Arrange nectarine wedges and cherry halves on top of the frangipane. Sprinkle fruit with lemon juice.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until frangipane is golden brown and set. The fruit should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Cool tart in the tin on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before removing. Let cool completely or serve warm.
Dust generously with icing sugar before serving. Garnish each slice with a fresh mint sprig.
notes: Serve warm or at room temperature.
This tart can be stored at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerated for up to 4 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato Dauphinoise and Glazed Parsnips
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast rests on a clean white porcelain plate, its golden-brown crust contrasting with the tender, juicy interior. Beside it, a neat square of potato dauphinoise displays its delicate, thinly sliced layers, baked to a creamy, golden-edged perfection. Glazed parsnip batons, caramelized to a warm golden hue, are artfully arranged alongside. A rich, glossy pan sauce, made from the chicken's drippings, is spooned over the chicken, adding depth. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley, providing a pop of color. Served on a simple light wooden table with a folded cotton napkin, under soft, natural lighting, creating a refined bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Peel potatoes. Thinly slice potatoes (2mm thick) using a mandoline.
Lightly rub a gratin dish with one minced garlic clove.
Arrange potato slices in layers in the prepared dish. Season each layer with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.
In a small saucepan, gently warm milk and cream with the remaining minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Do not boil.
Pour warm milk mixture over the potatoes. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and potatoes are tender. Let dauphinoise rest for 10 minutes after baking.
While dauphinoise bakes, prepare parsnips. Peel parsnips. Cut into 5cm (2-inch) batons or thick wedges.
Melt half of the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add parsnips to the skillet. Cook for 10-12 minutes, turning frequently, until golden brown and tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and remaining butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer the skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Return skillet (used for chicken) to medium heat. Add chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced. Adjust seasoning.

To plate, place a portion of potato dauphinoise on each plate. Arrange a chicken breast beside it. Neatly place glazed parsnips alongside. Spoon pan sauce over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Pasta with Grilled Watermelon and Herbed Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: This dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a moderately sized individual portion of orecchiette pasta. The golden, tender pasta forms the base, generously coated in a creamy, off-white herbed yogurt sauce. Nestled among the pasta are vibrant red, burst roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled from the heat. Interspersed throughout are succulent, grilled watermelon cubes, displaying distinct char marks and a deeper, caramelized red hue, contrasting beautifully with the pasta. The dish is garnished with bright green fresh mint and basil leaves, scattered artfully to add freshness and color. A dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese provides a final savory touch. The arrangement is organized yet natural, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The scene features a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere. A fork is positioned to the side, ready for dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty rustic bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon as an accompaniment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Cut watermelon into 2.5 cm cubes. In a bowl, toss watermelon cubes with 15 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Marinate for 10 minutes.

Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high heat. Grill watermelon cubes for 2-3 minutes per side, until grill marks appear and watermelon is slightly tender. Do not overcrowd the pan. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add orecchiette pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta water before draining.

While pasta cooks, prepare the yogurt sauce. In a medium bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt, remaining 30 ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped mint, chopped basil, and 30 g grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. If using, add chili flakes.
Gradually whisk in reserved pasta water into the yogurt sauce until desired creamy consistency is reached.
Add drained pasta to a large serving bowl. Add roasted cherry tomatoes, grilled watermelon cubes, and the yogurt sauce. Toss gently to combine.
Divide pasta among four plates. Garnish each serving with remaining grated Parmesan cheese and a few fresh mint or basil leaves. Serve immediately.
