notes: Ensure watermelon is ripe but firm enough to hold its shape after grilling.
The yogurt sauce is best served immediately as it can thicken over time.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Garlic Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast, cut into thick diagonal slices, rests elegantly on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken boasts a golden-brown sear, revealing a juicy, tender interior. A rich, creamy garlic mushroom sauce pools generously around the chicken and lightly coats the top. Thick slices of sautéed cremini mushrooms are nestled beside and partially beneath the chicken. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green against the creamy sauce and earthy mushrooms. The plate is positioned on a clean, light-toned wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm, appetizing colors in a professional, approachable restaurant style.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil and half the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board. Tent with foil.
Add remaining butter to the same skillet. Add diced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently 3-5 minutes until sauce reaches desired consistency.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick diagonal medallions. Do not fan out slices.
Return chicken medallions to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Warm through 1-2 minutes.
Stir in half of the fresh parsley. Taste sauce. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mahshi Bathenjan (Stuffed Eggplant with Savory Rice)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two halved Mahshi Bathenjan (stuffed eggplants) on a clean white porcelain plate, arranged slightly offset. Each eggplant half displays its deep purple skin, contrasting with the golden-brown, savory rice and ground meat filling. The filling is moist, plump, and studded with finely chopped herbs and tomato. A vibrant, rich red tomato-lemon sauce generously pools around the eggplants, coating the tops. The eggplant flesh appears tender. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley or mint garnishes the top. The setting is a modern bistro: simple wooden table, white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting defines textures. The background is minimally blurred. A small white bowl of plain yogurt and warm pita bread are subtly placed nearby, honoring cultural serving traditions. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a single, refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain yogurt
Serve with warm pita bread
Serve with a simple cucumber and tomato salad
instructions: Cut eggplants lengthwise. Scoop out flesh, leaving 1 cm shell. Chop scooped flesh. Sprinkle eggplant shells with salt. Let sit 30 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced onion until translucent. Add ground meat. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.

Add chopped eggplant flesh to pan. Cook 5 minutes. Stir in rice, grated tomatoes, tomato paste, minced garlic, parsley, mint, allspice, cinnamon, and black pepper. Season with salt. Mix well. Cook 2 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Stuff eggplant shells firmly with rice mixture. Do not overstuff.
Arrange stuffed eggplants in a large pot or deep baking dish. They should fit snugly.
In a bowl, whisk hot water or broth with remaining tomato paste, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and salt. Pour sauce over eggplants. Sauce should reach halfway up the eggplants.
Cover pot tightly. Simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes, or bake in oven until rice is tender and eggplant is soft. Check internal temperature of meat if using.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh mint or parsley.
notes: Do not overstuff eggplants, as rice expands during cooking.
Adjust seasoning of stuffing and sauce to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Baked Pasta Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Cheesy Baked Pasta Crostini is presented on a rustic, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Two to three pieces of golden-brown toasted baguette serve as the base, each generously topped with a warm, chunky mixture of small pasta, diced red bell pepper, and tomato. The melted mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese form a bubbly, slightly browned crust over the topping, clinging to the pasta and vegetables. Freshly torn vibrant green basil leaves are casually scattered over the crostini, providing a fresh contrast to the rich red and orange tones of the baked pasta. A simple, everyday fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A casually folded, off-white cloth napkin rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, evoking a relaxed, lived-in family dining area. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the food, emphasizing its homely and comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side for individual preference.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar as an accompaniment.
Pair with a light, crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease an oven-safe dish.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, breaking up tomatoes.
Add cooked pasta to the pan. Stir to combine. Season with salt and black pepper.
Transfer pasta mixture to the prepared oven-safe dish. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella and grated Parmesan over the top.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and edges are lightly golden.
While pasta bakes, slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Toast slices in a toaster or under the grill until golden brown and crisp.
Spoon warm cheesy pasta mixture generously onto toasted bread slices. Garnish with fresh torn basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Any small pasta shape works well for this recipe, such as ditalini, small shells, or elbow macaroni.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mediterranean Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of penne pasta forms the base, tossed in a vibrant, glossy sauce. The pasta is coated with a rich, reddish-orange hue from the sun-dried tomatoes and broth, interspersed with deep green olive halves and pale green artichoke quarters. Freshly chopped green oregano and parsley flecks are visible throughout, adding contrasting color. Thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are nestled on top of the pasta, showing a crisp exterior and moist interior. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The colors are natural and appealing. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad as an appetizer.
Pair with a dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain. Reserve 125ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits. Cook 2 minutes until reduced.
Add chicken broth, sun-dried tomatoes, artichoke hearts, and olives to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes.
Stir in chopped oregano.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency.
Stir in butter until melted and sauce emulsifies.
Slice chicken breasts into thick chunks.
Divide pasta among 4 plates. Top each with sliced chicken.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to taste for desired heat.
Fresh oregano is preferred for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Pasta with Artichoke, Sun-Dried Tomato, and Olive
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of al dente fusilli pasta is mounded centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pasta is generously coated in a rich, savory sauce, showcasing the vibrant colors of its key ingredients. Prominent are rustic, roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes, deep purple-black Kalamata olives halved lengthwise, and tender quartered artichoke hearts, all glistening with olive oil. The sauce has a moderate consistency, clinging well to the pasta strands. A generous scattering of fresh, bright green oregano leaves provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness on top. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The dish is presented on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, creating soft shadows. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chili flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in drained, roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes, quartered artichoke hearts, and halved olives. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Add cooked pasta to the pan. Toss well to coat. Add reserved pasta water gradually to achieve desired sauce consistency.
Stir in fresh chopped oregano. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves and a drizzle of olive oil.
notes: For an added layer of flavor, a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese can be added at serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Beef & Vegetable Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, centrally placed on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. The base of the bowl holds a generous portion of fluffy, white short-grain rice, subtly interspersed with soft, diced red tomatoes, offering a hint of color and gentle texture. On one side of the rice, rich, savory beef chunks, seared to a deep brown and glistening from their sauce, are neatly arranged with translucent, tender slices of caramelized onion. Opposite the beef, vibrant green broccoli florets and bright orange carrot batons are artfully separated, maintaining their distinct colors and firm-tender textures from blanching. A contrasting deep red Gochujang sauce is drizzled sparingly over the beef and vegetables, creating dynamic lines without overwhelming the ingredients. The entire bowl is finished with a generous sprinkle of golden toasted sesame seeds and thin slices of bright green onion, adding both visual appeal and aromatic freshness. The composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing each ingredient clearly. A pair of dark metal chopsticks rests beside the bowl, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin. The setting is clean, modern bistro-style with natural, even lighting from above, highlighting the food's natural colors and textures against a softly blurred, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with kimchi on the side.
Offer extra Gochujang for individual preference.
Serve with a small bowl of clear broth.
Eat with chopsticks and a spoon.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into 5 cm thin batons

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame oil
ingredients.quantity: 30 ml (divided: 15 ml for marinade, 15 ml for vegetables/finish)

instructions: Prepare Beef Marinade: In a large bowl, combine 15 ml sesame oil, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Add beef chunks. Toss to coat. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

Cook Rice: Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed rice, 600 ml water, and diced tomatoes. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Vegetables: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon. Immediately plunge into an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Repeat blanching for carrot batons for 2 minutes. Drain and cool. In a bowl, toss blanched broccoli and carrots with 10 ml sesame oil and a pinch of salt.

Cook Beef & Onions: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add sliced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Push onions to one side. Add marinated beef chunks in a single layer. Sear beef for 3-4 minutes per side until browned. Stir beef and onions together. Cook until beef is cooked through and sauce has slightly thickened.
Prepare Gochujang Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk Gochujang with remaining 5 ml sesame oil and 15 ml hot water (or a bit more, to desired consistency).

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked rice evenly among 4 deep serving bowls. Arrange beef and onion mixture on one side of the rice. Neatly arrange blanched broccoli florets and carrot batons on the other side. Drizzle Gochujang sauce over the beef and vegetables. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.
notes: Adjust Gochujang amount to your preferred spice level.
For an extra touch, a fried egg can be added on top of each bowl.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Street Corn and Black Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mexican Street Corn and Black Bean Salad is artfully arranged on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Charred yellow corn kernels are interspersed with dark black beans, vibrant green diced avocado, finely diced red onion, and thin slices of red chili. Fresh, chopped cilantro is generously sprinkled throughout, adding bright green contrast. The ingredients are lightly coated in a creamy, tangy smoked paprika-lime dressing, ensuring each component is visible and well-integrated. Textures range from charred corn to creamy avocado and crisp onion. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a colorful Mexican textile napkin and lime wedge. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients, creating an inviting, authentic casual dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas or tortilla chips for scooping.
Offer extra lime wedges on the side for added zest.

ingredients.name: Black beans
ingredients.quantity: 2 x 400 g cans, rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: Jalapeño or serrano chili
ingredients.quantity: 1-2, deseeded and thinly sliced (adjust to taste)

instructions: If using fresh corn, char kernels on a hot skillet or grill until slightly browned. If using frozen, cook according to package directions and cool.
In a large bowl, combine charred corn, rinsed black beans, diced avocado, finely diced red onion, and sliced chili.
For the dressing, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, beer, smoked paprika, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Add chopped fresh cilantro.
Gently toss all ingredients until well combined and coated with the dressing.
Serve immediately, or chill for 15 minutes for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Cheddar Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Creamy Chicken and Cheddar Bake sits on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The dish fills the plate adequately, showcasing golden-brown melted cheddar cheese bubbling over tender, cubed chicken pieces and vibrant green broccoli florets. The creamy, rich sauce peeks through, coating the ingredients. The chicken cubes are seared with slight browning, contrasting with the soft, cooked broccoli. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, homely family kitchen. Simple, everyday flatware is casually placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting appeal of the dish. A casually placed cloth napkin adds to the relaxed, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad or crusty bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat a large oven-safe skillet or pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Chicken does not need to be cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Once melted, add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the onion and garlic. Stir for 1 minute to cook the raw flour taste.
Gradually whisk in the milk, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens and is smooth.
Remove from heat. Stir in 150g of grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season the cheese sauce with salt, pepper, and dried thyme.
Add the seared chicken cubes and broccoli florets to the cheese sauce in the skillet. Stir to combine.
Smooth the mixture in the skillet. Sprinkle remaining 50g cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown and melted. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: This dish is versatile; feel feel to add other vegetables like peas or corn.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Chorizo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow steel pan holds a vibrant bed of golden-hued rice. The rice is studded with thick chunks of dark red chorizo and small orange carrot dice. Four whole bone-in chicken thighs, skin seared to a deep mahogany brown, are nestled into the rice, spaced evenly around the pan. Small pools of reddish oil from the sausage glisten on the surface. Bright green parsley sprigs are scattered across the top. The scene is set on a rustic wooden table with a white linen napkin and a small bowl of olives. Natural light highlights the crispy chicken skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lemon wedges for acidity
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Serve directly from the cooking pan in the center of the table

ingredients.name: Chorizo sausage, cut into thick chunks

instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add chorizo chunks and carrots to the same pan. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until the liquid evaporates and the mixture darkens.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in hot chicken stock and smoked paprika. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the rice, skin-side up.
Simmer undisturbed for 18 minutes until rice is tender and chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a cloth and rest for 5 minutes.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C
Use a wide pan to ensure even cooking of the rice layer

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin lightly crisp, rests on a rustic white ceramic plate. Alongside, a generous serving of tender, golden-brown potato wedges, their exteriors slightly caramelized. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are naturally scattered over the chicken and potatoes, adding vibrant green accents. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits nearby. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The plate is positioned on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded blue and white checkered cloth napkin and simple silver cutlery are placed beside it. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, homely family meal. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking sheet for family-style meals.
Pair with a simple green salad or steamed seasonal vegetables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Mince garlic cloves. Finely chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper to the bowl with potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange potato wedges in a single layer on one half of the prepared baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the other half of the baking sheet alongside the potatoes.
Slice the lemon into thin rounds. Place a few lemon rounds on top of and around the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender and browned. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra crispiness, broil chicken for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Southwestern Spicy Black Bean and Corn Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Southwestern Spicy Black Bean and Corn Rice Skillet is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features fluffy, reddish-orange rice, generously mixed with dark, glossy black beans, bright yellow corn kernels, and visible flecks of red bell pepper and green cilantro. The onion, bell pepper, and jalapeño are diced. The texture is hearty and comforting. A few sprigs of fresh cilantro are casually scattered on top, and a bright green lime wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The background is a warm, cozy family kitchen setting, with soft, natural lighting from above. Everyday stainless steel flatware is placed beside the bowl. The overall scene is homely and inviting, showcasing a satisfying, naturally portioned meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a dollop of sour cream or a sprinkle of shredded cheese as optional toppings.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, diced red bell pepper, and minced jalapeño. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add ground cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked long-grain rice until coated.
Pour in vegetable broth and undrained diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in rinsed black beans and frozen corn kernels. Cook uncovered for 5 minutes, or until heated through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh chopped cilantro.
Serve hot with lime wedges.
notes: For extra spice, leave some seeds in the jalapeño or add a pinch of cayenne pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hearty Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented on a rustic, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The dish features fluffy, reddish-orange long-grain rice infused with tomato, interspersed with whole dark black beans, bright yellow corn kernels, and tender, browned 2 cm chicken cubes. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro is scattered over the top. The components are naturally piled in the center of the plate, allowing some of the grains, beans, and corn to spill slightly, creating an inviting, unpretentious appearance. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table with visible grain. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside the plate. A lime wedge is positioned nearby, ready for squeezing. The scene is lit with warm, soft light, evoking a cozy family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer extra lime wedges and a small bowl of your favorite salsa or a simple pico de gallo for diners to add.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and minced jalapeño. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed rice to the skillet. Stir and toast for 2-3 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir in diced tomatoes, black beans, corn, chicken broth, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove skillet from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: This dish is excellent for meal prep and reheats well.
Adjust jalapeño quantity for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Agnolotti del Plin with Goat Cheese & Balsamic, Cherry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an expensive bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim, resting on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. The lighting is dramatic and professional, casting soft shadows that enhance depth. A single individual portion of approximately 10-12 golden-hued Agnolotti del Plin, small pinched parcels with a delicate, silken texture, are arranged in an organic, flowing composition across the plate, leaving abundant negative space. The Agnolotti are coated in a glistening brown butter sauce, showcasing their tender, plump forms. A precise, controlled drizzle of vibrant, ruby-red cherry gastrique, with its viscous sheen, artfully sweeps across the plate, creating intentional contrast against the pasta. Three to four perfectly crispy, deep-green sage leaves are thoughtfully placed among the agnolotti, adding a textural element and a pop of color. Delicate, translucent shavings of aged Parmesan cheese are scattered gracefully over the dish, catching the light. The overall presentation is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the exquisite execution and premium quality of each element. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant European flatware are positioned beside the plate, creating a sophisticated, uncluttered scene that highlights the culinary mastery and refined elegance of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a 'primo piatto' (first course) in a multi-course Italian meal.
Accompany with a glass of light-bodied red wine, such as a Pinot Noir or a Barbera.
instructions: Prepare Pasta Dough: On a clean surface, combine '00' flour and semolina. Form a well in the center. Add whole eggs and egg yolks to the well. Gradually incorporate flour into eggs with a fork. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in plastic. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Prepare Filling: In a bowl, combine goat cheese, ricotta, grated Parmesan, balsamic glaze, salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix until well combined and smooth.
Roll Pasta: Divide dough into four portions. Working with one portion at a time, pass dough through a pasta machine, gradually decreasing thickness until setting 6 (thin but not translucent).

Form Agnolotti: Lay pasta sheet on a lightly floured surface. Place small teaspoonfuls of filling along one edge, spaced about 2 cm apart. Fold the pasta sheet over the filling to create a long roll. Gently press around each filling mound to seal. Using a fluted pasta wheel or knife, cut between mounds to form individual agnolotti. Pinch the top edge of each agnolotti to create the traditional 'plin' (pinch). Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

Prepare Cherry Gastrique: In a small saucepan, combine pitted cherries, aged balsamic vinegar, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cherries are softened and sauce thickens to a syrupy consistency. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Keep gastrique warm.
Cook Agnolotti: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully add agnolotti. Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until they float and are tender. Do not overcook.

Prepare Brown Butter Sauce: While pasta cooks, melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook, swirling occasionally, until butter turns a golden brown and smells nutty. Add sage leaves to crisp for 30 seconds. Remove sage leaves. Keep butter warm.

Plate Dish: Using a slotted spoon, transfer cooked agnolotti directly into the brown butter sauce. Gently toss to coat. Arrange 10-12 agnolotti per plate in an organic, flowing composition. Drizzle cherry gastrique artistically around and over the agnolotti. Garnish with crispy sage leaves. Shave fresh Parmesan over the dish using a vegetable peeler. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Cherry-Balsamic Gastrique and Goat Cheese Crémeux
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on an elegant, matte white modern designer plate with a subtle, organic texture, resting on a premium grey veined marble surface. The duck breast, cut into two thick medallions, showcases a perfectly rendered, golden-crisp skin and a vibrant, medium-rare pink interior. Adjacent to the duck, a delicate quenelle of creamy, off-white goat cheese crémeux provides a soft contrast. A rich, glossy, deep ruby-red cherry-balsamic gastrique is artfully drizzled across the plate, connecting the elements with fluid lines. A few fresh, halved cherries are precisely placed near the duck, their bright red contrasting with the dish. A tiny, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme adds a final, precise touch of color and freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the dish, emphasizing the architectural precision of the composition. The setting is ultra-minimalist, featuring only a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle and elegant silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and rich colors of the dish.
instructions: Score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Pour off excess fat.

Flip duck breasts. Sear meat-side down for 3-4 minutes. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 60°C (140°F) for medium-rare. Rest duck breasts on a cutting board for 10 minutes before slicing.

For the Cherry-Balsamic Gastrique: While duck rests, drain most of the rendered duck fat from the pan, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add pitted cherries to the pan. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.

Deglaze the pan with balsamic vinegar. Add sugar. Bring to a simmer and reduce over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until the sauce is syrupy and coats the back of a spoon. Stir in 10g unsalted butter until melted and glossy. Season with a pinch of salt. Remove from heat.
For the Goat Cheese Crémeux: In a small bowl, combine soft goat cheese, heavy cream, and a pinch of salt. Whisk vigorously or use a small food processor until smooth and light. Adjust seasoning.

To plate: Slice each rested duck breast into thick medallions. Arrange 2-3 duck medallions artfully on one side of a large, minimalist plate. Create a delicate quenelle or smear of goat cheese crémeux on the plate. Drizzle the glossy cherry-balsamic gastrique organically around the duck and crémeux. Garnish with a few fresh cherry halves and a tiny sprig of fresh thyme.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Pork and Potato Broth with Sourdough Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, rustic soup presented in a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic bowl on a light reclaimed wood surface. The rich, earthy brown broth holds tender, slow-cooked pork chunks (2 cm) and soft, pale fermented potato cubes (1 cm). A few crisp, golden sourdough croutons (2 cm cubes) float on the surface, offering textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green herbs, like finely chopped parsley or chives, are sparingly sprinkled, adding a natural pop of color. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space around the bowl, emphasizing the soup's wholesome, ingredient-focused nature. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its warm tones and inviting textures. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige subtly grounds the scene, with a hint of a green plant in the clean, uncluttered background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra crusty sourdough bread for dipping.
instructions: Prepare broth ingredients. Wash carrots and celery. Keep peels and ends. Roughly chop onion, carrots, celery, and garlic. Reserve pork shoulder.
Combine pork shoulder, chopped onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, and 2.5 litres water in a large pot. Bring to a simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 2 hours.
Meanwhile, prepare fermented potatoes. Wash potatoes. Peel half the potatoes; keep peels for the broth if desired. Cut peeled potatoes into 1 cm cubes.
Make brine: Dissolve 20g sea salt in 500ml non-chlorinated water.
Place potato cubes in a clean jar. Pour brine over potatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily to release gas.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Remove pork shoulder; shred or cut into 2 cm chunks. Set aside.
Return strained broth to a clean pot. Add remaining whole potatoes (if any) cut into 2 cm cubes. Simmer until tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain fermented potato cubes. Add cooked pork chunks and fermented potato cubes to the soup. Heat through gently.
Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
For sourdough croutons: Cut stale sourdough bread into 2 cm cubes. Toss with olive oil. Toast in a pan over medium heat or in an oven until golden and crisp.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives and toasted sourdough croutons. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure proper air release (burping) during potato fermentation to prevent pressure buildup.
Use seasonal and locally sourced ingredients for best flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Adobo with Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Adobo is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing the dish's rich, savory appeal. Two pieces of braised chicken thigh, with a deep brown, slightly glazed skin, are nestled beside substantial chunks of tender, golden-brown potato. Both are generously coated in a dark, glossy, reduced adobo sauce. The sauce appears thick and clings well to the ingredients. A mound of fluffy white garlic rice, subtly flecked with golden-brown fried garlic bits, is served neatly alongside the main dish, either directly on the plate or in a small, traditional white ceramic rice bowl. The plate is garnished with thin slices of vibrant red bird's eye chili and finely chopped bright green spring onions, adding color and freshness. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a minimal, blurred restaurant-style background, creating an inviting and authentic casual dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra plain or garlic rice.
Offer a side of fresh sliced tomatoes and red onions.
instructions: Rinse chicken thighs. Pat dry.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Do not brown garlic.
Return seared chicken to the pan.
Pour in vinegar. Let it simmer uncovered for 2 minutes without stirring.
Add soy sauce, water, whole black peppercorns, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add potato chunks to the pot. Stir gently.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and potatoes are tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium-high. Simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce to a glossy consistency.

While adobo simmers, prepare garlic rice: Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. While rice cooks, sauté 2-3 cloves of minced garlic in a small amount of oil until golden. Stir into cooked rice.
Serve adobo hot with garlic rice. Garnish with sliced fresh chilies and chopped spring onions, if desired.
notes: The balance of sour, salty, and savory is key to authentic Adobo flavor.
The vinegar's harshness dissipates during simmering, leaving a complex tang.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Fillet, Forest Mushroom, Beer Jus, Pea
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a pristine, oversized white bone china plate with generous negative space. The focal point is a perfectly seared pork fillet, cut into two thick, tender medallions with a caramelized crust and a hint of pink interior, placed off-center. Adjacent to the pork, a smooth, earthy forest mushroom purée forms a delicate, organic swoosh. A rich, glossy, dark amber beer jus pools elegantly beside the pork, reflecting light. A vibrant, silky green pea emulsion is artfully placed as a small, vivid dot, offering a striking color contrast. Three to four plump, jewel-like confit cherry tomatoes, softened and slightly burst, are meticulously arranged, adding a pop of red and a touch of sweetness. The dish is garnished with a few delicate, bright green pea shoots, providing a final touch of freshness and height. The composition is asymmetrical and natural, emphasizing the quality of ingredients and precision of technique. The plate rests on a polished dark wood table or a white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, directional lighting that creates soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, sits nearby. The overall impression is one of sophisticated simplicity and culinary artistry.

ingredients.name: Dark beer (e.g., stout or dark ale)

instructions: Prepare Pork Fillet: Trim pork fillet. Season with salt and pepper. Sear pork in a hot pan with 15 ml olive oil until golden brown on all sides. Transfer to a baking tray. Roast in a preheated oven at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Rest pork for 5 minutes. Cut into thick medallions.

Make Mushroom Purée: Finely dice 1 shallot and 1 garlic clove. Slice mushrooms. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced shallot and garlic until fragrant. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until tender and liquid evaporates. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a blender. Add 30g butter. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.

Prepare Beer Jus: Finely dice remaining 1 shallot and 2 garlic cloves. In a saucepan, sauté diced shallot and garlic in 15 ml olive oil until softened. Deglaze with dark beer. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock and 1 thyme sprig. Bring to a simmer. Reduce until sauce coats the back of a spoon. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Whisk in 30g cold butter until glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Confit Cherry Tomatoes: Place cherry tomatoes in a small oven-safe dish. Add 20 ml olive oil, 1 crushed garlic clove, and 2 thyme sprigs. Season lightly with salt. Roast in the same 180°C oven for 15-20 minutes until tomatoes are tender and slightly burst. Set aside.

Create Pea Emulsion: Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch green peas for 2 minutes until bright green and tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Blend peas with 40g butter and a splash of the pea blanching water (1-2 tablespoons) until very smooth. Season with salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture. Keep warm.

Assemble Dish: On a warm, minimalist plate, create a subtle sweep or dot of mushroom purée. Place 2-3 thick pork medallions artfully beside it. Spoon a small pool or drizzle of the beer jus beside the pork. Add a vibrant dot or small streak of pea emulsion. Arrange 3-4 confit cherry tomatoes elegantly around the components. Garnish with a few delicate pea shoots or microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure all components are prepared and kept warm for seamless plating.

For precise pork cooking, a meat thermometer is essential. An internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for whole cuts of pork followed by resting is considered safe and yields a tender, slightly pink interior. This temperature will rise to 65-68°C during resting.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Lemon-Cherry Upside-Down Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Sustainable Lemon-Cherry Upside-Down Cake is presented on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate. The top of the cake, now the base, showcases a rich, glossy brown caramel layer with vibrant, deep red whole pitted cherries and thin, translucent half-moon apple slices embedded within, their natural imperfections adding character. The cake itself is a light golden-brown, revealing a tender, moist crumb. A few delicate curls of fresh lemon zest are placed artfully on the plate beside the cake. The overall composition is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing the natural beauty of the ingredients. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed to the side. In the soft, natural light, the whole inverted cake, still on its rustic wooden stand, is visible in the slightly blurred background, completing the eco-conscious and unpretentious aesthetic. Simple, elegant French flatware, perhaps a vintage fork, rests on the napkin, complementing the understated setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve simply, perhaps with a cup of black coffee or herbal tea.
Enjoy as a light dessert or afternoon treat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 20 cm round cake pan.
Pit cherries. Slice apple thinly into half-moon shapes. Keep skins on apple for zero-waste.
Make brown sugar caramel: Melt 50 g butter and 50 g brown sugar in a small saucepan with 30 ml water over medium heat. Cook until dissolved and slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Pour caramel into the prepared cake pan. Arrange pitted cherries and apple slices decoratively over the caramel.
Prepare cake batter: Cream remaining 70 g butter and 100 g brown sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well.
Zest the entire lemon into the batter. Squeeze 15 ml lemon juice and add to batter.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Mix until just combined.
Pour cake batter gently over the fruit in the pan. Smooth top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack or serving plate. Let cool completely.
notes: This recipe emphasizes using the whole lemon and seasonal fruits to reduce waste.
Compost any fruit scraps or peels not used.
Adjust fruits based on seasonal availability in your region.

recipes.recipe_name: Foie Gras Torchon, Cherry-Balsamic Gelee, Brioche Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate holds a minimalist composition. A thick, creamy beige medallion of perfectly chilled foie gras torchon sits slightly off-center. Adjacent to it, a precisely cut 3cm square of deep ruby-red cherry-balsamic gelee provides a striking color contrast and elegant sheen. A single, golden-brown, thin rectangular brioche crisp stands artfully leaned against the foie gras, offering a textural counterpoint. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their precision and quality. A delicate sprinkle of flaky sea salt glistens atop the foie gras. The plate is presented on a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and polished silver flatware, under dramatic, focused lighting creating soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Foie Gras Torchon: Season de-veined foie gras with 2g salt and 1g black pepper. Roll tightly in plastic wrap to form a cylinder. Poach in 70°C water bath for 20 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Chill completely under pressure for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight.

Prepare Cherry-Balsamic Gelee: Pit cherries. Blend cherries to a smooth puree. Strain puree through a fine-mesh sieve to yield about 50ml cherry juice. In a small saucepan, combine balsamic vinegar, cherry juice, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half until slightly syrupy. Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water. Squeeze out excess water. Whisk bloomed gelatin into warm balsamic-cherry reduction until dissolved. Pour gelee mixture into a shallow, flat dish to a thickness of 3mm. Chill until firm, about 2 hours.

Prepare Brioche Crisps: Preheat oven to 160°C. Thinly slice brioche into 2mm thick slices. Cut slices into 3cm x 6cm rectangles. Arrange on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely.
Assemble: Carefully unwrap chilled foie gras torchon. Using a hot, dry knife, slice the torchon into four 2cm thick medallions. Cut the firm cherry-balsamic gelee into four 3cm x 3cm squares.

Plate: On each cold plate, place one foie gras medallion slightly off-center. Position one gelee square next to the foie gras. Lean one brioche crisp against the foie gras. Finish with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt over the foie gras.
notes: Use highest quality foie gras and aged balsamic vinegar for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Puttanesca Vegetariana con Mozzarella e Parmigiano
recipes.visual_description: The Puttanesca Vegetariana is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous individual portion of spaghetti twirled into a refined, yet inviting mound. The pasta is richly coated in a deep red, rustic tomato sauce. Scattered throughout are halved Kalamata olives, their dark purple contrasting with small, melting cubes of fresh mozzarella, adding creamy white accents. A light, even dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano covers the dish, lending a subtle golden warmth. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, providing a burst of color and aromatic freshness. The dish exhibits moderate negative space, highlighting its comforting textures and natural, organic arrangement. It rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware. A small bowl of extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano sits nearby, completing the authentic, casual bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Stir in red pepper flakes and dried oregano. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Add pitted Kalamata olives and drained capers. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes. Sauce should thicken slightly.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water.
Drain spaghetti. Add spaghetti to the sauce.
Toss to coat the spaghetti evenly.
Add cubed fresh mozzarella. Toss gently until mozzarella begins to melt.
Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Toss to combine.
Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The sauce benefits from using high-quality canned tomatoes.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Sourdough Apple-Cherry Cake with Lemon Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous slice of Sourdough Apple-Cherry Cake is presented on a round, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm cream hue. The cake slice, with its golden-brown crust, reveals a moist, tender crumb speckled with diced apple pieces and delicate swirls of dark red cherry compote. A thin, smooth white lemon glaze is artfully drizzled over the top, creating subtle, organic lines. The presentation is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space on the plate, emphasizing the cake's natural textures and colors. The plate rests on a light-toned, natural wood surface, possibly reclaimed, showcasing its subtle grain. A folded, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is uncluttered, featuring a hint of greenery from a potted herb, maintaining an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake tin.
Make Cherry Compote: Combine pitted cherries, 20g brown sugar, and 30ml water in a small saucepan. Simmer 8-10 minutes until cherries soften and liquid thickens. Cool completely.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a large bowl, combine sourdough discard, remaining 130g brown sugar, eggs, and oil. Whisk until smooth.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Grate lemon zest from the lemon. Dice apples into 1cm cubes. Fold lemon zest and diced apples into the batter.
Pour half of the batter into the prepared tin. Spoon dollops of cooled cherry compote over the batter.
Cover with remaining batter. Gently spread to even top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Make Lemon Glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar with 2-3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice until smooth and pourable.
Drizzle glaze over cooled cake before serving.
notes: To minimize waste, apple peels and cores can be used to make apple scrap vinegar or a simple apple tea.
Lemon peels can be candied or used to infuse water, then composted.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Saffron Risotto, Roasted Garlic Emulsion, Tomato Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cut into two thick, tender pieces, forms the elegant centerpiece on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, delicate pattern. The chicken, with its perfectly crisp, golden-brown skin, is artfully positioned atop a flowing, vibrant saffron risotto, which cascades naturally across a portion of the plate, showcasing its creamy, al dente texture and rich yellow hue. Around the chicken and risotto, precisely placed roasted cherry tomato halves glisten, their deep red contrasting with the dish's golden tones. A delicate drizzle of creamy roasted garlic emulsion creates an abstract pattern, adding a subtle touch of elegance. A clear, glistening pool of vibrant tomato consommé occupies a section of the abundant negative space, reflecting the ambient light. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are meticulously placed as the sole garnish, providing a precise pop of color and freshness. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and minimalist silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity against an ultra-minimalist background, emphasizing the premium quality and masterful execution.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

Prepare Roasted Garlic Emulsion: Cut tops off garlic heads. Drizzle with 10ml olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast 45 minutes until soft. Squeeze out pulp. Blend with 50ml hot chicken stock until smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Tomato Consommé: Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 10ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 20 minutes until softened. Blend roasted tomatoes. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to extract clear liquid. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Saffron Risotto: In a saucepan, heat 10ml olive oil and 20g butter over medium heat. Sauté diced shallot and minced garlic until translucent, 3 minutes. Add Arborio rice. Toast 2 minutes. Pour in white wine. Cook until absorbed. Add saffron threads. Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for stock to absorb before adding more. Continue 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente. Stir in 30g butter and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid.

Prepare Pan-Seared Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season skin with salt and pepper. Heat 20ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake 10-12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes.

To Plate: Spoon a fluid, artistic smear of saffron risotto onto the center of each plate. Slice each chicken breast in half lengthwise, on an angle. Place chicken pieces artfully on the risotto. Arrange a few roasted cherry tomato halves around the chicken. Drizzle roasted garlic emulsion around the plate. Pour a small amount of clear tomato consommé into the negative space. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkish Summer Fruit Medley
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Turkish Summer Fruit Medley is presented in a shallow, white porcelain dessert bowl, placed on a light wooden table surface. The fruits are precisely prepared: figs are quartered, red grapes halved, orange segmented into neat pieces, and apricots quartered. The ruby-red pomegranate arils are generously scattered throughout. The composition is natural and flowing, showcasing the rich colors of deep red figs, purple grapes, bright orange segments, and ruby pomegranate arils. A light, glistening rosewater-agave dressing coats the fruit. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of emerald green chopped pistachios and delicate bright green mint chiffonade, offering textural contrast and aromatic freshness. A folded off-white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the freshness. The background suggests a clean, modern bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in small individual bowls, common for desserts.
Offer a side of Turkish tea or coffee.
Can be served after a main meal or as a light breakfast.
instructions: Prepare fruits: Quarter figs. Halve grapes. Segment orange, remove pith. Extract pomegranate arils. Quarter apricots.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together agave nectar, lemon juice, rosewater, orange blossom water, and cinnamon.
Combine: Gently combine figs, grapes, orange segments, apricots, and most pomegranate arils in a large bowl.
Dress: Pour dressing over fruit. Gently toss to coat.
Chill: Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve: Spoon chilled fruit medley into individual serving bowls. Garnish with remaining pomegranate arils, fresh mint chiffonade, and chopped pistachios.
notes: Adjust sweetness of dressing to fruit ripeness.
Chill thoroughly for best flavor.
Ensure all fruits are ripe and fresh for optimal taste and texture.
traditional_techniques: Use of rosewater and orange blossom water

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Caramelized Shallot Purée, Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, its skin a rich golden-brown, rests prominently on a pristine bone china plate. Beside it, a sinuous, flowing sweep of glossy, deep amber caramelized shallot purée creates an elegant backdrop. A small, artful cluster of vibrant red slow-roasted cherry tomatoes, slightly collapsed and glistening with oil, nestles near the chicken. Delicate, golden-crisp pancetta shards are scattered sparingly over the tomatoes and the chicken, adding textural contrast. A few drops of bright green garlic-oregano oil are precisely dotted around the composition, enhancing color and aroma. The plating emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the sophisticated simplicity and precise execution of each element. The dish is presented on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle shadows, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in the background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Preheat oven to 150°C. Place cherry tomatoes in a small baking dish. Add 2 cloves of garlic, lightly crushed. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil, a pinch of sugar, and salt. Roast for 45-50 minutes until blistered and slightly collapsed. Set aside.

Peel and thinly slice shallots. In a small saucepan, melt 15g butter with 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium-low heat. Add shallots. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very tender. Add 50ml chicken stock. Simmer until stock reduces. Transfer to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Cut pancetta into small irregular pieces. Render pancetta in a cold pan over medium heat until golden and crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Reserve rendered fat.
Finely chop remaining 2 garlic cloves. Finely chop fresh oregano leaves. In a small bowl, combine 3 tablespoons olive oil, chopped garlic, and chopped oregano. Season with a pinch of salt.

Heat 1 tablespoon reserved pancetta fat and 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts, skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Add remaining 15g butter to the pan. Baste chicken with butter. Transfer skillet to the preheated 150°C oven. Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

To plate, spoon a generous swirl of caramelized shallot purée onto one side of each plate. Place one whole chicken breast, skin-side up, next to the purée. Arrange a cluster of slow-roasted cherry tomatoes beside the chicken. Scatter crispy pancetta over the tomatoes and around the chicken. Drizzle the garlic-oregano oil over the chicken and tomatoes. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chai Spiced Chocolate Brownies
recipes.visual_description: Four generous squares of rich, dark brown chai spiced chocolate brownies are casually arranged on a cream-colored, everyday ceramic plate. The brownies have a slightly cracked, glossy top and a dense, fudgy interior visible on the cut edges. A few whole chai spices, such as star anise pods and cardamom pods, are loosely scattered on the wooden table next to the plate. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casually folded, light brown cloth napkin is placed nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, homely atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the brownies.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
Gently heat milk in a small saucepan. Add chai tea bags. Steep for 5 minutes. Remove tea bags.
Melt chocolate and butter in a heatproof bowl over a simmering pot of water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate large bowl, whisk eggs and sugar until pale and fluffy.
Pour melted chocolate mixture into egg mixture. Stir well.
Sift flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt into the wet mixture. Fold gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Stir in the steeped chai milk and vanilla extract.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. A toothpick inserted should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter. Do not overbake.
Let cool completely in the pan before cutting into squares.
notes: For fudgier brownies, do not overbake. They will set more as they cool.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, is the focal point on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a generous pile of roasted potato chunks, each piece a warm golden hue with a slightly caramelized exterior. The potatoes are irregularly shaped 3cm chunks, showing their rustic preparation. Both chicken and potatoes are lightly dusted with finely chopped fresh green parsley, adding a vibrant color contrast. A small, bright yellow lemon wedge sits subtly near the chicken. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and warm colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple Greek salad.
Offer warm pita bread for dipping in pan juices.
A side of tzatziki sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks.
Mince garlic. Zest one lemon. Juice both lemons.
Finely chop fresh oregano and rosemary.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, minced garlic, lemon zest, chopped oregano, chopped rosemary, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange seasoned potatoes in a single layer in a large roasting pan.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up among the potatoes.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over chicken.
Pour lemon juice and chicken broth into the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Potatoes should be tender and golden.
Halfway through roasting (around 25-30 minutes), baste chicken and potatoes with pan juices.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Quinoa Salad with Avocado
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, clean composition on a light ceramic plate with a natural, unglazed rim. The cooked quinoa forms a loose, organic base, its light tan grains providing a textural counterpoint. Diced bell peppers in vibrant reds, yellows, and oranges are scattered throughout, alongside halved crimson cherry tomatoes and creamy, pale green diced avocado chunks. Thinly sliced red onion adds subtle purple accents. The quick-pickled bell pepper slices, slightly softened and translucent, are artfully distributed, lending a deeper, almost jewel-toned hue. Fresh green parsley leaves are gently tossed in, providing a final pop of color and freshness. A light sheen of vinaigrette coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural luster. The plating avoids any rigid arrangement, embracing a natural, unfussy pile. The plate sits on a light bamboo surface, complemented by a simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, casting gentle shadows that highlight textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery, emphasizing the eco-conscious and ingredient-focused presentation.
instructions: Thinly slice one bell pepper for quick-pickling. In a small saucepan, combine white vinegar, 125ml water, sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until dissolved. Pour hot liquid over sliced bell pepper in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Combine rinsed quinoa and 400ml water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Dice the remaining two bell peppers. Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice avocado. Thinly slice red onion. Chop fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, 2g salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine cooked and cooled quinoa, diced bell peppers, halved cherry tomatoes, diced avocado, sliced red onion, and chopped parsley.
Drain the quick-pickled bell peppers and add them to the salad. Pour vinaigrette over the salad.
Gently toss all ingredients to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Harvest Quinoa Starter
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a round, matte cream ceramic plate, showcasing a minimalistic and natural composition. At the center, a small, neat mound of fluffy, pearlescent white quinoa forms the base. Around it, vibrant, jewel-toned pieces of fermented red, yellow, and orange bell peppers, alongside ruby-red tomato halves, are artfully scattered, their irregular shapes and glossy surfaces adding organic texture. The fermentation process lends a subtle sheen to the vegetables, highlighting their natural colors. A small, creamy dollop of pale green avocado crema sits adjacent to the quinoa, its smooth texture contrasting with the other elements. A delicate drizzle of golden olive oil glistens across the dish. The overall presentation emphasizes natural forms and colors, with ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Small firm tomatoes (e.g., Roma or cherry)

instructions: Wash bell peppers and tomatoes. Cut bell peppers into 1 cm dice. Halve or quarter small tomatoes.
Dissolve 10g sea salt in 500ml filtered water. Stir until fully dissolved.

Place diced bell peppers and tomatoes in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small bag filled with water to keep vegetables below brine. Cover jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily. Store in refrigerator once fermented.

Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water. Combine quinoa with 300ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.
Halve avocados and scoop flesh into a small bowl. Add lime juice and a pinch of salt. Mash with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving some texture.

On each starter plate, place a small mound of cooled quinoa. Artfully arrange a portion of the fermented bell peppers and tomatoes around or beside the quinoa. Dollop a small amount of avocado crema next to the quinoa. Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Garnish sparingly with chopped fresh cilantro or parsley, if using.
notes: This recipe highlights plant-forward ingredients and utilizes fermentation as a sustainable preservation method.
Adjust fermentation time to your preferred level of tanginess. Taste daily after day 3.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken & Corn Pasta Arancini
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, crispy Chicken & Corn Pasta Arancini are presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Each arancino is a uniform sphere, approximately 4-5 cm in diameter. The exterior exhibits a finely textured, golden-brown panko crust. A few arancini are subtly arranged, with one possibly broken open to reveal the creamy pasta, small diced chicken, bright yellow corn kernels, and a hint of melted mozzarella within. The interior shows a soft, cohesive texture. Colors are primarily warm golden tones, complemented by the internal yellow, white, and pink hues. The plate features moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting appeal. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, ensuring the arancini are the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer or snack.
Often accompanied by a simple marinara sauce for dipping.
Can be part of an antipasto platter with other small bites.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside to cool completely.
Dice cooked chicken into small 5 mm cubes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature during initial cooking. Mince onion and garlic. Finely dice cherry tomatoes.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté minced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Add frozen corn kernels to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until heated through. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Transfer mixture to a large bowl.
Add cooled pasta, diced chicken, and grated Parmesan cheese to the bowl with the corn mixture. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Cut fresh mozzarella into 1.5 cm cubes.
Prepare a breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and panko breadcrumbs in a third.

Take about 2 tablespoons of the pasta mixture. Flatten slightly in your palm. Place one mozzarella cube in the center. Carefully form the mixture around the mozzarella, shaping into a compact sphere, about 4-5 cm in diameter.
Roll each sphere first in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, roll thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C. Ensure oil is deep enough to submerge arancini.
Fry arancini in batches, 3-4 at a time, for 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Use a slotted spoon to turn them for even browning. Maintain oil temperature.
Remove fried arancini with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve hot.
notes: Ensure pasta mixture is well-chilled before forming arancini for easier handling.
Do not overcrowd the frying pot to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork Loin with Fermented Garlic-Onion Paste
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked pork loin is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The pork loin is presented as two thick, rustic medallions, showcasing its tender, juicy interior and a light golden-brown exterior. Around the pork, braised root vegetables – large, organic chunks of orange carrots, pale parsnips, and off-white celeriac – are arranged naturally, their softened textures and earthy colors visible. A rich, dark braising liquid pools subtly at the bottom of the plate, lightly coating the vegetables. A small, creamy dollop of fermented garlic-onion paste sits alongside the pork. A few fresh thyme sprigs are scattered for a natural, understated garnish. The plate is set on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its simple, clean composition and natural textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of green foliage.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (carrot tops, onion skins, herb stems)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Garlic-Onion Paste: Mince 50 g garlic and 1 large onion. Combine with 10 g sea salt and 20 ml apple cider vinegar. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar. Ferment at room temperature for 7-10 days. Release gas daily.

Make Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth: Combine 200 g vegetable scraps, 500 ml water, 5 g sea salt, 5 g black peppercorns, 2 bay leaves, and 3 thyme sprigs in a pot. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.

Sear Pork Loin: Preheat oven to 160°C. Season 600 g pork loin with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown. Remove pork.

Braised Root Vegetables: Peel and cut 2 medium carrots, 2 medium parsnips, and 1 small celeriac into large, rustic chunks. Add remaining chopped garlic (50g) and onion (1 large) to the pot. Sauté 2 minutes. Add root vegetable chunks. Sauté 5 minutes.

Braise Pork and Vegetables: Return seared pork loin to the pot with vegetables. Pour in strained vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cover pot. Braise in preheated oven for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until pork is very tender. Internal temperature of pork should reach 75°C.

Rest and Serve: Remove pork loin from pot. Rest 10 minutes. If braising liquid is too thin, reduce it over high heat on stovetop. Slice pork loin into thick medallions. Serve pork with braised root vegetables. Spoon reduced braising liquid over. Add a dollop of fermented garlic-onion paste on the side. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for garlic-onion paste based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
Use seasonal, local root vegetables for best flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Pommery Jus, Bell Pepper Confit, Braised Cipollini
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, minimalist bone china coupe plate, maximizing negative space. A perfectly pan-seared chicken supreme, with crispy, deep golden-brown skin and exposed wing bone, rests off-center. Its flesh appears juicy. Adjacent, a small, organic mound of vibrant red bell pepper confit batons gleams softly. Three glossy, golden-brown braised cipollini onions are artfully placed near the confit. A rich, amber Pommery mustard jus is elegantly spooned onto the plate, forming a flowing, asymmetrical pool complementing elements without overwhelming them. A delicate fresh thyme sprig provides a subtle green accent. The composition is precise and minimalist, emphasizing component quality. The plate sits on a polished dark wood table, casting professional shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, rests beside. The background is clean, ensuring the food is the focal point.

ingredients.name: Chicken Supremes (bone-in, skin-on chicken breast with first wing bone)

instructions: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken supremes skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest 10 minutes on a wire rack.

Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds and membranes. Place skin-side up on a baking sheet. Roast under a hot grill until skin is charred and blistered. Transfer to a bowl, cover with cling film. Let steam 10 minutes. Peel skins. Cut bell pepper flesh into 1.5cm batons. Place batons in a small saucepan. Cover with 85ml olive oil. Add 1 thyme sprig. Gently confit over very low heat for 20 minutes until tender. Season with salt.

Peel cipollini onions. Heat 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add onions. Cook 8-10 minutes, turning, until lightly caramelized. Deglaze with 50ml white wine. Add 100ml chicken stock and 1 thyme sprig. Bring to a simmer. Cover and braise 15-20 minutes until tender. Season with salt and pepper. Reduce liquid if needed.

Pour off excess fat from chicken searing pan, leaving 15ml. Add chopped shallots to pan. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute. Deglaze with remaining 100ml white wine. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce by half. Add remaining 400ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half again until slightly thickened. Remove from heat. Whisk in Dijon mustard and Pommery mustard. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until jus is emulsified and glossy. Add white wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a smooth jus.

Place one rested chicken supreme slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange a small, organic mound of bell pepper confit beside the chicken. Place three braised cipollini onions artfully around the confit. Spoon a generous, flowing pool of Pommery mustard jus onto the plate, surrounding elements without covering them completely. Garnish with a tiny fresh thyme sprig if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken with Tomato, Mozzarella, and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Chicken with Tomato, Mozzarella, and Garlic is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, roasted chicken thigh, cooked whole, sits prominently. It is topped with melted, bubbling fresh mozzarella that drapes over its edges. Around the chicken, vibrant red cherry tomato halves are nestled, some slightly burst from roasting, releasing their juices. Thinly sliced, caramelized red onion wedges are interspersed, adding depth. Minced roasted garlic pieces are visible among the vegetables. The dish is lightly drizzled with golden olive oil.
