Fresh green basil leaves, torn into irregular pieces, are scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The background features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the skillet. Add red onion wedges and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add thinly sliced garlic and halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften slightly.
Stir in dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nesting them among the vegetables.
Distribute torn mozzarella pieces over the chicken and vegetables.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh torn basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, vibrant orange-red tomato risotto is presented in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The risotto flows gently, indicating its fluid, 'all'onda' consistency. On top, two or three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are nestled into the rice, showcasing a crisp exterior and tender interior. Bright green chopped basil is mixed throughout the risotto, with fresh whole basil leaves and a light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese garnishing the top. A subtle drizzle of olive oil glistens on the surface. The plate sits on a rustic wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon). The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, emphasizing the dish as the focal point. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp white wine.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 bunch, chopped, plus leaves for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken. Rest.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 25g butter. Sauté diced onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast grains.
Pour in white wine (if using). Cook until absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well.
Add one ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Cook for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan and remaining 25g butter.
Fold in chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick chunks.
Serve risotto immediately. Top with chicken chunks, fresh basil leaves, and extra Parmesan.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (finishing with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken & Cottage Cheese Patties
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Chicken & Cottage Cheese Patties are presented on a rustic, well-used wooden dining table, set on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight beige hue. Each patty, about 7-8 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, has a golden-brown, lightly crispy exterior from pan-frying. The interior, revealed slightly on one patty, shows a tender, moist texture with visible specks of minced chicken, white cottage cheese curds, and green parsley. Three to four patties are casually arranged on the plate, slightly overlapping, creating a natural, unpretentious mound. A few small, fresh parsley leaves are scattered loosely around the patties as a functional garnish. The overall color palette is warm browns and whites, with touches of green. The lighting is soft and warm, as if from a kitchen window or overhead fixture, highlighting the comforting appeal. A casually folded plain linen napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is uncluttered, emphasizing the homely nature of the snack.
instructions: Place minced chicken in a large bowl.
Add cottage cheese, minced garlic, diced onion, egg, 60 g breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper.
Mix all ingredients well until combined.
Form the mixture into 12 small patties, about 2 cm thick.
Lightly coat each patty with extra breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Place patties in the hot skillet. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if needed.
Cook patties for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from skillet and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Wine Cherry Entremet with Orange-Vanilla Mousse
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of the Red Wine Cherry Entremet is presented on an elegant, pristine white porcelain plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice reveals distinct, architectural layers: a vibrant, deep ruby red wine cherry gelee layer sits atop a delicate, creamy off-white vanilla bean mousse. Below the mousse, a thin, light orange-hued vegan sponge cake base is visible, subtly infused with orange zest. The cake slice is coated in a flawless, glossy red wine mirror glaze, reflecting light beautifully. The glaze creates a clean, sophisticated sheen over the entire dessert. A single, perfectly ripe fresh cherry with its stem, and a delicate, thin curl of candied orange peel are precisely placed beside the entremet, adding a touch of color and texture. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the dessert's minimalist elegance. The setting includes a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and a polished silver dessert fork, all illuminated by dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows.

ingredients.name: Cashew cream (soaked cashews blended with water)
Coconut cream (thick part from chilled can)

instructions: Prepare Brandy Cherry Compote: Combine 100g pitted cherries, 30g sugar, 15ml brandy, and 15ml orange juice in a small saucepan. Simmer 10-12 minutes until cherries are soft. Cool completely.

Prepare Red Wine Cherry Gelee: Combine 150g pitted cherries, 200ml red wine, 50g sugar, and 1 cinnamon stick in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes. Remove cinnamon stick. Dissolve 4g agar-agar in 30ml cold water. Stir into hot cherry mixture. Simmer 1 minute. Pour into a 15 cm diameter silicone mold or a small flat container. Chill until set, about 2 hours. Cut a 14 cm disc if using a flat container.

Bake Orange Sponge Cake: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 16 cm round cake pan. Whisk dry ingredients: 120g flour, 100g sugar, 5g baking powder, 2g salt. Add orange zest. Whisk wet ingredients: 60ml orange juice, 80ml plant-based milk, 40ml vegetable oil, 5ml vanilla extract. Pour wet into dry. Mix until just combined. Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 10 minutes. Invert onto wire rack. Cool completely. Trim to 16 cm diameter if needed.

Make Vanilla Bean Mousse: Combine 200g cashew cream, 150ml coconut cream, 50ml maple syrup, 5ml vanilla bean paste in a bowl. Whisk until smooth. In a small saucepan, dissolve 2g agar-agar in 30ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk agar-agar mixture into cashew cream mixture. Chill briefly until slightly thickened but still pourable.

Assemble Entremet: Line an 18 cm diameter entremet ring or springform pan with acetate film. Place on a flat tray. Place the orange sponge cake layer at the bottom of the ring. Spread the cooled brandy cherry compote evenly over the sponge cake. Pour half of the vanilla bean mousse over the compote. Carefully place the set red wine cherry gelee disc on top of the mousse. Pour the remaining vanilla bean mousse over the gelee, filling the mold. Smooth top. Freeze minimum 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.

Prepare Red Wine Mirror Glaze: In a saucepan, combine 100ml red wine, 150g sugar, 75g glucose syrup. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat. Stir in 50ml coconut cream and 75g vegan white chocolate (or cacao butter). Stir until melted and smooth. Dissolve 2g agar-agar in 30ml cold water. Stir into glaze. Bring to a simmer. Cook 1 minute. Add red food coloring if desired. Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool to 35-40°C.

Glaze and Finish: Remove frozen entremet from freezer. Remove ring and acetate. Place entremet on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Pour cooled glaze evenly over the frozen entremet. Ensure full coverage. Let excess glaze drip. Transfer entremet to a serving plate using two spatulas. Refrigerate 3-4 hours to thaw and set.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature for the sponge cake.
The entremet must be fully frozen before glazing for a smooth finish.
Adjust sweetness of glaze to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Potato and Roasted Turkey Warm Salad
recipes.visual_description: A warm, comforting salad presented in a large, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Diced roasted sweet potatoes, round sliced carrots, and thinly sliced red onion are casually mixed with tender shredded turkey and vibrant baby spinach. The vegetables display varied textures, from the soft, slightly caramelized sweet potato cubes to the tender carrot rounds. A light, glossy maple-mustard dressing coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural colors. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, with ingredients touching and overlapping, showcasing a generous home-cooked portion. A simple, everyday ceramic plate is set beside the bowl, with basic flatware. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and dice sweet potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and slice carrots into 0.5 cm thick rounds.
Thinly slice red onion into half-moons.
In a large bowl, toss diced sweet potatoes, sliced carrots, and red onion with 30 ml olive oil, 2.5 ml dried thyme, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, shred or dice cooked turkey breast into bite-sized pieces. If using raw turkey, cook it now to 75°C internal temperature, then shred or dice.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 30 ml olive oil, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, and remaining 2.5 ml dried thyme in a small bowl.
In a large serving bowl, combine roasted vegetables, shredded turkey, and baby spinach.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Loin with Olive-Almond Crumble and Cheesy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a refined casual dining dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. At the center, a generous portion of creamy, golden-hued cheesy rice, studded with deeply caramelized onion. The rice is free-flowing. Three thick, round medallions of pan-seared pork loin, with golden-brown crusts and tender interiors, are arranged atop the rice. The pork is presented as whole, unsliced chunks. A vibrant scattering of olive-almond crumble, featuring toasted almond slivers and dark, chopped Kalamata olives, provides contrasting texture and color over the pork and rice. Fresh, finely chopped green parsley is sprinkled for a pop of color. The plate is on a rustic light wooden table. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm atmosphere with a blurred, unobtrusive modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread to sop up any juices.
instructions: Pat pork loin dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork loin until golden brown on all sides, about 8-10 minutes total.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast 15-20 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Rest pork 10 minutes before slicing.
While pork roasts, melt butter and remaining 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sugar. Continue cooking onion until deeply caramelized and golden brown, about 15-20 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, coating grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes, until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small dry skillet, toast almonds over medium heat until lightly golden, about 3-4 minutes. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Combine toasted almonds and chopped olives in a small bowl.
Slice rested pork loin into thick medallions.
Serve cheesy rice. Top with pork medallions. Sprinkle generously with olive-almond crumble. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, then rests to allow carryover cooking to 66-68°C (150-155°F). For well-done, cook to 71°C (160°F) and rest.
Do not overcook the pork; it will dry out.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage and Creamy Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rigatoni pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pasta is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, interspersed with golden-brown crumbled spicy Italian sausage. Several creamy white dollops of fresh ricotta cheese are nestled on top of the pasta, creating a striking visual contrast. Bright green torn basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light dusting of grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese completes the plating. The textures are varied: firm pasta, tender sausage, and smooth ricotta. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and standard silver fork and spoon are placed neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere with a casual bistro feel.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add crumbled Italian sausage. Cook until browned and cooked through, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and black pepper.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 125 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Add drained rigatoni to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves. Gently fold in 150 g of the ricotta cheese until just combined, leaving some visible streaks.
Divide pasta among serving plates. Top each portion with a dollop of the remaining ricotta cheese. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente tagliatelle, generously coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato-butter sauce, forms the base. The sauce glistens, showcasing tender, golden-brown sautéed mushroom slices and flecks of vibrant green parsley. Thick, golden-crusted pan-seared chicken medallions, cut into substantial chunks, are arranged artfully on top of the pasta. A light sprinkle of grated white Parmesan cheese and fresh green parsley provides a contrasting garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting its textures. A small, vibrant mound of fresh, crisp arugula salad sits beside the main plate, offering a fresh counterpoint. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes, then slice into thick medallions.

Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion and cook 3-4 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms and cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add minced garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook 10-15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While sauce simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water before draining.

Add remaining 30g butter and half of the grated Parmesan cheese to the sauce. Stir until melted and combined. Add drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat, adding reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired consistency.
Gently fold in most of the chopped fresh parsley. Serve pasta immediately, topped with chicken medallions. Garnish with remaining Parmesan and fresh parsley. Serve with fresh arugula on the side.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to desired spice level.
Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in poached chicken with glossy, pale skin. The chicken rests on a bed of fragrant, light-yellow Jasmine rice infused with ginger and pandan. Slices of fresh, cool cucumber are arranged neatly to the side. The chicken is lightly drizzled with a mixture of soy sauce and sesame oil. Three small ceramic dipping bowls contain bright red chili sauce, dark soy sauce, and a vibrant green ginger-scallion oil. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate on a light wood table. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a traditional ceramic soup spoon sit to the right. Natural light highlights the moist texture of the meat and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side bowl of hot chicken broth
Include chili sauce, ginger-garlic sauce, and dark soy sauce
Serve at room temperature as per tradition
instructions: Rub chicken with salt to remove impurities.
Rinse chicken under cold water.
Boil 3 liters of water with 30g crushed ginger and scallions.
Submerge chicken in boiling water.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Turn off heat and cover pot.
Steep chicken for 30 minutes.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Submerge chicken in ice water for 5 minutes.
Drain chicken and rub skin with sesame oil.
Sauté 20g minced ginger and minced garlic in chicken fat.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add 600ml poaching liquid and pandan leaves.
Cook rice until liquid is absorbed.
Cut chicken into large chunks.
notes: Save the remaining poaching liquid for a light soup
Rubbing the chicken with salt ensures a smooth skin texture
Using rendered chicken fat for the rice is essential for authenticity

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Creamy Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Tuscan Creamy Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of golden pappardelle pasta, gently tossed in a creamy, blush-toned sauce, forms the base. Thick medallions of seared chicken thigh are arranged naturally atop the pasta, showcasing their golden-brown crust. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes and vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed throughout the pasta, adding color and freshness. Julienne strips of rich red sun-dried tomatoes provide visual depth. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded linen napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a subtly blurred background hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere. The composition is clean, professional, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil, julienned
Dry white wine or chicken broth

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest. Do not clean the skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and julienned sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-5 minutes until they begin to soften and burst.
Pour in white wine or chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Return to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Slice rested chicken thighs into thick medallions.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce in the skillet. Cook until just wilted.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and lemon juice. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Gently fold in sliced chicken medallions.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Peruvian Arroz con Pollo is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, showcasing vibrant colors and textures. Two golden-brown, seared chicken pieces, a thigh and a drumstick, are prominently nestled atop a generous bed of fluffy, emerald-green rice. The rice is infused with cilantro, speckled with bright red diced bell pepper and tender green peas, and small diced carrots. The chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender, moist meat beneath. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered over the dish as a garnish, adding a burst of fresh green. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich hues and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Salsa Criolla (sliced red onion, aji limo, lime juice, and cilantro).
Pair with a glass of Chicha Morada or Inca Kola.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on

instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Do this in batches to avoid crowding the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced red onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red bell pepper. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in aji amarillo paste, cumin powder, and dried oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
In a blender, combine fresh cilantro with 100 ml of chicken broth. Blend until smooth to create a vibrant green cilantro paste.
Add rice to the pot with the cooked aromatics. Stir to coat the rice, toasting for 2 minutes.
Pour in the dark beer (or chicken broth) and remaining chicken broth. Stir in the cilantro paste. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in frozen green peas and small diced carrots. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving. Check chicken internal temperature, it should be 75°C (167°F).
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Roasted Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of homestyle roasted chicken and root vegetables is presented on an everyday, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh rests slightly off-center. Around it, thick chunks of roasted carrots, wedges of tender potatoes, and caramelized onion wedges are casually arranged. The vegetables show slight charring and a soft texture. The overall color palette is warm browns, golden yellows, and earthy oranges. A few fresh rosemary leaves are scattered for garnish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a cozy, naturally lit kitchen. A simple cloth napkin and standard metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The scene evokes a comfortable, lived-in family meal atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the roasting pan for a family-style meal
Serve with a simple green salad

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled, cut into 3-4 cm thick chunks

ingredients.name: fresh rosemary sprigs or dried rosemary

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, carrot chunks, onion wedges, and smashed garlic cloves.
Drizzle vegetables with 30 ml olive oil. Add salt, pepper, dried rosemary, and dried thyme. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Rub remaining 30 ml olive oil over chicken skin. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables on the baking tray.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
Patting chicken skin dry helps achieve crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coq au Vin is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are positioned centrally, coated in a glossy, deep-burgundy wine sauce. Surrounding the chicken are whole, golden-brown button mushrooms, translucent pearl onions, and crispy bacon lardons. The sauce is rich and thick, clinging to the meat. A pinch of fresh green parsley is scattered over the top. The background features a dark wood bistro table with a clean white cotton napkin and a small side plate of crusty baguette. Natural, even lighting highlights the velvety texture of the sauce and the rustic, braised appearance of the vegetables. The entire plate is visible with elegant negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of the same red wine used in the braise
Serve in wide, shallow bowls

ingredients.name: dry red wine (Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in a heavy pot over medium-high heat until skin is golden. Remove from pot.
Fry bacon lardons in the same pot until crisp.
Add whole pearl onions and whole mushrooms to the bacon fat. Brown for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot. Pour in red wine and chicken stock.
Add thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Mix butter and flour into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste into the simmering liquid to thicken the sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes until glossy. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry red wine for the best flavor profile
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Braised Chicken with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan braised chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of creamy, golden polenta forms the base, with a whole, succulent chicken thigh resting centrally on top. The chicken has a rich, deep brown seared skin and is generously coated in a vibrant red-orange tomato sauce, featuring rustic chunks of softened red bell pepper, onion, and sliced garlic. A few vibrant green sprigs of fresh rosemary are placed atop the chicken, and a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adds a final touch. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple light wooden table with a folded neutral cotton napkin and standard Italian flatware beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its inviting colors and textures in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion, sliced garlic, and diced red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
While chicken braises, prepare polenta. Bring water or vegetable broth to a boil in a separate saucepan. Slowly whisk in instant polenta. Reduce heat to low.
Cook polenta, stirring constantly, for 3-5 minutes until thickened and creamy. Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs from the chicken sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Spoon creamy polenta onto serving plates. Place one or two braised chicken thighs on top of the polenta. Ladle generous amounts of the rustic tomato sauce over the chicken and polenta.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For a richer flavor, use chicken stock instead of water for the polenta.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Miso Glaze, Charred Negi, Pea Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a pristine Japanese bone china plate with a subtle, organic pattern. A vibrant green, silky-smooth pea puree forms a fluid, organic swirl. Beside it, two thick, golden-brown seared chicken breast medallions, each perfectly cooked to reveal a moist interior, are brushed with a delicate, glossy miso glaze. Two or three precisely cut, charred negi batons are artfully arranged near the chicken. A single, irregular shard of golden, crispy chicken skin tuile stands upright, adding architectural height and texture. A few delicate microgreens are placed with precision, and a light dusting of sansho pepper finishes the dish. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. Polished wooden chopsticks are positioned beside the plate on a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the food's sophisticated simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a small side cup of clear dashi broth for palate cleansing.
Accompanied by a tiny portion of pickled ginger (gari) to refresh the palate.
instructions: Remove skin from chicken breasts. Reserve skin. Season chicken breasts lightly with salt.
Place chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Place another baking sheet on top. Bake at 180°C until golden and crispy. Break into irregular shards. Set aside.
Combine white miso paste, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring, until glaze thickens slightly. Set aside.

Heat a cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a thin layer of olive oil. Sear chicken breasts, skin-side down (if using skin-on for searing, then remove after crisping for tuile or just use skinless from start), until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (about 10-15 minutes). Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Slice each breast into two thick medallions.
While chicken rests, char negi stalks directly over a gas flame or in a hot dry pan until lightly blackened and tender. Cut charred negi into 4cm batons.

Blanch green peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain well. Transfer peas to a blender. Add butter, chicken stock, and a pinch of salt. Blend until very smooth. Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness.

To plate, create a fluid swirl or small pool of pea puree on one side of a bone china plate. Arrange two chicken medallions beside the puree. Brush chicken with miso glaze. Artfully place 2-3 charred negi batons. Insert one crispy chicken skin tuile shard. Garnish with a few microgreens and a light sprinkle of sansho pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Tongue with Spicy Miso Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef Tongue with Spicy Miso Glaze is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Thick, tender chunks of rich, dark brown beef tongue are nestled centrally. Alongside, golden-brown sautéed trumpet mushroom rounds are arranged organically. A glossy, deep reddish-brown miso-gochujang glaze is generously spooned over the tongue and mushrooms, creating inviting pools of sauce. A fine dusting of grated, off-white kefalotiri cheese melts slightly into the warm glaze. Bright green, finely sliced scallions are scattered over the dish, with a light sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds adding a subtle texture. The plating emphasizes natural shapes and moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A set of dark chopsticks rests beside the plate, and a small, empty white rice bowl is positioned subtly to the side. A folded white cotton napkin completes the casual yet refined presentation. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures. The entire plate is visible, with a soft-focus restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed white rice.
Accompany with a small dish of quick-pickled daikon or cucumber for a refreshing contrast.
instructions: Clean beef tongue. Trim excess fat. Place tongue in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes. Drain water. Rinse tongue under cold water. Carefully peel off and discard the tough outer skin. Cut tongue into large 5 cm chunks.
Heat neutral oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef tongue chunks on all sides until browned. Remove tongue from pot. Set aside.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced ginger to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Deglaze with sake or dry white wine. Scrape up any browned bits.

Return beef tongue to the pot. Add soy sauce, mirin, and dashi or beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef tongue is fork-tender. Check internal temperature of thickest part of beef tongue, should be minimum 75°C (167°F).

Remove tongue from braising liquid. Strain braising liquid into a separate saucepan. Skim off any fat. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened and reduced by half (about 250-300 ml).

In a small bowl, whisk together dark miso paste, gochujang, brown sugar, and sesame oil with 60 ml of the reduced braising liquid until smooth. Add this mixture back to the remaining reduced braising liquid in the saucepan. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the glaze thickens to a glossy consistency.

Slice trumpet mushrooms into 1 cm thick rounds or halves, depending on size. Heat a separate pan with a touch of neutral oil over medium-high heat. Sauté mushrooms until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice braised beef tongue chunks into thick 2-3 cm medallions or keep as larger chunks if preferred. Arrange beef tongue and sautéed trumpet mushrooms on individual plates.
Spoon the warm miso-gochujang glaze generously over the beef tongue and mushrooms. Grate kefalotiri cheese directly over the dish.
Garnish with finely sliced scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: The initial blanching and peeling of the beef tongue are crucial for tenderness and removing impurities.
Adjust gochujang quantity to your preferred spice level.
Kefalotiri cheese can be substituted with Pecorino Romano or a sharp aged cheddar if unavailable, though the flavor profile will differ slightly.

recipes.recipe_name: Whipped Feta-Yogurt Crémeux, Framboise Gel, Mint Tuile
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an exquisite, matte white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight the minimalist composition. A generous, organically shaped dollop of the Whipped Feta-Yogurt Crémeux, a soft, off-white hue, forms the central anchor, showcasing its smooth, creamy texture. Beside it, small, artfully placed irregular dots and short, flowing lines of vibrant, glossy framboise gel create a striking color contrast, their deep crimson catching the light. Perched delicately on the crémeux or standing nearby is a single, thin mint tuile, its translucent, golden-green surface hinting at its crisp texture and infused with fine specks of fresh mint. The overall arrangement is asymmetrical and natural, with each element purposefully positioned to create a sense of effortless elegance. The plate rests on a polished dark wood table, complemented by a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the textures and the thoughtful simplicity of the plating.
instructions: Prepare Framboise Gel:
Blend raspberries until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds.
Combine raspberry purée, sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk in agar-agar powder. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat. Stir in Framboise Eau de Vie.
Pour gel into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 1 hour.
Once set, blend gel until smooth and pipeable. Transfer to a piping bag. Keep chilled.
Prepare Whipped Feta-Yogurt Crémeux:
Soak gelatin sheet in cold water for 5 minutes until softened.
Crumble feta cheese into a bowl. Add Greek yogurt and sugar.
Whip mixture until smooth. Use a stand mixer or hand mixer.
Gently heat 20 ml of the heavy cream until warm. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Dissolve gelatin in warm cream.
Pour gelatin mixture into feta-yogurt mixture, whisking constantly.
Whip remaining heavy cream until soft peaks form.
Gently fold whipped cream into feta-yogurt mixture. Add Framboise Eau de Vie.
Transfer crémeux to a piping bag. Chill for at least 2 hours to set.
Prepare Mint Tuile:
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
Finely chop mint leaves. Or, blend mint with a tiny bit of egg white to form a paste.
In a bowl, whisk together sugar, melted butter, flour, and egg white until smooth.
Stir in chopped mint or mint paste.
Spread thin layers of batter onto the prepared baking sheet using an offset spatula. Create irregular, natural shapes.
Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until edges are golden and centers are crisp. Watch carefully.
Immediately remove from oven. While warm, gently drape tuiles over a rolling pin or curved surface to create a subtle curve. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
Assemble Dish (Serves 4):
Pipe generous dollops of Whipped Feta-Yogurt Crémeux onto one side of each serving plate. Create an organic, flowing shape.
Pipe small, irregular dots or lines of Framboise Gel around the crémeux.
Delicately place a Mint Tuile upright, leaning against the crémeux or standing freely.
Garnish with 1-2 tiny fresh mint micro-leaves, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken with Tomato and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Skillet Chicken with Tomato and Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh is positioned prominently on top of a generous bed of reddish-orange tomato-infused rice. The rice is interspersed with tender, 2cm cubed potatoes, 1cm diced carrots, and finely diced onions, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. The chicken has a crisp exterior from searing and a succulent interior. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is inviting and balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and carrots to the skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice and diced tomatoes. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Nestle seared chicken thighs and cubed potatoes into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Cook 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Salsa with Avocado Crema
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a handcrafted, matte cream or light beige ceramic plate, resting on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. The dish features a smooth, pale green swirl or dollop of avocado crema, offering a soft, inviting base. Adjacent to it, a vibrant mound of diced fermented tomato salsa, showcasing rich reds, a hint of orange, and small flecks of deep green from the chili and garlic. The diced tomatoes are clean-cut, revealing their juicy texture. A few fresh, deep green coriander leaves are strategically placed on or near the salsa, providing a natural accent. Optionally, one or two irregularly shaped, brittle dehydrated tomato crisps, in shades of deep red or rustic orange, are placed subtly to add an organic textural contrast. Negative space is abundant, emphasizing the purity and natural beauty of each ingredient. The lighting is soft and natural, casting gentle shadows that highlight textures. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the plate, completing the eco-conscious, minimalist aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Salsa: Wash tomatoes. Dice tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Retain tomato skins and ends for crisps if desired.
Dice red onion into 0.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic and finely chop chili.
In a clean glass jar, combine diced tomatoes, red onion, minced garlic, and chopped chili.
Dissolve 10 g sea salt in 500 ml non-chlorinated water to make a 2% brine.
Pour brine over vegetables in the jar, ensuring all vegetables are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small plate to keep vegetables under the brine.
Cover jar with an airlock lid or a regular lid loosely to allow gas release.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp jar daily if using a loose lid.
Once fermented, transfer salsa to a clean container and refrigerate.
Prepare Avocado Crema: Halve avocados. Scoop flesh into a blender or food processor.
Add lime juice and 5 g sea salt. Blend until smooth. Add cold water gradually, 10 ml at a time, until desired creamy consistency is reached.
Transfer crema to a squeeze bottle or piping bag, or use a spoon for plating.
Assemble Dish: On a minimalist ceramic plate, create a small, neat pool or swirl of avocado crema.
Spoon a small portion of the fermented tomato salsa next to or on top of the crema.
Garnish with a few fresh coriander leaves.
If making dehydrated tomato crisps: dehydrate tomato skins/ends until brittle. Break into small, irregular pieces and place one or two next to the salsa for texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Avocado Tartare with Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant portion of Fermented Tomato & Avocado Tartare is centered on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The tartare forms a neat, round cylinder (7-8cm diameter), showcasing vibrant green diced avocado (8-10mm) and deep red diced fermented tomato (5mm). Finely diced translucent pink pickled red onion pieces are interspersed. A delicate pool of light tomato water encircles the base, hinting at its sustainable origin. The plate offers generous negative space. Garnishes are minimal: a few thin, curled rings of bright pink pickled red onion and a fresh cilantro sprig top the tartare. The scene is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural beige undyed linen napkin rests subtly beside. Soft, diffused natural light highlights fresh textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with a blurred hint of green foliage.

ingredients.name: Salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes (at least 3-5 days in advance): Wash and quarter tomatoes. Place in a clean jar. Add salt, garlic, and herbs. Cover tomatoes with filtered water if needed; ensure submerged (use fermentation weight). Seal jar with airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until desired tanginess. Strain tomatoes, reserving liquid (tomato water). Dice fermented tomatoes into small cubes (5mm).

Prepare Pickled Red Onion (at least 1 hour in advance): Thinly slice red onion into rings or half-moons. In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, water, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and bay leaf. Simmer, stirring until dissolved. Remove from heat. Pack sliced onion into a clean jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions; ensure fully submerged. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Prepare Avocado Tartare: Halve, pit, scoop out avocado flesh. Dice avocado into small cubes (8-10mm). Immediately toss diced avocado with lime juice to prevent browning. Gently fold in chopped cilantro and sliced green onion. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble the Dish: Drain pickled red onions, reserving a few rings for garnish. Finely dice the majority. Gently combine diced fermented tomatoes, diced pickled red onion, and avocado tartare. Taste and adjust seasoning. For plating, use a 7-8cm ring mold on each plate. Fill with tartare mixture, pressing gently. Lift mold. Drizzle reserved tomato water around tartare base. Garnish with reserved pickled red onion rings and a cilantro sprig. Finish with a light drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Brown Sugar Pineapple Chicken
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a glossy, rich brown sugar pineapple cream sauce. Diced, tender pineapple pieces are visible within the sauce, clinging to the chicken. Beside the chicken, a neat, modest mound of fluffy white rice provides a clean contrast. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh cilantro, adding a vibrant green accent. The overall presentation is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and warm colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
instructions: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a plate.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the same skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced pineapple, brown sugar, and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until pineapple softens slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in the full-fat coconut cream.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with cold water to form a smooth slurry. Pour slurry into the sauce, whisking constantly.
Simmer sauce for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until it thickens to a desired consistency.
Return cooked chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken to coat thoroughly.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust brown sugar to taste for desired sweetness.
The sauce should be glossy and thick enough to coat the chicken without being overly pasty.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallops with Creamy Tomato and Corn Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Tomato and Corn Risotto is centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid, not stiff, showcasing its rich texture with visible diced red tomatoes and yellow corn kernels throughout. Four perfectly seared, golden-brown sea scallops with a slight crust are arranged organically atop the risotto. A scattering of vibrant green fresh oregano leaves garnishes the dish. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Prepare ingredients. Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. If using fresh corn, cut kernels from cob.
Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it simmering over low heat.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent. This is toasting the rice.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add diced tomatoes and corn kernels. Stir to combine.
Add one ladleful of hot broth to the rice. Stir constantly until broth is almost fully absorbed. This is the risotto technique.

Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 20-25 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and slightly fluid. Rice should be al dente.

Remove risotto from heat. Stir in 40 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until butter and cheese melt, creating a creamy texture. This is mantecatura. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While risotto cooks, prepare scallops. Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil and 20 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Place scallops in a single layer in the hot skillet. Do not overcrowd. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and cooked through. They should have a beautiful crust. Cook in batches if necessary.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy risotto onto each plate. Arrange seared scallops on top or beside the risotto. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Crispy Soppressata, Bacon, and Herbed Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni with Crispy Soppressata, Bacon, and Herbed Breadcrumbs is presented in a white porcelain pasta bowl. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Diced soppressata cubes and bacon lardons are mixed throughout, with some visible on top, showcasing their crispy, reddish-brown texture. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown, coarse herbed breadcrumbs covers the top, adding textural contrast. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese forms a light layer. A few fresh basil leaves are placed artfully. The dish is centrally composed, leaving moderate negative space on the white bowl. It sits on a simple wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese
Offer crusty bread for dipping sauce
instructions: Cut bacon into 1 cm lardons. Dice soppressata into 1 cm cubes.
Tear bread into small pieces. Pulse in food processor to create coarse breadcrumbs.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs. Toast until golden brown and crispy. Stir frequently. Remove from pan. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley. Set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Cook over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving 15 ml in the pan.
Add diced soppressata to the pan with bacon fat. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove soppressata with a slotted spoon. Combine with cooked bacon. Set aside.
Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Add onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Add cooked rigatoni to the tomato sauce. Add cooked bacon and soppressata. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Chop remaining fresh parsley and basil. Stir into pasta. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion generously with toasted herbed breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Carciofi Pasta al Limone
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of Pollo e Carciofi Pasta al Limone is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among perfectly al dente fettuccine, which is lightly coated in a creamy, bright lemon-Parmesan sauce. Tender, quartered artichoke hearts are interspersed throughout, adding a pale green contrast. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan adorn the top. The dish exhibits a harmonious blend of warm golden, creamy white, and fresh green tones. The pasta is elegantly twirled to create height, with chicken pieces placed naturally on top, not fanned. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table surface with a white cotton napkin folded beside it. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting, with minimal, unobtrusive elements to maintain focus on the food.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80g, freshly grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and quartered artichoke hearts. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Meanwhile, cook fettuccine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the broth mixture. Add seared chicken chunks, lemon juice, lemon zest, and grated Parmesan cheese. Toss to combine.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Wild Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Wild Mushroom Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, golden-hued risotto, cooked to a fluid, flowing consistency, forms a natural pool on one side of the plate. Scattered throughout the risotto are tender, earthy brown wild mushroom slices and vibrant green flecks of fresh oregano. Beside the risotto, two or three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions are artfully arranged, showcasing their slightly crispy skin and juicy interior. The chicken pieces are whole, not fanned. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh oregano garnishes the chicken and risotto, adding a pop of green. The composition is balanced, leaving appropriate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Traditional Italian flatware is placed alongside the dish. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and fluid.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Accompany with a simple green salad and crusty bread.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, set aside. Keep warm.
Chop onion finely. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice kernels.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.

Add one ladleful of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Repeat this process, adding broth ladle by ladle, stirring constantly, until rice is creamy and al dente. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This is 'mantecatura'. Stir vigorously until risotto is creamy and fluid.
Stir in fresh oregano. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice each chicken breast into thick medallions or serve whole.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls. Place chicken medallions beside or on top of the risotto.
traditional_techniques: Risotto method (toasting rice, gradual broth addition, mantecatura)

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Black Bean and Pasilla Chili Soup
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, deep reddish-brown black bean soup fills a white porcelain bowl. The soup's surface is smooth with a subtle sheen, indicating its rich, velvety texture. A dollop of creamy, light green tarragon-lime crema sits slightly off-center on top, contrasting beautifully with the dark soup. Around the crema, a scattering of whole, glossy black beans adds visual interest and texture. A fresh sprig of vibrant green tarragon is placed artfully beside the crema, providing a pop of color and freshness. The bowl is set on a simple, clean wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Mexican pottery or a small dish of lime wedges. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting warmth and professional plating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Serve with a side of pickled red onions
Serve with a sprinkle of crumbled vegan cotija cheese
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from dried chilies. Place in a heatproof bowl. Cover with boiling water. Let soak for 20 minutes until softened. Drain, reserving some liquid.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add roughly chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes. Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add rehydrated chilies, sautéed onion, garlic, black beans (reserve 50g for garnish), dried oregano, cumin, smoked paprika, and 500ml of vegetable broth to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Add more reserved chili liquid if needed for desired consistency.
Pour blended mixture back into the pot. Add remaining vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare tarragon-lime crema: In a small bowl, combine vegan sour cream with 5g finely chopped fresh tarragon and a squeeze of lime juice.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with reserved whole black beans, a dollop of tarragon-lime crema, and a sprig of fresh tarragon. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Tataki Bites
recipes.visual_description: A clean, white rectangular porcelain platter showcases individual Beef Tataki Bites. Each bite features a 1cm thick cucumber round topped with a thinly sliced (2-3mm) piece of seared beef tenderloin. The beef displays a distinct, dark seared edge contrasting with a vibrant, deep red, rare interior. A light drizzle of clear, amber-colored Tataki dressing coats each bite. Finely sliced bright green green onions are sprinkled over the beef. Thin, vibrant red radish slices are placed sparingly among the bites, adding a pop of color. A scattering of golden toasted sesame seeds provides subtle texture. The composition is organized in neat rows, with ample negative space highlighting the precise arrangement. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere. The entire platter is visible, presenting a refined yet approachable snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an otsumami (snack with drinks) or as an appetizer before a meal.
Offer small individual dipping bowls of extra Tataki dressing for those who prefer more.
instructions: Prepare the Tataki Dressing: Whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, mirin, grated ginger, minced garlic, and sesame oil in a small bowl. Set aside.

Sear the Beef: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot. Sear beef for 60-90 seconds per side, rotating to sear all surfaces, until a deep brown crust forms. The interior should remain rare.
Rest and Chill Beef: Remove beef from pan. Immediately transfer to an ice bath or refrigerate for 15-20 minutes until thoroughly chilled. This firms the meat for slicing.
Slice Beef: Once chilled, slice the beef very thinly against the grain, about 2-3mm thick. Use a very sharp knife.
Prepare Cucumber Rounds: Slice cucumber into 1 cm thick rounds.
Assemble Bites: Place one thin slice of beef on each cucumber round.

Garnish and Serve: Arrange the assembled bites on a clean serving platter. Drizzle generously with the Tataki dressing. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions, radish slices, and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Use a high-quality cut of beef tenderloin for best results, as it is served rare.
Chilling the beef thoroughly after searing is crucial for achieving clean, thin slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Plum & Bean Earth
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a minimalist, unglazed ceramic plate in an earthy tone, showcasing natural textures. At the center, a quenelle of creamy, light beige sweetened kidney bean puree provides a soft, organic base. Around it, slices of ruby-hued fermented plums are arranged artfully but unfussily, highlighting their natural curves. A deep amber drizzle of dark beer reduction cascades gently over the plums and bean puree. Scattered sparingly are delicate, paper-thin, golden parmesan crisps, offering a subtle savory glint. A very fine dusting of the sardine umami crumb is applied with precision, providing an unexpected, deep flavor accent. A whisper of red chili dust adds a hint of warmth. The composition is clean, with ample white space, emphasizing the pure beauty and natural colors of each ingredient. The setting includes a light bamboo mat, a simple linen napkin, and soft, natural overhead lighting.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Plums: Wash plums, remove pits, and slice into 1 cm wedges. Dissolve 5g salt in 250ml filtered water to make a 2% brine. Place plum slices in a clean jar. Pour brine over plums, ensuring they are fully submerged. Cover lightly and let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours until lightly effervescent. Drain well before use.

Cook Sweetened Kidney Bean Puree: Rinse dried kidney beans. Soak in cold water overnight. Drain. Place beans in a pot, cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 60-90 minutes until very tender. Drain. Transfer hot beans to a food processor with 50ml maple syrup, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Blend until very smooth. Adjust sweetness if needed. Keep warm.

Make Dark Beer Reduction: Pour dark beer into a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook slowly until liquid has reduced to a thick, syrupy consistency (approx. 50ml). Set aside.
Prepare Chili Dust: Remove stem and seeds from dried chili. Toast lightly in a dry pan until fragrant. Grind into a fine powder using a spice grinder or mortar and pestle. Set aside.

Form Parmesan Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate parmesan cheese finely. On a parchment-lined baking sheet, spread small mounds of grated parmesan (approx. 5g each) into very thin circles. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely on the sheet; they will crisp further. Break into irregular shards.

Create Sardine Umami Crumb: Preheat oven to 100°C. Drain sardine fillets very well and pat extremely dry with paper towels. Place on a small baking sheet. Bake for 30-45 minutes, or until completely dehydrated and brittle. Let cool. Crumble or grind into a fine, savory powder.

Assemble the Dish: On each minimalist plate, place a generous quenelle of the warm sweetened kidney bean puree. Arrange a few slices of fermented plum artfully around the puree. Drizzle the dark beer reduction over the plums and bean puree. Carefully place a few shards of parmesan crisp on top. Lightly dust the entire dish with a tiny pinch of the sardine umami crumb and a whisper of chili dust. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe embraces a zero-waste philosophy; consider composting any fruit scraps. The fermentation of plums can be done in advance for deeper flavor.
Adjust sweetness of the bean puree and beer reduction to your preference. The sardine crumb and parmesan crisp offer a surprising savory counterpoint to the sweet elements.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Banana & Umami Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic dessert composition centers on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate. A generous, organic dollop of thick, pale beige Berbere Yogurt Cheese sits to one side, its surface smooth with a faint, warm speckle of spice. Adjacent to it, a portion of Fermented Green Banana Compote, its natural light brown hue from the cooked bananas, shows soft, mashed textures and occasional small chunks. A glistening, deep red Kimchi Glaze is artfully drizzled in a single, fluid line across the compote and partially onto the yogurt cheese, providing a vibrant, unexpected color contrast. Scattered over the compote and glaze are small, irregular chunks of dark, caramelized Candied Beef Tongue Crumbles, offering a contrasting crisp texture. The presentation emphasizes negative space, allowing each element to breathe. The table surface is light, natural wood, with a folded, undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the subtle textures and organic forms.
instructions: Rinse beef tongue. Place in a pot with 500ml water and 2g salt.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 2-3 hours until very tender.
Remove tongue. Peel outer skin while warm.
Cool tongue completely. Finely dice into 3mm cubes.
In a pan, heat 5ml olive oil. Add diced tongue, 15ml maple syrup, and 5g hot bean paste.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until tongue is caramelized and crisp.
Spread crisps on parchment paper. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
Line a sieve with cheesecloth. Place over a bowl.
Spoon yogurt into the cheesecloth.
Refrigerate for 6-8 hours, or overnight, until thick and creamy.
