Discard whey. Mix yogurt cheese with 2g berbere. Set aside.
Peel green bananas. Slice into 5mm thick rounds.
Place banana slices in a clean jar. Cover with filtered water. Add a pinch of salt. (Optional: Add 1 tablespoon kimchi liquid for fermentation).
Cover jar with a loose lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days until slightly tangy.
Drain bananas.
In a saucepan, combine fermented banana slices with 80ml maple syrup and 3g salt.
Simmer over low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until bananas soften and liquid thickens into a compote.
Mash lightly with a fork for desired consistency. Cool.
Finely mince 100g kimchi or use 50g kimchi liquid.
In a small saucepan, combine minced kimchi/liquid with 5ml maple syrup.
Simmer over low heat, stirring, until liquid reduces to a thick, glossy glaze.
Cool.
Place a dollop of Berbere Yogurt Cheese on each plate.
Spoon Fermented Green Banana Compote next to it.
Drizzle with Kimchi Glaze.
Sprinkle generously with Candied Beef Tongue Crumbles.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Tomato, Garlic, and Dijon Mustard
recipes.visual_description: A single, tender braised chicken thigh, golden-brown skin visible, is placed slightly off-center in a deep, clean white porcelain plate. A rich, rust-red tomato and Dijon mustard sauce generously pools around the chicken, showcasing visible flecks of finely sliced red chili, diced onion, and minced garlic. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is scattered over the chicken and sauce, with a small sprig of fresh thyme positioned artfully beside the thigh. The dish presents a warm, inviting color palette of deep reds, golden browns, and vibrant greens. The setting features a simple, light wooden table surface with a white cotton napkin and traditional European flatware, under soft, natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a light-bodied red wine like Pinot Noir or Beaujolais
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and finely sliced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is almost evaporated.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, Dijon mustard, chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Braised Beef Tongue with Kimchi-Green Banana Hash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table. The focus is on three to four thick-cut, pan-seared beef tongue medallions, coated in a glossy, dark reddish-brown berbere-gochujang glaze. The tongue pieces are arranged naturally, not fanned, showcasing their tender, rich interior and caramelized exterior. Beside the tongue is a neat mound of vibrant kimchi-green banana hash, featuring diced green bananas with a light golden crust, interspersed with bright red and orange chopped kimchi. A contrasting dollop of creamy, off-white yogurt cheese sits elegantly on the plate, offering a cool counterpoint. Freshly chopped green cilantro or scallions are sprinkled over the tongue and hash, adding a pop of verdant color and freshness. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing elements to breathe. Background elements are minimal: a folded cotton napkin, a single fork and knife, and a subtle, soft natural light illuminating the dish.
instructions: Rinse beef tongue. Place in a large pot with chopped onion, smashed garlic, and sliced ginger. Cover with beef broth. Add 5g salt and 3g black pepper.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender when pierced with a fork.
Remove tongue from broth. Let cool slightly. Peel off the outer skin. Discard skin and braising aromatics. Reserve braising liquid.
While tongue braises, peel green bananas. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
In a separate pot, cover banana cubes with water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10-15 minutes until tender but still firm. Drain.

In a small saucepan, combine berbere, gochujang, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, and 125 ml of reserved braising liquid. Whisk until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer, cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Set aside.

Heat 15 ml neutral oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add chopped kimchi and cooked green banana cubes. Sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until kimchi is slightly caramelized and bananas are lightly browned. Season with remaining salt and pepper.

Slice the peeled beef tongue into 1.5 cm thick medallions. Heat remaining 15 ml neutral oil in another large pan over medium-high heat. Sear tongue medallions for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly crispy.
Add seared tongue medallions to the glaze saucepan. Gently toss to coat thoroughly.
Divide kimchi-green banana hash among 4 white porcelain plates. Arrange 3-4 glazed beef tongue medallions beside the hash. Place a generous dollop of yogurt cheese on the plate.
Sprinkle chopped cilantro or scallions over the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thai Basil Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A neat mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies one side. Adjacent, a generous portion of spicy Thai basil chicken (Pad Krapow Gai) is artfully placed, featuring finely diced chicken pieces wok-fried to a light golden-brown, intermingled with vibrant green holy basil leaves, thinly sliced red bird's eye chilies, and minced garlic. The chicken has a glossy, rich brown sauce clinging to it, indicating proper caramelization and seasoning. Scattered around the chicken are bright red halved cherry tomatoes, adding a fresh, juicy contrast. A few fresh basil leaves garnish the top. The overall presentation is clean and balanced, showcasing the vibrant colors and varied textures. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate on a light wooden table surface, under natural, even lighting, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies and a squeeze of lime).

ingredients.name: Thai Bird's Eye Chilies, thinly sliced

instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package instructions. Keep warm.
Combine soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and water/stock in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves. This is the stir-fry sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince to the wok. Break up the chicken with a spatula. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the stir-fry sauce over the chicken. Stir well to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Add holy basil leaves to the wok. Stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds until basil wilts. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve the spicy basil chicken directly alongside a portion of warm jasmine rice. Garnish with halved cherry tomatoes and a few fresh basil leaves.
notes: Holy basil (krapow) is traditional for this dish. If unavailable, Thai basil or sweet basil can be used as a substitute, though the flavor will be slightly different.
Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Green Curry Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Thai Green Curry Chicken is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The vibrant green curry is fluid and inviting, filled with tender, seared chicken chunks. Visible elements include quartered Thai eggplant, bright green bell pepper squares, and pale sliced bamboo shoots. The curry’s surface glistens, topped with fresh, dark green Thai basil leaves and a few thin slices of red Thai chili, adding a pop of contrasting color. Fluffy, white jasmine rice is served neatly beside the curry in a smaller, matching white bowl. The arrangement sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Thai ceramic spoon. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and rich textures, against a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background. The presentation is professional yet approachable, emphasizing authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra jasmine rice.
Offer additional fresh sliced Thai chilies on the side for custom spice levels.
Serve with a side of fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies (Prik Nam Pla) for dipping.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Cook according to package directions. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Mince garlic. Slice Thai chilies.
Quarter Thai eggplant. Cut green bell pepper into 2cm squares. Drain bamboo shoots.
Heat oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat.
Add green curry paste and minced garlic. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in 200ml coconut milk. Stir well to combine with paste. Bring to a simmer.
Add chicken chunks. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until chicken is seared on all sides. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add remaining 600ml coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add Thai eggplant, green bell pepper, and bamboo shoots. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, or until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in most Thai basil leaves and sliced Thai chilies. Reserve some for garnish.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce or palm sugar as needed.
Serve hot with jasmine rice.
traditional_techniques: Stir-frying curry paste to release aromatics
Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors
Cooking with coconut milk for creamy texture

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew is thick, filling the bowl, showcasing large, irregular chunks of seared chicken. Tender diced potatoes, vibrant orange carrot slices, bright green broccoli florets, and earthy brown mushroom slices are visibly suspended in the rich, opaque cream sauce. The chicken pieces are golden-brown, contrasting with the paler sauce. Vegetables retain their distinct shapes and natural colors. Fresh, chopped green parsley is sprinkled on top. The bowl sits on a well-used, light brown wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. Warm, inviting lighting suggests a cozy kitchen. A standard metal spoon rests beside the bowl. The background is softly blurred, indicating a lived-in family kitchen.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks (3cm). Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Stir until smooth and thickened.
Add diced potatoes (2cm cubes), sliced carrots (1.5cm slices), dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Add broccoli florets and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in heavy cream. Heat through, do not boil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Discard bay leaf. Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore is presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits centrally, partially submerged in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. The sauce is vibrant red-orange, studded with tender, irregular chunks of red and green bell peppers, dark quartered mushrooms, and soft diced onions. The chicken skin is crisp and inviting. Beside the chicken, a neat pile of golden-brown roasted potato wedges, with slightly crisped edges, provides a textural contrast. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. A dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese lightly covers the chicken and sauce. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a medium-bodied red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, bell pepper chunks, and quartered mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, oregano, and basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover skillet and transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and sauce alongside roasted potato wedges. Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Homestyle Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base, topped with hearty, golden-brown chicken chunks. The chicken is seared, showing irregular, appealing edges. Diced orange carrots, vibrant red bell pepper, and translucent yellow onions are scattered generously among the chicken. Freshly chopped green basil leaves are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish has a natural, unarranged look, as if scooped directly from the skillet onto the plate. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple metal fork resting nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting nature of the meal.
instructions: Rinse rice. Combine rice with 600ml chicken broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 4-5 minutes until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion, carrots, and bell pepper to the same skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Return seared chicken to the skillet with vegetables. Stir to combine.
Stir in chopped fresh basil. Serve immediately over cooked rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Tofu Crème Brûlée with Mixed Berry Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single Tofu Crème Brûlée is presented in a clean, white porcelain ramekin. The top features a perfectly caramelized, golden-amber sugar crust, smooth and shiny, with subtle dark spots from the torch. Beneath the crisp crust, the creamy, off-white custard is visible along the edges of the ramekin. The ramekin sits on a simple wooden table surface, slightly off-center. Beside it, a small, artful swirl of vibrant red mixed berry coulis adds a pop of color. A few fresh, small mint leaves are placed delicately near the coulis for garnish. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The lighting is natural and even, creating soft shadows. A simple white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the ramekin. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Boil water for a water bath.
Drain silken tofu. Combine tofu, plant-based milk, granulated sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla extract in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Ensure no tofu lumps remain.
Pour the mixture evenly into four 150 ml capacity oven-safe ramekins.
Place ramekins in a deep baking dish. Carefully pour boiling water into the baking dish, reaching halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center is still slightly wobbly.
Remove ramekins from water bath. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until fully set.
For the berry coulis, combine mixed berries, water, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and break down.
Press the berry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds and pulp. Discard solids. Chill coulis.
Just before serving, sprinkle about 15 g of brown sugar evenly over the top of each chilled crème brûlée.
Use a kitchen torch to caramelize the sugar until it forms a dark, amber, crisp crust. Work quickly and evenly.
Let the caramelized sugar cool and harden for a few minutes.
Serve immediately with a drizzle of the chilled berry coulis on the side of the plate.
notes: Ensure the tofu mixture is completely smooth for a silky custard.
Do not overbake the crème brûlée; it will continue to set as it cools.
Thorough chilling is crucial for the crème brûlée to set properly.
A good kitchen torch is essential for achieving a perfect caramelized sugar crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Shrimp and Blue Cheese Gnocchi
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Shrimp and Blue Cheese Gnocchi is presented in a pristine white porcelain shallow bowl. The plump, off-white potato gnocchi are coated in a velvety, pale ivory sauce, subtly speckled with dark blue crumbs from the melted cheese. Nestled among the gnocchi are succulent, whole pinkish-orange shrimp, their natural curl adding visual interest. A generous scattering of golden-brown, roughly chopped toasted cashews provides a textural contrast and nutty aroma. Vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the dish, enhancing the color palette. The sauce pools slightly at the bottom, indicating its creamy consistency. The dish is placed on a simple, clean wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant-style background, maintaining focus on the food.

ingredients.name: Large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Prepare ingredients: Roughly chop cashews. Finely mince shallot. Mince garlic. Chop fresh parsley.
Toast cashews: Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Add chopped cashews. Toast 3-5 minutes until golden and fragrant. Stir frequently to prevent burning. Remove from pan and set aside.
Cook gnocchi: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add gnocchi. Cook according to package directions, typically 2-3 minutes, until gnocchi float to the surface. Drain well and set aside.

Sear shrimp: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add shrimp in a single layer. Sear 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove shrimp from skillet and set aside.
Prepare sauce base: Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallot. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze (optional): If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook 1-2 minutes until wine is mostly evaporated.

Make blue cheese sauce: Pour in heavy cream and chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add crumbled blue cheese. Stir constantly until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. Simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Combine: Add cooked gnocchi and seared shrimp to the skillet with the sauce. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Serve: Divide the creamy gnocchi and shrimp among four individual plates or shallow bowls. Garnish each serving generously with toasted cashews and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef, Mushroom & Tomato Bruschetta
recipes.visual_description: A homely starter portion of Beef, Mushroom & Tomato Bruschetta rests on a simple, well-used wooden dining table. Two generous slices of rustic ciabatta bread, lightly toasted to a golden-brown, are piled high with a rich, savory topping. The beef is finely ground and browned, mixed with small diced mushrooms and vibrant red diced tomatoes. Cooked brown rice adds texture, subtly integrated. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered generously over the topping. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens. The plate is a simple, off-white ceramic with natural imperfections. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene. The background shows a relaxed, lived-in family dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while bread is warm and crisp.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese on the side for diners to add as desired.
instructions: Prepare brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Dice mushrooms into small pieces. Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced mushrooms and minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms soften.
If using, pour in red wine. Cook, scraping up browned bits, until liquid evaporates.
Stir in cooked brown rice and diced tomatoes. Cook for 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the fresh basil, roughly chopped. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice ciabatta loaf into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Lightly brush both sides with olive oil.
Toast bread slices in a dry pan or under a grill until golden and crisp.
Spoon generous portions of the beef mixture onto each toasted bread slice.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves. Drizzle lightly with olive oil.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure beef is fully cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Matar Tamatar Curry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Aloo Matar Tamatar Curry is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, showcasing its rich, semi-thick, reddish-orange gravy. Cubed, tender potatoes and bright green peas are suspended in the aromatic tomato-onion base. The surface is adorned with a generous scattering of fresh, verdant cilantro leaves, providing a refreshing contrast. The dish is centrally placed on a simple wooden table, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the bowl, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a small, round traditional Indian metal katori containing a side of basmati rice or a piece of warm, fluffy naan bread complete the authentic Indian dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with Basmati rice, naan bread, or roti.
Accompaniments such as cooling raita (yogurt dip) or a spicy Indian pickle enhance the meal.
instructions: Peel and dice potatoes into 2-3 cm cubes. Finely chop onions. Puree tomatoes.
Heat oil or ghee in a deep pan or pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Allow them to splutter and turn golden brown (Tadka).
Add chopped onions. Sauté until translucent and golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato puree. Cook, stirring occasionally, until oil separates from the mixture (Bhunao technique). This takes about 8-10 minutes.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add diced potatoes and mix well to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in 250 ml water. Add salt to taste. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Add green peas. Cook uncovered for 5 minutes until peas are tender and gravy thickens slightly.
Stir in garam masala. Cook for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro.
traditional_techniques: Bhunao (Sautéing aromatic base until oil separates)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Blue Cheese Risotto with Seared Shrimp and Toasted Cashews
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Blue Cheese Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a fluid, flowing consistency. The risotto is a creamy, pale ivory, dotted with subtle blue cheese. Several whole, plump, pan-seared shrimp, displaying vibrant pinkish-orange color, are nestled naturally on top. The shrimp are not sliced. A generous sprinkling of golden-brown toasted cashew halves adds contrasting crunch. Freshly chopped green chives or parsley are scattered over the dish, providing a pop of color. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, allowing textures and colors to shine. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting enhances the inviting appearance.

ingredients.name: Raw Cashews, halved or roughly chopped
Fresh Parsley or Chives, finely chopped

instructions: Toast cashews: Preheat a dry pan over medium heat. Add cashews. Toast for 3-5 minutes until golden and fragrant. Stir frequently. Remove and set aside.
Prepare shrimp: Pat shrimp dry. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Sear shrimp: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add shrimp in a single layer. Sear for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and cooked through. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove shrimp and set aside.

Start risotto base: In the same pan (or a separate heavy-bottomed pot), add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice: Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 1-2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.

Add stock: Begin adding hot stock, one ladleful (about 120ml) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until liquid is almost fully absorbed before adding the next ladleful. Continue this process for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.

Finish risotto: Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter, crumbled blue cheese, and heavy cream. Stir vigorously until cheese is melted and risotto is creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Combine and serve: Gently fold seared shrimp into the risotto.
Plate immediately in wide, shallow bowls. Garnish generously with toasted cashews and fresh chopped parsley or chives.
notes: Ensure risotto remains fluid and creamy, not stiff. Adjust stock quantity as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Mandarin Dark Chocolate Almond Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably crafted Mandarin Dark Chocolate Almond Entremet is centered on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a delicate gold rim. The entremet boasts a flawless, high-gloss dark chocolate mirror glaze, reflecting the ambient light with architectural precision. Its geometric shape is sharp, showcasing the clean lines of a perfectly molded individual pastry. A single, precisely placed, golden-brown candied almond shard stands elegantly on the glaze, accompanied by a vibrant, miniature mandarin segment and a scatter of dark, glossy cocoa nibs. These few, deliberate garnishes enhance visual appeal without clutter. The composition features abundant negative space on the plate, emphasizing the pastry as the singular focal point. The setting is a haute patisserie shop, with the plate resting on a pristine white marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the plate. Dramatic, professional lighting creates deep shadows, highlighting the entremet's textures and contours. The background is ultra-minimalist and out of focus, ensuring maximum visual impact on the exquisite dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
For the Almond Dacquoise: Sift almond flour, powdered sugar, and cocoa powder together. Set aside.
Whip aquafaba with cream of tartar until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold dry ingredients into whipped aquafaba until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spread mixture thinly onto prepared baking sheet. Bake 12-15 minutes until set. Cool completely. Cut into four 6cm diameter circles.
For the Mandarin-Cinnamon Confit: Combine mandarin juice, zest, sugar, cornstarch, and cinnamon stick in a saucepan.
Whisk constantly over medium heat until mixture thickens and boils. Remove cinnamon stick.
Pour confit into four small silicone molds (approx. 4cm diameter). Freeze until solid, at least 2 hours.
For the Dark Chocolate Mousse: Melt 150g dark chocolate over a double boiler. Let cool slightly.
Whip chilled coconut cream until light and fluffy.
Whip 80ml aquafaba until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold melted chocolate into whipped coconut cream. Then fold in whipped aquafaba and vanilla extract until smooth.
For Assembly: Place a dacquoise circle at the bottom of four individual entremet molds (approx. 7cm diameter, 5cm high).
Pipe a layer of chocolate mousse into each mold. Place a frozen mandarin confit insert in the center.
Cover with more chocolate mousse, filling molds to the top. Smooth the surface. Freeze entremets for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For the Mirror Glaze: Melt remaining 50g dark chocolate.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, 40g granulated sugar, and 15g cocoa powder. Bring to a simmer.
Remove from heat. Add melted chocolate and 15g cornstarch. Whisk until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Let glaze cool to 30-35°C (86-95°F).
To Finish: Unmold frozen entremets onto a wire rack placed over a baking sheet.
Pour mirror glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off.
Carefully transfer glazed entremets to serving plates. Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for 30-45 minutes.
For Garnish: Lightly toast flaked almonds. Cut small, precise segments from a fresh mandarin.
Place a few toasted flaked almonds, a tiny mandarin segment, and a sprinkle of cocoa nibs on each entremet for decoration.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Lamb Rump with Crispy Roasted Potatoes, Pea Puree, and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rosemary Lamb Rump is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, set on a simple light wooden table. The seared lamb rump, a whole succulent piece with a golden-brown crust and a hint of pink interior, is the centerpiece. Beside it, a neat scoop of fluffy brown rice adds an earthy contrast. A vibrant green, smooth pea puree is artfully dolloped near the lamb, its creamy texture visible. Golden-brown, crispy roasted potato chunks are strategically placed around the lamb, showcasing their irregular, rustic shapes. A fresh sprig of rosemary rests atop the lamb, providing a touch of green garnish. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the natural colors and textures of each component. Standard European flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are positioned beside the plate, completing the professional yet approachable casual dining aesthetic under soft, natural lighting.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800g, peeled and cut into 2cm chunks or wedges

instructions: Rinse 200g brown rice. Cook according to package instructions. Simmer until water absorbed and rice is tender, about 35-40 minutes. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Place potato chunks in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender but not breaking apart. Drain well. Toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 30-40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crispy.

Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add 300g frozen peas. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender. Drain immediately and transfer to a blender. Add 50g butter, 100ml stock, and a pinch of salt. Blend until smooth. Adjust seasoning. Keep warm.

Score the fat side of each lamb rump in a crisscross pattern. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe frying pan over medium-high heat. Place lamb rumps fat-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until fat is golden and crispy. Turn and sear remaining sides for 2-3 minutes. Add 4 sprigs of fresh rosemary and 4 crushed garlic cloves to the pan. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 8-12 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 55-60°C). Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove lamb from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Cover loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Place a scoop of brown rice on one side of a white porcelain plate. Arrange 1 piece of rested lamb rump next to the rice. Spoon a dollop or spread of pea puree on the plate. Arrange a portion of crispy roasted potato chunks around the lamb and puree. Garnish the lamb with a small sprig of fresh rosemary.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Tofu Goulash with Beer and Rice
recipes.visual_description: The Tofu Goulash is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base. Rich, reddish-brown goulash is spooned over the rice, showcasing seared 2 cm tofu cubes nestled within the thick, glossy tomato-paprika sauce. Diced onions and visible specks of caraway seeds add texture and depth to the sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware (fork and knife) are placed beside the plate. A small white ramekin with a dollop of plant-based sour cream is placed nearby. Natural, soft, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and rustic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of plant-based sour cream or yogurt.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in large pot over medium-high heat. Sear tofu cubes until golden brown on all sides. Remove tofu from pot.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil to pot. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, caraway seeds, and cayenne pepper. Cook 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Pour in beer. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Simmer 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared tofu to pot. Stir gently to combine.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 25-30 minutes until sauce thickens and flavors meld.
Meanwhile, cook rice according to package directions.
Remove bay leaf from goulash. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot tofu goulash over cooked rice. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Lamb Loin with Rosemary Potatoes and Pea Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Lamb Loin with Rosemary Potatoes and Pea Puree is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, golden-brown roasted lamb loin chunks are arranged centrally. Alongside are several crisp-edged, fluffy rosemary potato wedges. A vibrant green, smooth pea puree is spooned neatly beside the lamb and potatoes. A small, inviting mound of earthy brown rice completes the ensemble. The dish exhibits natural, balanced colors: the rich brown of the lamb, golden potatoes, and bright green puree, complemented by the subtle brown of the rice. A fresh sprig of rosemary garnishes the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil
Offer crusty bread for dipping in any pan juices
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat lamb loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 20 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear lamb loin on all sides until golden brown. This takes about 2-3 minutes per side.

Transfer lamb loin to the preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Internal temperature should reach 63°C for medium-rare. Let rest 10 minutes before slicing.
While lamb roasts, wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Toss with 20 ml olive oil, 2 sprigs chopped rosemary, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes on a baking tray. Roast in the same oven as the lamb for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and golden brown.
Cook brown rice according to package instructions. Usually 1 part rice to 2 parts water, simmered until water absorbed.
For pea puree, blanch frozen green peas in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain well.
Transfer peas to a food processor. Add 10 ml olive oil, butter, 1 sprig chopped rosemary, and chicken stock. Process until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut rested lamb loin into thick 3-4 cm chunks.
Portion lamb chunks, roasted potato wedges, pea puree, and brown rice onto plates. Garnish with fresh rosemary sprigs.
notes: Adjust lamb roasting time based on desired doneness. Use a meat thermometer for accuracy.
The pea puree can be thinned with more stock or water if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle, Butternut Squash, and Cannellini Beans
recipes.visual_description: A rich, rustic Italian braised beef ragu is generously plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Wide pappardelle pasta strands are thoroughly coated in the deep reddish-brown sauce. Tender, shredded beef chunks are visibly intertwined with the pasta. Soft, earthy-toned 2cm cubes of butternut squash and creamy white cannellini beans are scattered throughout. The sauce has a moderate sheen. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese and vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnish the dish. The plating is natural and abundant, showcasing the ragu's hearty texture. The dish sits on a simple wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and a traditional fork are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table
Pair with a robust red wine

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Cut beef into 4-5cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until well browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add pancetta to the pot. Cook until crisp. Remove pancetta, leaving fat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
During the last 45 minutes of braising, add butternut squash cubes to the pot. Stir gently.
In the last 15 minutes, stir in drained cannellini beans.
Remove rosemary, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Shred beef with two forks directly in the pot. Stir to combine.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat.
Serve hot, garnished with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The ragu can be made ahead and reheated; flavors often improve overnight
Adjust consistency with a little pasta water if needed when tossing with pasta

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage & Broccoli Crostini with Apple Mostarda
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant, bite-sized crostini are artfully arranged on a clean, rectangular white porcelain platter. Each crostini features a golden-brown toasted baguette slice as its base. A generous mound of finely crumbled, browned Italian sausage is layered on top, interspersed with vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. Small, glistening cubes of amber-hued apple mostarda are delicately placed atop the sausage and broccoli, adding a touch of sweetness and shine. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a scattering of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley provide the finishing garnish. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with thoughtful negative space between each piece. The platter rests on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, set against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Arrange on baking sheet. Drizzle with 10ml olive oil. Bake 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.

Heat 10ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook 8-10 minutes until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from pan. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.

Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in the same pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add blanched broccoli florets. Sauté 3-4 minutes until lightly charred. Season with salt and pepper. Add cooked sausage back to the pan. Toss to combine. Set aside.

Peel and dice apple into small 0.5 cm cubes. In a small saucepan, combine diced apple, Dijon mustard, white wine vinegar, honey, and 30ml water. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are tender and liquid reduces to a glaze. Season with a pinch of salt.
To assemble, spoon the sausage and broccoli mixture onto each toasted crostini. Top each with a small amount of apple mostarda. Garnish with grated Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh chopped parsley.
Arrange 8-12 finished crostini on a serving platter.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Sausage, Broccoli, and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente orecchiette pasta forms the base, tossed with crumbled, golden-brown Italian sausage and vibrant green broccoli florets. The dish exhibits a harmonious blend of textures: the firm bite of pasta, the tender crispness of broccoli, and the savory chew of the sausage. A light, glossy sauce coats the ingredients, reflecting natural light. The overall color palette is warm, with the deep green of broccoli contrasting against the rich brown of the sausage and the pale yellow of the pasta. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano adorns the top, adding a creamy white highlight. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded neutral-toned cotton napkin and classic silver flatware placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and emphasizing the food's freshness. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a light red wine.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cut broccoli into small florets.
Add orecchiette to boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Add broccoli florets to pasta water during the last 3 minutes of pasta cooking.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage into skillet.
Cook sausage, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to sausage. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Drain pasta and broccoli, reserving 250ml pasta water.
Add pasta and broccoli to sausage skillet.
Whisk Dijon mustard into chicken broth (or reserved pasta water). Pour into skillet.
Toss everything to combine. Cook 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Add more pasta water if needed for consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes for desired spice level.
Using reserved pasta water helps create a cohesive sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Scallop Carbonara with Crispy Pancetta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Scallop Carbonara is artfully presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden linguine, perfectly coated in a glossy, emulsified egg and Pecorino Romano sauce, forms a nest in the center. The pasta strands are glistening, showcasing their al dente texture. Scattered among the pasta are several plump, seared scallops, their surfaces a rich golden-brown with a delicate crust, contrasting beautifully with their pearly white interiors. Small, crispy cubes of rendered pancetta are interspersed throughout, adding pops of deep amber and texture. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley crowns the dish, alongside a dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's rich colors—golden pasta, brown scallops, and green parsley—and inviting textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic European flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a crisp white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, pat scallops dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
In a large skillet, cook diced pancetta over medium heat until crispy and rendered. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon, leaving rendered fat in the skillet. Set crispy pancetta aside.
Add olive oil and minced garlic to the skillet with pancetta fat. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant. Remove garlic from skillet to prevent burning.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add scallops to the hot skillet in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and opaque. Remove scallops from skillet and set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk together egg yolks, whole egg, grated Pecorino Romano, and a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper.
Immediately after draining pasta, add it to the skillet with the rendered pancetta fat. Toss to coat.
Slowly add reserved hot pasta water, about 60ml at a time, to the egg mixture while whisking constantly. This tempers the eggs.

Pour the tempered egg mixture over the hot pasta in the skillet. Quickly toss vigorously with tongs to create a creamy sauce. Add more pasta water, 30ml at a time, if needed to achieve desired consistency. The heat from the pasta will cook the eggs into a sauce, not scrambled.
Gently fold in crispy pancetta and seared scallops.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Pecorino Romano.
notes: Ensure scallops are very dry before searing for a good crust.
The key to carbonara is to temper the egg mixture with hot pasta water and toss quickly to prevent scrambling.
Use high-quality Pecorino Romano for authentic flavor.
traditional_techniques: Emulsification of egg and cheese with pasta water to create the carbonara sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Kidney Bean and Jalapeno Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Kidney Bean and Jalapeno Salad is mounded casually on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Vibrant red kidney beans form the base, mixed with finely diced red bell pepper, crisp white onion, and bright green chopped cilantro. Small, crumbled pieces of seasoned ground beef are subtly interspersed, adding savory depth without dominating. Thin slices of pickled jalapeno chilies provide tangy accents. Golden-brown, irregularly shaped bread croutons are scattered generously over the top, adding crucial crunch. The salad is lightly coated in a glossy, reddish vinaigrette. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple fork and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm kitchen light illuminates the scene, evoking a comfortable, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. Focus is on natural colors and varied textures of this hearty, homely salad.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a hearty side dish or light main meal.
Can be accompanied by a simple glass of iced tea or lemonade.
Often enjoyed during casual family gatherings or backyard cookouts.
instructions: Drain and rinse kidney beans thoroughly. Set aside.
Cut bread into 1.5 cm cubes for croutons. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add bread cubes and toast until golden and crisp. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan, crumble ground beef. Cook over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat. Season beef with cumin, chili powder, salt, and black pepper. Stir well. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine drained kidney beans, chopped pickled jalapenos, diced red onion, diced red bell pepper, and chopped cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, hot sauce, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
Add cooked ground beef to the bean and vegetable mixture. Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all ingredients and coat evenly.
Serve the Kidney Bean and Jalapeno Salad immediately, topped with the toasted bread croutons.

recipes.recipe_name: Fennel, Mushroom, and Blood Orange Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl, showcasing its creamy, fluid consistency. The al dente rice is coated in a luscious, pale orange-hued sauce. Tender, earthy sliced mushrooms and translucent, slightly softened fennel slices are scattered throughout. Bright segments of blood orange, their deep ruby and orange tones contrasting with the risotto, are artfully placed on top. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley and delicate rosemary sprigs add fresh color and aromatic appeal. The dish is framed by a simple wooden table surface, with a crisp white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. Traditional European-style flatware rests beside the plate. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately.
Pair with a crisp dry white wine.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Heat broth in a saucepan. Keep it hot.

Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Trim fennel bulbs; thinly slice half, finely dice the other half. Clean mushrooms; slice thinly. Zest one blood orange. Segment both blood oranges, reserving any juice. Squeeze remaining orange halves for juice.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced fennel. Cook for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Add rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until grains are translucent at edges. Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Add one ladle of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After about 10 minutes of cooking the risotto, add sliced mushrooms and sliced fennel to the pot. Continue adding broth and stirring.
When rice is al dente, remove from heat. Stir in butter, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, and blood orange juice. Stir vigorously to create a creamy, fluid consistency (mantecatura).
Stir in chopped fresh rosemary. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle risotto into warm bowls. Garnish with blood orange segments, fresh chopped parsley, and blood orange zest.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Pineapple Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of spaghetti, lightly coated in a glossy, savory-sweet garlic sauce, forms the base. Golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast chunks are artfully placed on top of the pasta. Roasted pineapple wedges, exhibiting slight caramelization on their edges, are arranged around the chicken, creating visual balance and vibrant color contrast. A light drizzle of the pan sauce coats the entire dish, enhancing its sheen. Fresh green scallions, thinly sliced on the bias, are scattered over the top. A bright lime wedge rests on the side of the plate. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and a fork are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant-style background. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let rest 5 minutes. Cut into thick chunks.
While chicken cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Cut pineapple into 2 cm thick wedges or chunks. Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the same skillet. Add pineapple. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until caramelized.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the skillet with pineapple. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, cornstarch, and 30 ml water. Pour sauce mixture into the skillet. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Add drained pasta and cooked chicken chunks to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired sauce consistency.
Plate pasta with chicken and pineapple. Garnish with sliced scallions and a lime wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Macaroni with Spicy Sausage and Chard
recipes.visual_description: The baked macaroni dish is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion. Golden-brown melted mozzarella forms a rustic crust over the top. Beneath, tender macaroni noodles are coated in a rich, savory red tomato sauce. Visible elements include substantial, browned chunks of Italian sausage, vibrant green wilted Swiss chard leaves, and bright green, thinly sliced pickled jalapeno rings scattered throughout, adding color and a hint of zest. A few fresh basil leaves are torn and placed on top for garnish. The dish rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the comforting textures and rich colors, highlighting the hearty appeal of this Italian-American comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Swiss chard, stems removed and leaves chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage. Break up the sausage into chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage from skillet, leaving rendered fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add chopped Swiss chard to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 3-5 minutes.
Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Add cooked macaroni and pickled jalapeno slices. Stir to combine.
Stir in half of the mozzarella cheese and half of the Parmesan cheese.
Smooth the top of the macaroni mixture. Sprinkle remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and the dish is heated through.
Garnish with fresh torn basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Sesame Chicken and Eggplant Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spicy Sesame Chicken and Eggplant Noodles is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The egg noodles, tossed in a rich, glossy brown sauce, form a loose mound at the center. Scattered throughout are generous, irregular chunks of seared chicken, displaying golden-brown crusts and moist interiors. Cubes of tender, slightly charred eggplant show soft, purplish skin and creamy flesh. Bright red bell pepper strips and vibrant green spring onion slices are interspersed, adding pops of color and freshness. A light sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds garnishes the top. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface with a white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a relaxed atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks
Offer a side of chili oil for extra heat
instructions: Slice chicken into 2 cm chunks.
Cut eggplant into 2 cm cubes.
Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, chili garlic sauce, brown sugar, cornstarch, and chicken broth in a bowl. Whisk well. Set aside.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add eggplant cubes. Stir-fry 5-7 minutes until tender and slightly browned.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced red bell pepper to the wok. Stir-fry 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook 1-2 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Add cooked egg noodles to the wok. Toss gently to coat everything with sauce.
Stir in most of the sliced spring onions.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining spring onions and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Maíz y Pimientos Rostizados
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant main course featuring seared chicken chunks, roasted bell pepper strips, and sweet corn kernels, arranged naturally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is golden-brown and tender, cut into 3-4 cm chunks. The bell peppers, cut into 1 cm wide strips, display bright red, yellow, and orange hues with slight charring, offering a soft yet firm texture. The corn kernels are plump and brightly yellow. All elements are lightly coated in a savory, glistening sauce. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green cilantro leaves scattered over the top and a lime wedge placed to the side. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin beside the plate, and natural, even lighting, creating an inviting and authentic Mexican dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Salsa roja
Crema
Fresh avocado slices

ingredients.name: Bell peppers (red, yellow, or orange)
ingredients.quantity: 2 large (approx. 400 g total), cut into 1 cm wide strips

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt, black pepper, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add sliced onion and bell pepper strips to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly charred.
Stir in minced garlic, dried oregano, and corn kernels. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid. Simmer uncovered for 2-3 minutes to slightly reduce sauce, if desired. Stir in fresh lime juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Verjus-Ginger Glaze and Coriander Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A mound of fluffy basmati rice, infused with finely diced ginger and speckled with vibrant green chopped coriander, is neatly placed on one side. A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, approximately 180g, is sliced into thick, uniform medallions and arranged beside the rice. A glossy, amber-hued verjus-ginger glaze is generously spooned over the chicken, creating a delicate sheen. A few fresh coriander sprigs are artfully placed on the chicken for a fresh garnish. The setting includes a stainless steel fork and knife, and a folded white cotton napkin, with natural, even lighting illuminating the food.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rice, 500ml chicken stock, 20g finely diced ginger, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in chopped coriander.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, let rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté finely diced shallots and 20g grated ginger over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Deglaze skillet with verjus. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce heat and simmer until verjus has reduced by half.
Add 100ml chicken stock. Continue to simmer and reduce until the sauce slightly thickens to a glaze consistency.
Remove from heat. Whisk in unsalted butter until melted and incorporated, creating a glossy glaze. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions. Plate a portion of coriander rice. Arrange chicken medallions beside the rice. Spoon Verjus-Ginger Glaze generously over the chicken. Garnish with a few fresh coriander leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Chana Masala with Basmati Rice
recipes.visual_description: The Authentic Chana Masala is presented in a deep white porcelain katori (bowl), showcasing its rich, reddish-brown hue. The chickpeas, plump and tender, are generously coated in a thick, glossy, aromatic gravy, flecked with finely diced onions and vibrant green specks of fresh coriander. A small, vibrant mound of fluffy white basmati rice, with distinct, separate grains, sits directly on the white porcelain plate beside the curry katori. A separate, smaller white porcelain katori holds a dollop of creamy, pale green cucumber raita, garnished with a light sprinkle of roasted cumin powder. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The dish rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and a traditional Indian serving spoon rest beside the plate. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the texture of the chickpeas and the sheen of the curry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with fluffy basmati rice
Accompanied by warm naan bread
Paired with a cooling cucumber raita
instructions: Rinse basmati rice under cold water until clear. Combine rice, 500ml water, and 5g salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
In a small bowl, combine yogurt, finely grated or small diced cucumber, roasted cumin powder, and a pinch of salt. Mix well. Chill until serving.
Heat oil or ghee in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds. Sauté until fragrant and crackling, about 30 seconds.
Add finely diced onions. Cook, stirring frequently, until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in grated ginger, minced garlic, and green chilies. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes. Increase heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens and oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add drained chickpeas and 250ml water or vegetable broth. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir occasionally.
Stir in garam masala, amchur powder, and half of the chopped fresh coriander. Season with salt to taste. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes.
Ladle Chana Masala into serving bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh coriander. Serve hot with fluffy basmati rice and a side of cucumber raita.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty stew sits in a wide, shallow cream-colored ceramic bowl on a rustic oak table. The dish features large 3cm chunks of golden-seared chicken and 2cm cubes of tender yellow potatoes. Slices of brown mushrooms and bright green peas are distributed throughout the glossy, thick savory sauce. The arrangement is casual and homestyle, with ingredients naturally overlapping. A single sprig of fresh thyme rests on top. To the side, a thick piece of crusty bread sits on a small plate next to a heavy stainless steel spoon and a folded linen napkin. Warm, soft kitchen light illuminates the textures of the meat and vegetables, creating a cozy atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices
Pair with a simple green side salad
Serve in deep ceramic bowls

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 3cm chunks
Yellow potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken in batches until golden.
Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add butter to the same pot.
Sauté onion and mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Slowly pour in chicken stock while stirring.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add potatoes and thyme sprigs.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Ensure potatoes are fork-tender.
Stir in green peas and cook for 2 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and remove thyme sprigs.
notes: Do not overcook the peas to maintain their bright green color
Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during simmering
Ensure the sauce coats the back of a spoon before serving

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Lemon Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared cod fillet rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing its golden-brown, lightly crisp crust. The cod is presented as a whole, thick piece, its flaky white interior peeking slightly where the fillet naturally separates. Alongside the cod, a neat bundle of vibrant green asparagus spears is arranged, cooked to a tender-crisp texture. A glossy, pale yellow lemon butter sauce is generously spooned over the cod and asparagus, glistening under natural, even lighting. The sauce pools slightly around the base of the cod, indicating its fluid consistency. Bright green specks of fresh chopped parsley are scattered across the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A fresh lemon wedge, cut lengthwise, is placed beside the cod, ready for a final squeeze. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro ambiance. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant setting. The composition is balanced, allowing for appropriate negative space, highlighting the fresh ingredients and refined cooking.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock or dry white wine

instructions: Pat cod fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Trim woody ends from asparagus.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place cod fillets in skillet. Sear 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy.
Flip cod. Cook 3-4 minutes until flaky and opaque. Remove cod. Keep warm.
Add butter to the same skillet. Melt over medium heat.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock or white wine. Simmer 1 minute.
Squeeze in juice from 1 lemon. Stir well. Stir in chopped parsley. Remove from heat.
Steam or blanch asparagus 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with salt.
Plate cod fillets. Arrange asparagus alongside.
Spoon lemon butter sauce over cod and asparagus.
Garnish with fresh lemon wedges. Serve immediately.
notes: Use fresh, high-quality cod for best results. Adjust cooking time based on fillet thickness.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Chicken and Red Lentil Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion served in a traditional shallow stainless steel bowl or a rustic ceramic bowl. The dish features thick, creamy red lentils that have softened into a golden-yellow consistency. Nestled into the lentils are four large, moist chunks of seared chicken showing browned edges. The surface is finished with a light drizzle of melted ghee and a pinch of red chili powder. Fresh, roughly torn green cilantro leaves are scattered over the top. Beside the bowl sits a single folded warm roti. The lighting is warm and domestic, set on a dark wooden kitchen table with a simple cloth napkin. The entire arrangement is captured from a top-down angle, showing the natural textures of the legumes.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm roti or steamed basmati rice
Include a side of plain yogurt or raita
Add a small spoonful of mango pickle
instructions: Dice chicken into 3cm chunks.
Rinse red lentils under cold water until clear.
Heat oil in a small pot over medium heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté onion in the same pot until translucent.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in turmeric, cumin, and garam masala.
Add lentils and water to the pot.
Return chicken chunks to the pot.
Simmer for 20 minutes until lentils are soft and creamy.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in salt and lemon juice.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Red lentils cook faster than green or brown varieties and create a creamy texture.
Adjust chili powder if a spicier profile is desired.
Ensure the chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Paprika Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: Seared chicken chunks, vibrant diced bell peppers, and fluffy, paprika-tinted rice are naturally mounded on a simple, round ceramic plate. The chicken pieces are golden-brown and tender, nestled amongst the distinct red and yellow bell pepper dices. The rice is fully cooked, absorbing the rich flavors, displaying a warm, inviting hue from the paprika. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a final touch of color. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with a plain cloth napkin and a simple fork alongside. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene, capturing the comforting, homemade essence of the meal.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides, about 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion and bell peppers into 1.5 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Add onion and bell peppers to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to lightly toast the rice.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Distribute evenly within the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly with a lid. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
Remove skillet from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Corn Mini Tostadas
recipes.visual_description: Smoky Chipotle Corn Mini Tostadas are presented on a rustic terra cotta platter, showcasing 10-12 small, round tostadas. Each tostada features a crisp, golden-brown corn tortilla base, approximately 6 cm in diameter. Piled generously on top is a vibrant, savory corn mixture. The corn kernels are golden yellow, mixed with finely diced red chipotle, subtle bits of green cilantro, and a hint of smoky red paprika. Some corn kernels show slight charring, indicating a quick sauté. The texture contrast is evident between the firm, crisp tortilla and the soft, slightly creamy corn topping. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro leaves adorns each tostada. Fresh lime wedges are casually placed on the platter for squeezing. The entire arrangement is natural and inviting, reflecting a homely Mexican kitchen, under warm, soft lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for an added burst of citrus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut corn tortillas into 6 cm rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet.
Brush tortilla rounds lightly with olive oil. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove from oven.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in corn kernels, minced chipotle, and smoked paprika. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until corn is tender and slightly browned.
Season corn mixture with salt and black pepper. Stir in fresh lime juice.
Spoon corn mixture onto each crisp tortilla round.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Smoked Paprika Chicken and Rice is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The dish features tender, browned chicken in thick chunks, nestled within moist, reddish-orange long-grain rice. Diced red bell pepper pieces and vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are visibly integrated throughout the rice, adding color and texture. The rice has a natural, slightly loose consistency, not overly dry or clumped. The overall plating is natural and comforting, with components touching or slightly overlapping. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Simple, everyday flatware (a sturdy fork and spoon) is casually placed beside the bowl. A cream-colored cloth napkin is folded loosely nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting.

ingredients.name: Light lager or pale ale beer

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and minced chili to the pan. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
