Prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, and sake (if using). Add 5ml of toasted sesame oil. Set aside.
Pat tuna fillets dry with paper towels. Season tuna with salt and black pepper.

Heat 10ml of toasted sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear tuna fillets for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness. Remove tuna from pan and set aside.

Add remaining 5ml of toasted sesame oil to the same pan. Add sliced onion and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and broccoli florets. Sauté for another 5-7 minutes until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Pour the prepared sauce into the pan with the vegetables. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring to coat vegetables.

To serve, divide cooked brown rice into two donburi bowls. Place one seared tuna fillet on top of the rice in each bowl. Spoon the sautéed broccoli and onion mixture with sauce over the tuna and rice.
Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust tuna cooking time to your preferred doneness.
Brown rice can be cooked in advance to save time.

recipes.recipe_name: Catalan Honey-Glazed Chicken with Shichimi & Garlic Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Catalan Honey-Glazed Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A whole, un-sliced chicken thigh, golden-brown with a crispy, slightly sticky skin from the honey-shichimi glaze, is positioned centrally. The glaze is a rich reddish-brown, glistening under natural light. A creamy, off-white garlic cream sauce pools elegantly around the base of the chicken, offering a smooth contrast to the textured meat. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and a light dusting of red shichimi togarashi for a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a neutral cotton napkin beside it. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting. The presentation is clean, professional, and highlights the dish's warmth and refined simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer crusty bread (Pan de Pagès) to sop up the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Shichimi Togarashi
ingredients.quantity: 5 g (approx. 1 tsp), plus more for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and 2g (approx. 0.5 tsp) shichimi togarashi.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Do not move chicken during searing.
Flip chicken. Sear for 2 minutes on the flesh side.
Remove chicken from pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add 3 minced garlic cloves to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with sake. Scrape up any browned bits. Stir in honey and remaining 3g (approx. 0.5 tsp) shichimi togarashi. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Spoon the glaze over the chicken.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
While chicken roasts, prepare garlic cream. In a small saucepan, melt clotted cream over medium-low heat. Add remaining 3 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced and thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove saucepan from heat. Whisk egg yolk into the cream mixture until fully incorporated and sauce is smooth.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Plate one chicken thigh per serving. Spoon garlic cream around the chicken. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and a light sprinkle of shichimi togarashi.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
The egg yolk adds richness and slight thickening to the cream; ensure the cream is off the heat when whisking it in to prevent scrambling.

recipes.recipe_name: North African Spiced Roast Chicken with Caramelized Sweet Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of North African Spiced Roast Chicken sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, roasted whole, is the focal point. Alongside it are several caramelized sweet potato wedges, their edges slightly charred, displaying warm orange and deep brown tones. Whole roasted garlic cloves, softened and golden, are interspersed among the sweet potatoes. The dish is garnished generously with vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The chicken and sweet potatoes are arranged naturally, showcasing their textures. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of couscous or flatbread.
Offer harissa on the side for added spice.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, combine 30 mL olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Rub spice mixture generously over chicken.
Peel sweet potatoes. Cut into 3 cm thick wedges.
Peel garlic cloves. Leave whole.
On a large baking tray, toss sweet potato wedges and whole garlic cloves with remaining 30 mL olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Arrange spiced chicken thighs on the same baking tray among the sweet potatoes and garlic. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip sweet potatoes and garlic. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust spice levels to personal preference.
For extra crisp skin, broil for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Sweet Potato and Thyme-Garlic Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its beautifully seared crust. Beside it, a generous swirl of vibrant orange, creamy sweet potato puree provides a soft, inviting contrast. A rich, glossy brown thyme-garlic jus is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the plate, pooling elegantly. A few whole, tender confit garlic cloves are placed near the chicken. The dish is garnished simply with a fresh green thyme sprig, adding a touch of natural color. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual yet refined restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Peel garlic cloves. Place cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Cook on very low heat for 20-25 minutes. Garlic should be soft and golden. Do not brown. Remove garlic cloves. Reserve oil.

Peel and dice sweet potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash or pass through a ricer. Stir in heavy cream, 30g butter, and 2-3 confit garlic cloves (mashed). Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts in hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Return skillet to medium heat. Add remaining 15g butter. Add remaining thyme sprigs and 2-3 mashed confit garlic cloves. Sauté 1 minute. Deglaze pan with chicken stock. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes, until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper. Strain for a smoother jus, or leave as is.

Spoon a generous portion of sweet potato puree onto each plate. Place a whole seared chicken breast beside the puree. Drizzle thyme-garlic jus over and around the chicken. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Earthy Harvest Kofta with Fermented Squash Puree and Apple-Onion Quickle
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone, resting on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. The dish features a smooth, creamy base of vibrant orange fermented butternut squash puree, spread in a natural, organic shape on one side of the plate, leaving ample white space. Three or four golden-brown, seared beef and sausage kofta, retaining their natural oblong shape, are artfully arranged atop the puree, slightly overlapping. Their rich, caramelized crust contrasts with the soft puree. Adjacent to the kofta, a small, neat mound of thinly sliced, translucent quick-pickled red onion and pale apple shimmers, providing a delicate pink and white accent. A few crisp, dark green mixed salad leaves are strategically placed near the kofta and quickle, offering a fresh, verdant touch. The composition is clean, unforced, and celebrates the natural textures and colors of each ingredient. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the subtle sheen on the kofta and the freshness of the greens. The background is minimal, perhaps showing a hint of a natural plant or an undyed linen napkin in a complementary beige, maintaining an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic. No ornate garnishes or rigid patterns are used; the focus is on the pure beauty and simplicity of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Potato, finely grated and squeezed dry
Butternut squash, peeled, deseeded, cut into 3 cm cubes
Fresh herbs (e.g., parsley, cilantro), for garnish

instructions: Prepare Apple-Onion Quickle: In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced apple and red onion in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Prepare Fermented Squash Puree: In a large pot, combine squash cubes, chopped onion, and smashed garlic. Add enough vegetable stock to cover. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer until squash is very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain most liquid, reserving some. Transfer squash mixture to a blender. Add fermented chili paste if using. Blend until very smooth, adding reserved stock as needed to reach a creamy consistency. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Kofta: In a large bowl, combine beef mince, sausage meat, grated onion, grated potato, fermented chili paste, grated ginger, minced garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined. Form into 12-16 oval or cylindrical kofta shapes.

Cook Kofta: Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Carefully place kofta in the pan. Cook, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Assemble Dish: Spoon a generous portion of warm fermented squash puree onto each of four plates, creating a clean base. Arrange 3-4 cooked kofta on top of the puree. Place a small mound of quick-pickled apple and onion next to the kofta. Garnish with a few fresh salad greens and a sprig of fresh herb if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: Use squash peels, seeds, and apple/onion cores/peels to make a quick vegetable stock for the puree or other recipes.
Any leftover quickle liquid can be used in salad dressings.
Trimmed greens can be added to the stock pot.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Corn Enchiladas with Ancho Chili Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Three plump, golden-baked chicken and corn enchiladas, generously coated in a rich, glossy ancho chili sauce, are arranged side-by-side on a clean white porcelain plate. The melted Oaxaca cheese forms a bubbly, inviting crust atop the deep red-brown sauce. Beside them, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, exhibiting subtle charring, are neatly clustered. A dollop of cool, white crema Mexicana sits next to the enchiladas, offering a textural contrast. Freshly chopped cilantro leaves are scattered across the dish, adding a pop of color. The presentation is balanced and approachable, set on a simple wooden surface with a subtle background of a ceramic salsa bowl and a stack of warm tortillas, all bathed in natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Mexican rice or refried beans.
instructions: Rehydrate ancho chilies: Place dried ancho chilies in a heatproof bowl. Cover with boiling water. Let soak for 20 minutes until softened. Drain, remove stems and seeds.

Cook chicken: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5 minutes per side until golden. Reduce heat, cover, and cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove, cool slightly, then shred using two forks.

Prepare filling: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté half of the diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves for 3 minutes until softened. Add corn kernels. Cook 5 minutes until tender. Stir in shredded chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.

Make ancho chili sauce: In a blender, combine rehydrated ancho chilies, remaining diced onion, remaining 2 minced garlic cloves, chicken broth, tomato paste, cumin, and oregano. Blend until smooth. Pour sauce into a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Season with salt.

Assemble enchiladas: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish. Briefly dip each corn tortilla into the warm ancho chili sauce to soften. Place about 60g of chicken-corn filling down the center of each tortilla. Sprinkle with a small amount of shredded cheese. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the baking dish. Repeat with remaining tortillas and filling.
Bake enchiladas: Pour remaining ancho chili sauce evenly over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle generously with remaining shredded cheese. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden.

Roast broccoli: While enchiladas bake, toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven for 15-20 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Serve: Arrange 3 enchiladas per plate alongside a portion of roasted broccoli. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a dollop of crema Mexicana.
notes: For spicier sauce, add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the ancho chili sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Pork Medallions with White Chocolate-Miso Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving on a clean white porcelain plate centered on a light wooden table. Two golden-brown pan-seared pork medallions, 2-3cm thick, are artfully leaned against a smooth, pale rose-kissed potato purée. A rich, glossy dark white chocolate-miso glaze is generously drizzled over the pork. Scattered around the dish are glistening caramelized raisins, providing a contrasting ruby hue and texture. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green chives adds a vibrant color pop. The composition has moderate negative space, appearing professional yet approachable. A neatly folded cotton napkin and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rest beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's textures and colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served alongside a small bowl of steamed short-grain rice
Accompanied by a light dashi-based soup
instructions: Cut pork tenderloin into 8 medallions, approximately 2-3cm thick. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Peel potatoes and cut into 3cm chunks. Place in a pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot. Add 30g unsalted butter, heavy cream, and rosewater. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.
In a small saucepan, combine red miso paste, mirin, sake, and soy sauce. Whisk until smooth. Set aside.
In a separate small saucepan over low heat, melt white chocolate, marshmallows, and remaining 30g unsalted butter, stirring constantly until smooth. Do not boil.
Gradually whisk the melted white chocolate mixture into the miso mixture until fully combined and glossy. Keep warm over very low heat.

Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add pork medallions and sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove pork from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
In the same pan (add a tiny bit more oil if needed), add raisins. Cook over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly plumped and caramelized.

To plate, place a central mound of rose-kissed potato purée on each plate. Lean two pork medallions against the purée. Generously spoon the white chocolate-miso glaze over the pork. Scatter caramelized raisins around the dish. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: This dish balances rich savory flavors with subtle sweetness and aromatic notes, showcasing a modern Japanese approach to fusion cuisine.
The marshmallows in the glaze provide body and a unique gloss, not an overt sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with White Chocolate Miso Glaze and Crispy Potato Cakes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a balanced and refined composition typical of casual Japanese dining. Two plump, pan-seared pork loin medallions, exhibiting a beautiful golden-brown crust and a tender, juicy interior, are positioned slightly off-center. Beside them sit two perfectly golden-brown, crispy potato cakes, their exteriors showing a delicate crispness. A glossy, rich White Chocolate Miso Glaze is artfully drizzled over the pork and gently swirled around the plate, its creamy hue providing a subtle contrast to the savory elements. The glaze has a slight sheen and hints of finely minced raisin, adding depth. A scattering of vibrant green, thinly sliced green onions provides a fresh, aromatic garnish, enhancing the visual appeal. The overall presentation is clean and uncluttered, with moderate negative space. The pork is presented as whole pieces, not sliced or fanned. The table setting features a natural wooden surface, a simple cotton napkin, and a pair of traditional Japanese chopsticks placed neatly beside the plate, emphasizing the cultural context. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed short-grain white rice.
Offer a side of pickled ginger or daikon (tsukemono) to cleanse the palate.
Pair with a light miso soup.

ingredients.name: High Quality White Chocolate, finely chopped
Neutral Oil (e.g., canola or vegetable oil)

instructions: Cut potatoes into large chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender, 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Mash potatoes thoroughly with butter and warm milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Form into 8 small, flat, round cakes (approx. 5 cm diameter, 1.5 cm thick). Chill for 30 minutes to firm.
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Slice pork loin into 8 medallions (approx. 1.5-2 cm thick).
In a small saucepan, combine white miso paste, sake, mirin, and dashi. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, whisking until miso is dissolved. Reduce heat to low.

Add finely chopped white chocolate, finely minced raisins, and marshmallow to the saucepan. Whisk continuously until chocolate and marshmallow are fully melted and glaze is smooth and slightly thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in rose water. Keep warm.

Heat neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C). Remove pork from skillet and let rest, loosely tented with foil.
In the same skillet, add more oil if needed. Pan-fry potato cakes over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.

Place 2 pork medallions and 2 crispy potato cakes on each plate. Drizzle generous amount of warm White Chocolate Miso Glaze over the pork and around the plate. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: The white chocolate, marshmallow, and rose water are used in very small quantities to provide subtle body, gloss, and aromatic complexity to the savory glaze, rather `than contributing overt sweetness or floral notes. Their purpose is to refine the glaze's texture and add nuanced depth.
Ensure the marshmallow is fully dissolved into the hot glaze to prevent any sticky texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Beet Relish and Garlic-Mustard Cream
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, light cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate, showcasing a single, generously portioned roasted chicken breast. The chicken, with its naturally browned, tender surface, sits whole, emphasizing its pure form. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant mound of deep ruby-red fermented beet relish offers a striking color contrast, its small, uniform cubes catching the light. Delicately draped beside the relish are a few translucent, pale purple strands of quick pickled red onion, adding a subtle touch of color and texture. A smooth, off-white garlic-mustard cream is artfully drizzled in a minimalist line across a portion of the chicken and plate, providing a creamy counterpoint. The only garnish is a sparse scattering of finely chopped fresh dill or chives, adding a natural green accent without overwhelming the clean composition. The plating emphasizes negative space, allowing each ingredient to breathe and highlight its natural beauty. The scene is set on a light-colored, subtly textured reclaimed wood or stone surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing textures and colors. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery from a nearby plant, maintaining an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Beet Relish: Wash beets thoroughly. Peel and dice beets into 1cm cubes. Place diced beets in a clean 1-liter glass jar. Add 15g sea salt and 10 black peppercorns to 500ml filtered water. Stir until salt dissolves. Pour brine over beets, ensuring beets are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if available. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days. Bubbles will indicate fermentation. Once fermented, store in the refrigerator.

Prepare Quick Pickled Red Onion: Thinly slice the red onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine 100ml apple cider vinegar, 10g sugar (optional), and 100ml water. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Place sliced onion in a heatproof jar. Pour hot vinegar mixture over onion. Let cool completely. Store in refrigerator.

Prepare Garlic-Mustard Cream: Mince garlic cloves very finely. In a small bowl, combine minced garlic, Dijon mustard, and mayonnaise. Stir until well combined. Season with a pinch of salt if needed. Cover and refrigerate until serving.

Roast Chicken: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts skin-side down (if skin-on) for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C at the thickest part. Remove from oven, let rest for 5 minutes before plating.

Assemble Dish: On each plate, place one roasted chicken breast. Spoon a generous portion of fermented beet relish alongside the chicken. Arrange a few strands of quick pickled red onion next to the relish. Drizzle a small amount of garlic-mustard cream over the chicken or alongside the relish. Garnish sparingly with chopped fresh dill or chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For true zero-waste, consider using a whole chicken for roasting and making stock from the carcass.
Beet greens, if available, can be sautéed and served as a side dish to reduce food waste.
Adjust fermentation time for beets based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
This recipe emphasizes minimal processing and celebrates the natural flavors of high-quality ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly (Kakuni) with Silky Potato Puree and Savory White Chocolate Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial chunk of glistening, deeply caramelized braised pork belly, known as Kakuni, anchors the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its surface reveals a rich, dark brown hue, reflecting the savory-sweet braising liquid. Beside the pork, a smooth, elegant quenelle of creamy, light beige potato puree provides a soft textural contrast. A subtle, artful drizzle of savory white chocolate sauce delicately cascades over a portion of the pork, adding a sophisticated sheen. Finely sliced vibrant green onions are sprinkled atop the pork for a fresh pop of color and garnish. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a set of traditional Japanese chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin, all bathed in natural, even lighting within a modern bistro setting, ensuring the dish remains the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed white rice on the side.
Offer a side of blanched green vegetables like bok choy or spinach.
instructions: Cut pork belly into 4 large, thick chunks. Place pork in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Simmer 10 minutes. Skim foam. Drain pork. Rinse pork under cold water.
Heat a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork belly chunks on all sides until golden brown. Remove excess fat.

Add sake, mirin, soy sauce, sugar, ginger slices, and dashi stock to the pot with the pork. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise 2-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Turn pork every 30 minutes. Remove pork from liquid. Strain braising liquid. Keep both warm.
Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot. Mash until smooth. Add butter and milk. Mix until creamy and smooth. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.

For the white chocolate drizzle, melt white chocolate in a double boiler or microwave. Stir in 1-2 tablespoons of the warm strained braising liquid until smooth and pourable. Adjust consistency if needed.

To plate, place a generous dollop of potato puree on each white porcelain plate. Place one chunk of braised pork belly beside the puree. Drizzle the savory white chocolate mixture artfully over the pork. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: The white chocolate drizzle is intended to add a subtle creamy sweetness and gloss, not to make the dish taste like dessert. Use high-quality white chocolate.
Ensure pork belly is very tender for the best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Buta Nikujaga (Braised Pork and Potato)
recipes.visual_description: The Buta Nikujaga is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl, featuring a hearty single portion. Braised pork belly cubes, 3cm, glisten with savory-sweet sauce. Tender potato wedges, 4cm, absorb the rich liquid. Bright 1cm thick carrot rounds and translucent onion wedges provide color and texture. A few vibrant green blanched green beans, 3cm pieces, add fresh contrast. The dish is bathed in a glossy, light brown braising liquid, clinging to ingredients. Thin slices of fresh ginger garnish the top. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and traditional Japanese chopsticks on a rest. Natural, even light illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer a small bowl of miso soup on the side.
Serve with a side of pickled daikon (tsukemono).
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add pork belly cubes. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove pork.
Add onion wedges to the pot. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add potato wedges and carrot rounds.
Pour in dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Bring to a gentle boil. Skim off any foam.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot with an otoshibuta (drop lid) or a smaller lid placed directly on the food.
Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and pork is very tender.
Remove otoshibuta. Increase heat slightly. Simmer uncovered for 5-7 minutes to reduce sauce slightly.
Stir in blanched green beans during the last minute.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh ginger slices.
notes: Adjust sugar and soy sauce to taste based on desired sweetness and saltiness.
For deeper flavor, brown the pork well before adding liquids.
The dish tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.
traditional_techniques: Otoshibuta (drop lid) use for even braising and flavor distribution.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Basil-Cottage Cheese Stuffing, Roasted Bell Pepper Coulis, Sautéed Forest Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken breast, stuffed with creamy basil-cottage cheese, anchors the pristine white bone china plate. The golden-brown chicken is presented whole. A vibrant, smooth red bell pepper coulis is artfully swiped across the plate, offering striking color contrast. Beside it, a precise cluster of earthy, sautéed forest mushrooms (sliced) is meticulously arranged. A light scattering of golden, crispy garlic breadcrumbs provides texture over the chicken and mushrooms. A single, small, vibrant green basil leaf serves as a delicate garnish. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, bathed in dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows. Ample negative space emphasizes the minimalist, sophisticated presentation. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded, and elegant minimalist cutlery complete the setting.

ingredients.name: Assorted forest mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake, oyster)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red bell peppers, remove seeds. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Cool, then peel skins.
For the coulis: Blend roasted bell peppers with 1 minced garlic clove and 100ml vegetable stock until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Finely dice half the small onion. Mince 1 garlic clove. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in 10ml olive oil until translucent. Cool.
Chop basil leaves finely. In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, chopped basil, sautéed onion and garlic, and 20g breadcrumbs. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Butterfly each chicken breast carefully to create a pocket. Stuff each chicken breast with an equal portion of the cottage cheese mixture. Secure opening with toothpicks if needed.
Season stuffed chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven.
Bake chicken for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.

While chicken bakes: Slice mushrooms. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Heat 15ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and thyme sprigs. Sauté until tender and browned. Add minced garlic during the last minute. Season with salt and pepper.
For crispy breadcrumbs: Heat 5ml olive oil in a small pan. Add remaining 30g breadcrumbs. Toast until golden brown and crisp. Stir constantly.

To plate: Spoon a swirl or smear of bell pepper coulis onto one side of a large white plate. Place a whole, rested stuffed chicken breast next to the coulis. Arrange a small, precise cluster of sautéed mushrooms. Sprinkle crispy garlic breadcrumbs over the chicken and mushrooms. Garnish with a small fresh basil leaf or a few drops of basil oil around the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Amaretti Semifreddo with Compressed Peach and Verbena Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A precisely plated single portion of Amaretti Semifreddo rests elegantly on a premium white Carrara marble surface. The semifreddo is a pristine, pale cream rectangle, subtly flecked with darker amaretti crumbs, showcasing its creamy texture. Around it, translucent, vibrant orange peach cubes, each precisely cut, are artfully scattered, catching the light. A crystal-clear, pale golden peach and verbena consommé pools gracefully around the components, creating a sense of delicate fluidity. An irregular, delicate golden-brown amaretti crisp shard leans against the semifreddo, providing architectural height and contrasting texture. A single, small, vibrant green lemon verbena leaf serves as a minimalist garnish. The composition utilizes abundant negative space, highlighting the refined ingredients. The setting includes an elegant bone china plate with a subtle rim, a polished silver dessert spoon, and a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: For the Amaretti Semifreddo: Combine 75g sugar and 30ml water in a saucepan. Heat to 121°C. Remove from heat.
Whip egg yolks in a stand mixer until pale. Slowly pour hot sugar syrup into yolks, whipping continuously until mixture is thick and cooled.
Whip heavy cream to soft peaks in a separate bowl. Gently fold whipped cream, 80g crushed amaretti, and amaretto liqueur into the yolk mixture.
Pour semifreddo mixture into a small terrine mold or individual molds lined with plastic wrap. Freeze for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
For the Compressed Peaches: Peel and pit 2 peaches. Cut into precise 1.5 cm cubes.
Place peach cubes in a vacuum seal bag with 100ml peach nectar and 10ml lemon juice. Vacuum seal and compress. Refrigerate for 2 hours.
For the Peach & Verbena Consommé: Roughly chop 2 peaches (skin on). Combine chopped peaches, verbena leaves, 20g sugar, and 150ml water in a saucepan. Simmer for 15 minutes.

Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Do not press solids. For maximum clarity, strain again through a coffee filter or cheesecloth-lined chinois. Chill consommé completely. Stir in 5ml lemon juice before serving.
For the Amaretti Crisps: Preheat oven to 160°C. Combine 30g finely ground amaretti, melted butter, 15g sugar, egg white, and flour. Mix well to form a paste.
Spread mixture very thinly onto a silicone mat-lined baking sheet using an offset spatula. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.
To Assemble: Slice semifreddo into elegant rectangles or squares. Place one piece on each chilled plate, positioned to one side.
Artfully arrange 5-7 compressed peach cubes around the semifreddo.
Gently spoon chilled peach and verbena consommé around the elements on the plate, creating a clear pool.
Carefully lean one amaretti crisp shard against the semifreddo. Garnish with a small fresh lemon verbena leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Tartaletas de Crema de Queso y Cereza
recipes.visual_description: A single, round "Tartaleta de Crema de Queso y Cereza" sits on a simple, rustic ceramic plate with natural, earthy tones and minor imperfections, reflecting a Peruvian home aesthetic. The pastry crust is a warm, golden-brown, forming a sturdy cup. Inside, the cream cheese filling is a creamy, off-white, with a smooth, slightly domed surface, showing a gentle set. A generous mound of vibrant, deep red cherry topping cascades over the cream cheese, with some whole or halved cherries visible, glistening with their natural juices. The cherries are plump and soft, some showing their natural dimples. The tartlet is presented casually on a well-used, dark wooden dining table, slightly worn and showing character. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a muted color lies beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, soft light, suggesting a cozy family kitchen atmosphere. No decorative garnishes are used; the food's natural appeal is the focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Enjoy with a small cup of strong, traditional Peruvian "café pasado" (filter coffee).
Serve with a refreshing glass of homemade "chicha morada" (purple corn drink).
These tartlets are often enjoyed as a comforting afternoon treat or a dessert after a family meal.
instructions: Combine flour, 50 g sugar, and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add egg yolk and mix until dough just comes together. Add ice water if dough is too dry. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll out dough on a floured surface to 3 mm thickness. Cut out four 10 cm circles. Gently press dough circles into four individual tartlet molds (about 8-10 cm diameter). Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper and fill with baking weights or dried beans. Bake for 10 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake for 5-7 more minutes until lightly golden. Cool.

Reduce oven temperature to 160°C. In a bowl, beat softened cream cheese and 75 g sugar until smooth. Beat in large egg and vanilla extract until just combined. Stir in lime zest if using. Do not overmix.
Pour cream cheese filling into the pre-baked tartlet shells. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until filling is set but still slightly wobbly in the center. Cool completely on a wire rack.

In a small saucepan, combine pitted cherries, 30 g sugar, and water or lemon juice. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cherries soften and sauce thickens slightly. Cool completely.
Spoon cooled cherry topping over each cooled cream cheese tartlet. Serve at room temperature or chilled.
notes: Ensure tartlets cool completely before adding cherry topping to prevent it from sliding off or warming the filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Mushroom Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The pan-seared beef medallions are centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Each medallion, approximately 4 cm thick, exhibits a deep brown, well-seared crust with a tender, slightly pink interior. Surrounding the beef is a rich, creamy garlic mushroom sauce, which is a warm golden-brown hue with visible slices of sautéed cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots. The sauce pools elegantly around the beef. A sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil and 20 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached and a crust forms. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F) for well-done, adjust cooking time accordingly.
Remove beef from skillet. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Add remaining 20 g butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallot. Sauté over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are golden brown and shallots are softened.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce wine by half, about 2 minutes.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme sprigs. Continue to simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in remaining 20 g butter until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Spoon garlic mushroom cream sauce onto plates. Place a beef medallion on top of the sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For food safety, ensure beef reaches desired internal temperature. A meat thermometer is recommended.
Resting the beef is crucial for juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Beet Puree and Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin rendered crisp and golden-brown, rests centrally on a matte, cream-colored ceramic plate. Adjacent to the chicken is a vibrant, smooth dollop of deep magenta roasted beet puree, its earthy color providing a striking contrast. Thinly sliced, translucent rings of quick-pickled red onion, a delicate pink-purple hue, are artfully scattered around the chicken and puree, adding visual interest and a touch of brightness. A single sprig of fresh green thyme garnishes the chicken. The composition is clean and minimalist, emphasizing natural textures and colors. The plate sits on a light, naturally textured wooden surface. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting its pure, unadorned beauty. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the plate, completing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare pickled red onion: Thinly slice red onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Pour hot liquid over onion slices in a heatproof jar. Let cool completely. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash beets. Cut beets into 2 cm wedges. Peel and quarter yellow onion. Peel 4 garlic cloves.
Toss beet wedges, yellow onion quarters, and 4 garlic cloves with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes until tender. Reserve 2 garlic cloves for sauce.

Prepare roasted beet puree: Transfer roasted beets, yellow onion, and 2 roasted garlic cloves to a food processor. Add 30 ml olive oil. Process until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Adjust consistency with a tablespoon of water if needed.

Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs, skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crisp. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast chicken for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

While chicken roasts, prepare mustard-garlic sauce: Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Remove chicken from skillet. Pour off excess fat, leaving 15 ml. Return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with vegetable broth. Stir in Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, scraping up browned bits, until slightly reduced. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Spoon a generous dollop of warm beet puree onto each plate. Place one pan-seared chicken thigh alongside. Arrange a few pickled red onion rings over and around the chicken. Drizzle chicken with mustard-garlic sauce. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Cocoa-Oatmeal Crusted Chicken with Savory Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, cocoa-oatmeal crusted chicken breast, presented as a whole piece, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken boasts a rich, golden-brown crust with visible oat texture and a subtle dark hue from the cocoa. It is generously draped with a velvety, earthy mushroom sauce, its deep brown color enhanced by the dark chocolate. The sauce features tender, sliced cremini mushrooms. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast and fresh aroma. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, showcasing the chicken and sauce. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard metal flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, creating a casual restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare three shallow dishes for breading. Dish 1: Flour. Dish 2: Whisk egg with 2 tbsp milk. Dish 3: Combine rolled oats, cocoa powder, salt, and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shake off excess. Dip in egg mixture, let excess drip off. Press firmly into oat-cocoa mixture to coat completely.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and rest on a cutting board.
In the same skillet, melt butter. Add diced shallot. Cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and thyme, cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in remaining milk and chopped dark chocolate. Stir until chocolate is melted and sauce is smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice each chicken breast into thick, diagonal medallions or leave whole. Arrange chicken on plates. Spoon mushroom sauce over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Fillet, Smoked Chili Jus, Coriander Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut, pan-seared beef fillet, cooked to a perfect medium-rare with a deep, caramelized crust. The beef is positioned slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate, allowing for abundant negative space. A glossy, dark mahogany smoked chili jus forms an elegant, organic pool or brushstroke beside the beef. Contrasting this richness are a few artful dots and a delicate drizzle of vibrant emerald green coriander oil, adding a fresh, aromatic counterpoint. A scattering of 2-3 delicate micro-coriander leaves provides a final pop of color and freshness. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, sits to the side. Dramatic, professional lighting creates subtle shadows, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish against an ultra-minimalist background, emphasizing sophistication and restraint.
instructions: Prepare the Smoked Chili Jus: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast beef bones/trimmings on a baking sheet for 30 minutes until deeply browned. Transfer bones to a large pot.
Drain excess fat from baking sheet. Add diced shallots, garlic, carrot, and celery to the baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Add roasted vegetables, tomato paste, smoked paprika, chili flakes, thyme, and bay leaf to the pot with bones. Deglaze the baking sheet with red wine, scraping up all browned bits. Pour into the pot.

Add beef stock to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Skim any foam. Simmer gently for 2-3 hours, or until liquid has reduced by half and flavors are concentrated. Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return strained jus to a clean saucepan. Gently reduce over medium-low heat until it coats the back of a spoon and is glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare the Coriander Oil: Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath.
Blanch fresh coriander in boiling water for 15 seconds. Immediately transfer to the ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well and squeeze out excess water.

Blend blanched coriander with neutral oil and a pinch of salt until smooth and vibrant green. Pass the oil through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove solids, creating a clear, bright green oil. Set aside.
Cook the Beef Fillet: Remove beef fillet from refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef fillet in the hot pan. Sear undisturbed for 3-4 minutes until a deep brown crust forms.

Flip the beef. Add butter to the pan. Baste the beef continuously with melted butter using a spoon for 3-4 minutes. Transfer the pan to a preheated 200°C oven for 5-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 60°C (medium-rare).
Remove beef from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Rest for 10 minutes before serving. Do not slice the beef before plating.

To Serve: Place one thick-cut beef fillet piece slightly off-center on each warm plate. Spoon a controlled, organic pool of the rich smoked chili jus beside or under the beef. Artfully dot or drizzle the vibrant green coriander oil around the plate. Garnish with a few delicate micro-coriander leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Root Vegetables and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate, set on a natural light wood table surface. A single generous portion features two to three large, rustic 4-5cm chunks of dark, tender braised beef. The beef is surrounded by fork-tender, irregularly cut 3-4cm potato chunks and vibrant 2cm carrot rounds, all coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown tomato-infused braising liquid. The liquid is thick but flowing, not dry. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The composition is organic and inviting. A cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and deep colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, 2cm carrot rounds, and diced celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add 3-4cm potato chunks to the pot during the last 45 minutes of cooking. Ensure potatoes are submerged.
Continue to simmer until potatoes are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Supreme with Pearl Barley Risotto, Roasted Tomato, and Carrot Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Seared Chicken Supreme is elegantly presented on a pristine, matte bone china plate, set on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. The golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken supreme, with its bone-in wingette, anchors the plate. A smooth, vibrant orange swoosh of carrot puree creates an organic base. A delicate quenelle of creamy pearl barley risotto rests gracefully. Artfully scattered are a few ruby-red roasted cherry tomatoes and soft, caramelized whole garlic cloves. A thin, golden Parmesan crisp leans against the chicken, adding an architectural element. Abundant negative space highlights the precise placement and natural forms. A scattering of fresh oregano provides a final verdant touch. Dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows completes the ultra-minimalist, sophisticated setting. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

For Roasted Tomatoes and Garlic: Place cherry tomatoes and garlic cloves on a baking tray. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.

For Carrot Puree: Boil chopped carrots in lightly salted water until very tender. Drain well. Blend carrots with 15g butter and a splash of cooking water until perfectly smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.

For Parmesan Crisps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Create four small circles (approximately 8cm diameter) of grated Parmesan. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove from oven. Let cool and harden. Carefully peel off parchment paper.

For Pearl Barley Risotto: Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add pearl barley. Toast for 2 minutes. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine evaporates. Add a ladle of warm chicken stock. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, until barley is creamy and al dente (about 30-35 minutes). Stir in remaining 15g butter and half of the chopped oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For Chicken Supreme: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crisp. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

To Plate: Spoon a generous swoosh of carrot puree onto one side of each plate. Place a rested chicken supreme next to the puree. Create a delicate quenelle of pearl barley risotto next to the chicken. Arrange a few roasted cherry tomatoes and garlic cloves around the dish. Lean one Parmesan crisp against the chicken or barley. Garnish with remaining fresh oregano leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Asado con Arroz Rojo y Frijoles
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous mound of vibrant, fluffy red rice occupies the center. Golden-brown, seared chicken thigh pieces, cut into substantial 3-4 cm chunks, are nestled atop the rice. Roasted red and yellow bell pepper strips, slightly softened with faint charring, are artfully arranged around the chicken and rice. A small, neat scoop of glossy black beans sits beside the rice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped cilantro leaves and a few thin rounds of bright green pickled jalapeno. The overall presentation is inviting, with a balanced composition and rich, natural colors. The plate rests on a simple wooden surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and a lime wedge beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side
Offer extra lime wedges for squeezing
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with 5 ml olive oil, 3 g cumin, 2 g oregano, salt, and pepper. Marinate 15 minutes.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut red and yellow bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Slice half the onion into thin strips. Toss bell pepper and onion strips with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.

Dice remaining half onion and mince garlic. Add 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, 2 g cumin, 1 g oregano, and tomato paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the pot. Stir 1 minute to coat grains. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Season with salt.

Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
While rice cooks, drain and rinse black beans. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Add beans. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat through 3-5 minutes.
Chop fresh cilantro. Slice lime into wedges.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks.

Serve individual portions: mound red rice on a plate. Arrange chicken chunks on top. Place roasted bell pepper and onion strips around the chicken. Add a scoop of black beans beside the rice. Garnish with chopped cilantro and a few pickled jalapeno slices. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust pickled jalapeno quantity based on desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Buffalo Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, use sodium citrate rather than roux
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of vibrant, creamy Spicy Buffalo Macaroni and Cheese is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The elbow macaroni is perfectly al dente, coated in a glossy, rich orange-red cheese sauce. The sauce appears smooth and luxurious, clinging to every pasta piece. A sprinkle of finely chopped bright green chives is scattered over the top, providing a fresh color contrast. A light dusting of golden-brown toasted panko breadcrumbs adds a textural element. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and colors, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium heat.
Pour in milk. Add sodium citrate. Whisk until sodium citrate dissolves completely.
Reduce heat to low. Gradually add shredded cheddar and Monterey Jack cheeses, whisking constantly.
Continue whisking until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth and emulsified.
Stir in buffalo hot sauce. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Add cooked macaroni to the cheese sauce. Stir to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives and toasted panko breadcrumbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Mac & Cheese with Crispy Brussels Sprouts
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoky Chipotle Mac & Cheese is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl or a shallow, wide-rimmed dinner plate. The mac and cheese is mounded slightly, showcasing its creamy, golden-orange hue with subtle flecks of chipotle. Its texture appears rich and comforting. Scattered artfully around and nestled into the mac and cheese are several crispy, roasted Brussels sprout halves. These sprouts display a vibrant green interior with beautifully charred, dark brown edges, adding visual contrast and a hint of bitterness. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives adds a bright green accent. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard, polished flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows, creating an inviting, modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Trim and halve Brussels sprouts. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and crispy. Set aside.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar and Monterey Jack cheeses until melted and smooth.
Add chipotle hot sauce, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and Dijon mustard. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Add cooked macaroni to the cheese sauce. Stir to combine.
Serve hot. Top each portion with roasted Brussels sprouts and a sprinkle of fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Asparagus and Spinach
recipes.special_requests: 6 grams saturated fat per serving or less
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Asparagus and Spinach is presented on a pristine white round porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. Two golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast chunks, retaining their natural shape, are positioned slightly off-center. Vibrant green asparagus spears, cooked to a crisp-tender perfection, are arranged neatly alongside the chicken. A bed of bright green, wilted spinach is nestled beneath the chicken pieces. A glossy, light pan sauce, infused with lemon and herbs, is artfully spooned over the chicken and vegetables. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned beside the chicken. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh ingredients and textures, with a soft, blurred restaurant-style background maintaining a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add trimmed asparagus spears. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add minced garlic to the skillet with asparagus. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add spinach to the skillet. Cook for 1-2 minutes until wilted.
Pour in chicken broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in lemon zest and chopped fresh parsley. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick pieces or leave whole if small.
Divide asparagus and spinach among four plates. Arrange chicken pieces beside the vegetables. Spoon the lemon-herb pan sauce over the chicken and vegetables. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Asparagus Purée, Blanched Asparagus, and Reduced Chicken Jus
recipes.special_requests: 6 grams saturated fat per serving or less
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, rests on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern. Beside it, a vibrant green asparagus purée forms a graceful, organic swoosh, its smooth texture contrasting with the chicken. Three crisp-tender blanched asparagus tips, precisely placed, add delicate visual interest and a fresh pop of color. A rich, glossy, dark amber chicken jus is artfully drizzled around the main components, creating an appealing sheen. A few delicate microgreens or chervil sprigs provide a final touch of verdant freshness. The plate is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside modern silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and abundant negative space. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the absolute focal point.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Jus: Combine chicken stock, diced shallot, minced garlic, thyme, and bay leaf in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until liquid is reduced by two-thirds, about 30-40 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Keep warm.

Prepare Asparagus Purée: Snap woody ends from asparagus. Reserve 12 small, perfect tips for garnish. Cut remaining asparagus into 2.5 cm pieces. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch asparagus pieces for 3-4 minutes until tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Blend blanched asparagus with 20ml olive oil and a pinch of salt until perfectly smooth. Add a tablespoon of hot water if needed for consistency. Pass purée through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.
Prepare Asparagus Garnish: Blanch reserved asparagus tips in boiling salted water for 1-2 minutes until crisp-tender. Transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Pat dry.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 10ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place chicken breasts in the skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and a crust forms. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Finish Jus: Stir butter into the warm chicken jus until melted and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate Dish: Place a spoonful of asparagus purée slightly off-center on each plate. Create a gentle swoosh or elegant dollop. Place one whole, rested chicken breast beside the purée. Artfully arrange three blanched asparagus tips near the chicken. Drizzle the rich chicken jus around the chicken and purée. Garnish with a few delicate microgreens or chervil sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Asparagus
recipes.special_requests: 6 grams saturated fat per serving or less
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown roasted chicken thigh is centered on an everyday off-white ceramic plate with a simple rim. The chicken, plump and juicy, shows a slightly crisped surface from roasting. Alongside, vibrant green asparagus spears are arranged naturally, some touching the chicken, others slightly overlapping. The asparagus maintains its tender-crisp texture. A thin, caramelized lemon slice rests on the chicken. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple folded cloth napkin and standard silver fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy light illuminates the dish, highlighting the natural colors and textures. The background is minimal, showing a hint of a lived-in kitchen atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium, half thinly sliced, half cut into wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry.
In a large bowl, toss chicken with 1 tablespoon olive oil, garlic powder, oregano, thyme, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon pepper.
Arrange chicken in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast chicken for 15 minutes.
While chicken roasts, toss asparagus with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon pepper.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Arrange asparagus around chicken. Place lemon slices on top of chicken.
Return to oven. Roast for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and asparagus is tender-crisp.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon Herb Sauce and Roasted Asparagus
recipes.special_requests: 6 grams saturated fat per serving or less
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, sliced into two or three thick, diagonal pieces, is placed slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken exhibits a golden-brown crust from searing. Beside the chicken, a generous portion of vibrant green roasted asparagus spears are neatly arranged. A light, glistening lemon-herb pan sauce is spooned generously over the chicken and slightly onto the plate. The chicken is golden-brown with a tender, white interior. Asparagus is bright green with slight char marks, indicating a tender-crisp texture. The sauce is a pale golden liquid, flecked with bright green chopped parsley. A sprinkle of bright yellow lemon zest adds a pop of color. The chicken breast is sliced into thick, diagonal pieces. Asparagus spears are whole, with trimmed ends. Fresh chopped parsley and grated lemon zest garnish the dish. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, crisp white cotton napkin is positioned to the side of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere with soft, warm tones. The portion is a single, refined restaurant-style serving.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Roast asparagus for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet with chicken to preheated oven. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet.
Bring broth to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 3-4 minutes until slightly reduced.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in butter, lemon juice (from 1/2 lemon, or to taste), and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper if needed.
Slice chicken breasts diagonally into 2-3 thick pieces. Arrange chicken and roasted asparagus on plates. Spoon lemon herb sauce over chicken. Garnish with lemon zest and fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Quick-Fermented Mushrooms & Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of pasta is presented on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate, reflecting natural, earthy textures. Long pasta strands are loosely coiled, forming a gentle mound. Tender, earthy mushrooms, halved or quartered, are interspersed, showcasing rich brown hues. Small, irregular crisps of golden-brown bacon are scattered sparingly, adding texture and savory notes. Vibrant green basil leaves, whole or gently torn, and small sprigs of fresh oregano provide aromatic freshness. A light dusting of finely grated hard aged cheese crowns the dish. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting organic forms and subtle color variations. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery, emphasizing sustainable principles.
instructions: Clean mushrooms. Separate stems from caps. Slice caps into halves or quarters. Reserve stems for broth.
Place mushroom stems in a small pot with 250ml water. Simmer 15 minutes. Strain to create mushroom broth. Set aside 200ml.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 100ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Dice bacon into small pieces. Render bacon in a large pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain bacon crisps on paper towel. Reserve 15ml bacon fat in the pan.
Finely dice onion. Sauté diced onion in reserved bacon fat until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine vinegar. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Cook 30 seconds.
Add mushroom broth (or water) to the pan. Simmer until liquid reduces by half, creating a light sauce.
Add cooked pasta to the pan with the mushroom mixture. Toss to combine. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water to achieve desired consistency.
Roughly chop fresh basil and oregano. Stir into the pasta. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with crispy bacon pieces and freshly grated hard aged cheese.
notes: This recipe emphasizes a 'quick-fermented' tang from red wine vinegar and deep mushroom flavor. For a true lacto-fermented element, pre-make lacto-fermented mushrooms separately and incorporate them.
Utilize mushroom stems for broth, and render bacon fat for cooking, minimizing waste. Compost any remaining organic scraps.
Embrace seasonal, local mushrooms for best flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Pan Sauce and Roasted Asparagus
recipes.special_requests: 6 grams saturated fat per serving or less
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp exterior, rests slightly off-center on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. Alongside, vibrant green asparagus spears are neatly arranged, showcasing their tender-crisp texture. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-herb pan sauce is elegantly spooned over and around the chicken, with some pooling subtly on the plate. Freshly chopped green parsley and fine lemon zest are sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, adding bright color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a clean and appealing presentation with moderate negative space. The focus is entirely on the beautifully cooked and plated dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to sop up the delicious pan sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Toss asparagus with 10ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add chicken breasts.
Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and a crust forms. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Transfer chicken to a plate. Tent with foil. Let rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 1 minute until reduced by half. If not using wine, skip this step and add stock directly.
Pour in chicken stock. Add thyme leaves. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes until sauce slightly thickens and reduces.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in lemon juice and chopped parsley. If desired, whisk in unsalted butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate one chicken breast per serving. Arrange roasted asparagus alongside. Spoon lemon-herb pan sauce generously over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh lemon zest.
traditional_techniques: Faire un fond de sauce (Making a pan sauce)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Garlic Pasta and Basil Stem Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta and chicken is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed cream ceramic bowl on a light reclaimed wood surface. The dish features al dente rigatoni coated in a delicate, golden sauce. Thick, rustic chunks of roasted chicken breast, showing natural pale golden-brown surfaces, are interspersed. Softened, translucent red onion slivers and whole, lightly crushed fermented garlic cloves are scattered throughout. A vibrant green basil stem oil generously drizzles over the dish, pooling in the bowl. Fresh, torn basil leaves are sparsely placed as natural garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, emphasizing natural textures and colors with ample negative space. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is loosely folded beside the bowl. The background is clean, subtly featuring natural plant greenery.

ingredients.name: Fermented garlic
ingredients.quantity: 1 head, cloves separated and lightly crushed

instructions: Prepare Basil Stem Oil: Wash basil stems. Roughly chop stems. In a small saucepan, combine chopped basil stems and 60ml olive oil. Heat gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Let cool. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing stems. Discard spent stems. Set oil aside.

Roast Chicken: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and black pepper. Drizzle with olive oil. Place on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Cut chicken into thick, rustic chunks.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

Sauté Aromatics: While pasta cooks, heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add 15ml olive oil. Add thinly sliced red onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add fermented garlic cloves. Sauté for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Create Sauce: Deglaze skillet with white wine or vegetable broth. Scrape up browned bits. Add 150ml reserved pasta water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.

Combine Dish: Add drained pasta to the skillet with sauce. Add roasted chicken chunks and half of the fresh basil leaves (torn). Toss gently to combine. Add more reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve: Divide pasta and chicken evenly among four shallow bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with basil stem oil. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately with a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Dakgalbi (Spicy Chicken Stir-fry)
recipes.visual_description: The Dakgalbi is a vibrant, rustic main course, served in a wide, shallow, dark stoneware bowl. Large, irregularly cut chunks of seared chicken, caramelized and glistening with a rich red-orange gochujang glaze, are the focal point.
