Return sauce to stovetop over low heat. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

For coconut rice: Combine basmati rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Coarsely chop toasted pecans.
Serve braised short ribs with mole sauce spooned over. Plate alongside a portion of coconut rice. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and toasted pecans. Serve with a lime wedge on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Rosemary-Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, rests centrally on a clean white round porcelain plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. Alongside, a generous portion of deep amber caramelized onion slices is artfully arranged. A glossy, rich brown rosemary-garlic pan sauce is generously spooned over and around the chicken. A small fresh rosemary sprig garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green. The overall color palette is warm and inviting. The plate sits on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and appealing colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of roasted potatoes or crusty bread.
Offer standard European flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until deep golden brown and caramelized. Remove onions from skillet and set aside.
Increase skillet heat to medium-high. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Place chicken breasts, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown.

Flip chicken breasts. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board.

Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. If using, pour in white wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let reduce by half. Add chicken stock, minced garlic, and chopped rosemary. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken breasts whole or halved if very large. Place caramelized onions alongside. Spoon pan sauce generously over chicken.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Garlic Parmesan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and moist, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced. It is generously coated and surrounded by a rich, ivory-colored creamy garlic parmesan sauce that glistens subtly. The sauce shows tiny flecks of minced garlic and melted cheese. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a contrasting pop of color on top of the chicken and sauce. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space around the dish. The scene features a simple wooden table surface, a folded white linen napkin beside the plate, and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to an even 2 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Whisk constantly until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A generous, home-style portion of Classic Beef Fried Rice is casually mounded on a round, rustic ceramic plate. Tender, pan-seared diced beef pieces are mixed throughout the fluffy, separated rice grains. Bright red and green bell pepper small cubes add pops of color and slight crunch, alongside vibrant green peas. Finely sliced scallions are scattered over the top, providing a fresh, aromatic finish. The rice has a light golden hue from the soy sauce, contrasting with the rich brown of the beef and the fresh greens of the vegetables. The dish appears warm and inviting, showcasing varied textures. The plate sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table. Next to it, a small, simple white rice bowl and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are casually placed. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot
Offer chili oil or sriracha on the side for added heat
Serve with a small side of pickled vegetables
instructions: Dice beef sirloin into 1 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice red and green bell peppers into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic and grate ginger.
Slice scallions, separating white and green parts.
Whisk eggs in a small bowl.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat. Add beef. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes. Remove beef from pan; set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced bell peppers and white parts of scallions. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Push vegetables to one side of the pan. Pour whisked eggs into the empty space. Scramble eggs until cooked. Break into small pieces.
Add cold rice and green peas to the pan. Stir to combine with vegetables and egg.
Pour soy sauce and sesame oil over the rice. Stir-fry vigorously for 3-5 minutes, breaking up any clumps of rice, until heated through and well combined.
Return cooked beef to the pan. Add green parts of scallions. Stir-fry for 1 minute to incorporate.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce, salt, or pepper if needed. Serve hot.
notes: Using day-old cold rice is crucial for good fried rice texture, as it prevents the rice from becoming mushy.
Cook in batches if your pan is not large enough to avoid overcrowding, which steams rather than fries the ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Peach, Goat Cheese, and Walnut Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh salad is casually presented on a simple, round white ceramic plate with a slight rim, resting on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. The plate is adequately filled but not overflowing, allowing some negative space. Mixed green leaves form a soft base. Juicy peach slices, cut into crescent shapes, are artfully scattered amongst the greens, showcasing their warm orange and red hues. Crumbled goat cheese, its creamy white contrasting with the greens and peaches, is generously sprinkled. Toasted walnut pieces, roughly chopped, add an earthy brown texture and are distributed throughout. A light drizzle of golden-yellow vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, binding them together. A casually folded beige linen napkin and a simple fork rest beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, Dijon mustard, honey, white wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper. Set aside.
Prepare the peaches: Wash peaches. Slice peaches into thin wedges.
Prepare the walnuts: Place walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat. Toast for 3-5 minutes until fragrant. Stir occasionally. Let cool.
Assemble the salad: In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens and sliced peaches.
Add cheese and walnuts: Crumble goat cheese over the salad. Sprinkle toasted walnuts evenly.
Dress and serve: Drizzle the prepared dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Golden pan-seared chicken breast, whole or in two thick pieces, positioned on a pristine white round plate. Earthy brown sautéed cremini mushroom slices are artfully scattered around. A rich, glossy Marsala wine sauce, deep amber, pools around the chicken, lightly coating it. Vibrant green fresh chopped Italian parsley garnishes the dish. Presented on a light wooden table with a crisp white linen napkin and silver flatware. A subtle glass of red wine in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights textures: crisp chicken surface, tender mushrooms, smooth shimmering sauce. Balanced composition with negative space, focusing on the refined single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or creamy polenta.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as a Chianti or Merlot.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken breasts lightly in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the same skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Allow chicken to warm through in the sauce.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cold butter until melted and incorporated (mantecare).
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a good quality dry Marsala wine for best flavor, not cooking Marsala.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Herb Chicken with White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Herb Chicken with White Beans is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown seared chicken thigh rests centrally, surrounded by a rustic arrangement of creamy cannellini beans, vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, and wilted dark green spinach leaves. The rich, herbed pan sauce lightly coats the ingredients. Freshly chopped parsley and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese provide a final, aromatic garnish, adding hints of green and white. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and a hint of a casual restaurant background, all bathed in natural, even lighting. Traditional Italian flatware is placed alongside the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken broth, cannellini beans, and halved cherry tomatoes to the pan. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in fresh spinach until just wilted. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato, Mushroom, and Bell Pepper Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted potato, mushroom, and bell pepper medley is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges are centrally arranged, showing their crisp exterior. Interspersed are vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, alongside deeply browned mushroom halves and caramelized onion wedges. Each vegetable displays distinct textures from roasting. The medley forms a balanced, organic pile, showcasing natural colors and forms, with moderate negative space. A light scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a bright contrast. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into wedges. Cut onions into thick wedges. Core, seed, and cut bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Halve mushrooms. Mince garlic. Chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, bell pepper strips, mushroom halves, minced garlic, olive oil, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme.
Season generously with salt and black pepper. Toss to coat all vegetables evenly.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Do not overcrowd. Use two sheets if necessary.
Roast for 30-40 minutes, flipping halfway, until vegetables are tender and potatoes are golden and crisp.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a serving plate. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Involtini with Mushroom and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: Two to three golden-brown beef involtini are arranged centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each involtino is cut on a slight diagonal, revealing the creamy, melted mozzarella, earthy sautéed mushrooms, and fragrant minced garlic within. The involtini are nestled in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce, which is spooned generously around and partially over the rolls. A few pan-seared cremini mushroom slices and halved roasted cherry tomatoes are artfully scattered in the sauce. The dish is garnished with several fresh, bright green basil leaves, providing a pop of color and aromatic contrast. The beef is tender, the mozzarella soft and gooey, and the sauce rich and inviting. The plate is set on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a silver fork and knife and a folded linen napkin, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting with an authentic Italian touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the rich tomato sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a side of polenta or pasta like tagliatelle.

ingredients.name: Beef top round or sirloin, thinly sliced

instructions: Pound beef slices thinly between two sheets of plastic wrap. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 10 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Add half of the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine cooked mushrooms and garlic with shredded mozzarella.
Lay beef slices flat. Place a portion of the mushroom-mozzarella filling on one end of each beef slice. Roll tightly. Secure each involtino with a toothpick or kitchen twine.
Heat remaining 20 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear involtini on all sides until golden brown. Remove involtini from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add remaining minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Let wine reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring sauce to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared involtini to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure involtini are mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender. Alternatively, braise in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for the same duration.
Remove toothpicks or twine before serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Mackerel with Umeboshi-Shiso Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a pan-seared mackerel fillet, skin crisped golden-brown, resting on a clean white porcelain plate. The whole fillet is generously coated with a vibrant, glistening umeboshi-shiso sauce, its reddish-purple color punctuated by dark green shiso flecks. The sauce pools gently around the fish. Beside the mackerel, a neat mound of finely grated white daikon radish offers a stark, refreshing contrast. Fresh green shiso leaves, whole or julienned, garnish the mackerel and daikon. The simple white plate leaves ample negative space. The scene is on a light wooden table, with traditional Japanese chopsticks and a small white rice bowl beside the plate. A folded cotton napkin sits nearby. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional bistro-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed Japanese white rice.
Offer a small bowl of miso soup as an accompaniment.
Serve with a side of tsukemono (Japanese pickled vegetables).

ingredients.name: Mackerel fillets
ingredients.quantity: 4 fillets (about 150-180g each), skin on, pin bones removed

ingredients.name: Fresh Shiso Leaves
ingredients.quantity: 20 leaves (16 for sauce, 4 for garnish), finely chopped for sauce, whole or julienned for garnish

instructions: Pat mackerel fillets dry with paper towels. Score skin lightly at 1-2 cm intervals. Season both sides with salt.

In a small saucepan, combine umeboshi paste, sake, mirin, soy sauce, water (or dashi), and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in finely chopped shiso leaves. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place mackerel fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Press gently with a spatula to ensure even skin contact.
Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Flip fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F).
Place one seared mackerel fillet on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of umeboshi-shiso sauce over and around the mackerel.
Garnish each plate with a small mound of grated daikon radish and a few fresh shiso leaves (whole or julienned). Serve immediately, optionally with steamed Japanese rice and a lemon wedge.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality, fresh mackerel.
Adjust the sweetness or tartness of the sauce to personal preference.
Ensure the pan is hot enough for a crispy skin without overcooking the fish.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Beef Tenderloin, Truffled Mushroom Duxelles, Garlic Confit Puree, and Red Wine Jus
recipes.visual_description: A thick, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, cooked to a tender medium-rare, anchors the composition, positioned slightly off-center on a large, pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent to the beef, a precisely formed quenelle of rich, earthy mushroom duxelles, finely diced and subtly infused with truffle, rests elegantly. A delicate, artful swirl of creamy white garlic confit puree provides a vibrant contrast in color and texture. A glossy, deep brown red wine beef jus is meticulously spooned around the base of the beef, creating an organic, reflective pool. The dish is garnished with a few vibrant green microgreens, precisely placed for a final touch of color. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, classic silver flatware, and a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the architectural precision and abundant negative space, showcasing the dish as a singular, refined masterpiece.
instructions: For Garlic Confit Puree: Preheat oven to 150°C. Place 2 whole garlic heads (tops sliced off) in a small oven-safe dish. Pour 100 ml olive oil over garlic. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Cover tightly with foil. Roast for 45-60 minutes until cloves are very tender. Squeeze softened garlic cloves into a small blender. Add 30 ml confit oil. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt. Set aside.

For Red Wine Jus: Finely dice 1 shallot. Sauté shallot in a small saucepan with 10 ml olive oil until softened. Deglaze with red wine. Reduce by half. Add beef stock. Simmer gently for 20-30 minutes until reduced by half and slightly thickened. Skim any foam. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For Truffled Mushroom Duxelles: Finely dice mushrooms and 1 shallot. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Sauté shallot in a pan with 10 ml olive oil until translucent. Add mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until all liquid evaporates and mushrooms are deeply browned. Add 10 grams butter and 1 thyme sprig (leaves only). Cook 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir in truffle oil if using. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

For Beef Tenderloin: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Place beef in a vacuum-sealable bag with 1 thyme sprig and 10 grams butter. Seal the bag. Cook in a sous vide bath at 54°C for 2 hours.

After sous vide, remove beef from bag. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat 10 ml olive oil and 30 grams butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Sear beef for 2-3 minutes per side, turning to create a deep brown crust on all surfaces. Rest beef on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

To Plate: Slice beef into 4 thick medallions (approximately 150g each). Place one medallion slightly off-center on each plate. Form a precise quenelle or small mound of mushroom duxelles next to the beef. Create a delicate swirl or dot of garlic confit puree. Spoon the red wine jus elegantly around the base of the beef. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Tuna & Greek Yogurt Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Tuna & Greek Yogurt Bake is presented in a shallow, everyday white ceramic bowl. The casserole is scooped naturally, showing its warm, bubbling consistency. The top features a golden-brown, slightly crispy melted cheddar cheese crust, with some cheese gently bubbling over the edges. Beneath the crust, the creamy, light-colored sauce is visible, studded with small, diced pieces of onion and celery, bright green peas, and chunky, flaked tuna mixed with tender elbow macaroni. The overall presentation is comforting and wholesome. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple white cloth napkin and a standard silver fork are casually placed beside the bowl. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen atmosphere with a soft, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain well.
Melt butter in a large oven-safe skillet or pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion and diced celery. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in broth and milk. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in Greek yogurt, half of the shredded cheese, salt, and pepper.
Add flaked tuna, cooked pasta, and peas (if using) to the sauce. Mix well to combine.
Transfer mixture to a 2-liter baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet.
Sprinkle remaining cheese and breadcrumbs (if using) over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and cheese is golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Tonkatsu Donburi
recipes.visual_description: Pork Tonkatsu Donburi is presented in a traditional white porcelain donburi bowl, showcasing a balanced composition. A generous bed of fluffy, nutty brown rice forms the base. Centered on the rice is a golden-brown, crispy Tonkatsu cutlet, sliced into thick, inviting chunks, not fanned. The pork is partially enveloped by a soft, gently cooked egg and tender, translucent slices of simmered onion, creating a harmonious blend of textures and colors. A delicate drizzle of creamy Japanese mayonnaise zigzags across the Tonkatsu. Freshly sliced vibrant green onions are scattered generously over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin, all bathed in natural, even lighting to highlight its warmth and inviting appeal. The background is clean and subtly blurred, evoking a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of miso soup
Served with tsukemono (Japanese pickled vegetables)
instructions: Rinse brown rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Pound pork cutlets to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season pork with salt and black pepper.
Set up breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with 1 beaten egg, one with panko.
Dredge each pork cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg. Coat thoroughly in panko, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok to 170°C. Fry pork cutlets one at a time for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Drain on a wire rack.
In a large skillet or donburi pan, combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced onion to the simmering sauce. Cook for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Slice each cooked tonkatsu into 1.5-2 cm wide strips. Arrange one sliced tonkatsu over the simmering onions in the skillet.

Lightly beat the remaining 3 eggs. Pour one-quarter of the beaten egg evenly over the tonkatsu and onions. Cover the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes, until the egg is mostly set but still slightly runny in the center.
Ladle a generous portion of hot brown rice into a large donburi bowl. Gently slide the tonkatsu, egg, and onion mixture from the skillet onto the rice. Repeat for each serving.
Drizzle Japanese mayonnaise over the tonkatsu. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure oil temperature is maintained for crispy tonkatsu.
Do not overcook the egg in the donburi sauce; it should remain slightly soft.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Mackerel with Umeboshi-Sansho Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly grilled mackerel fillet, skin-on, is the centerpiece on a clean, white rectangular porcelain plate. The skin is crisp, slightly charred, and glistens with a beautiful reddish-brown umeboshi-sake glaze. The moist, flaky flesh of the mackerel is visible. A neat mound of fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice sits beside the fish. A small, vibrant pile of blanched dark green spinach provides a color contrast. The dish is garnished with a few fresh, deep green shiso leaves and a small mound of white grated daikon radish, perhaps with a single red chili thread. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. Elegant wooden chopsticks are placed parallel to the plate. A small traditional ceramic rice bowl sits nearby. A folded white cotton napkin completes the setting. Natural, even lighting creates a refined Japanese bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup.
Offer green tea as a beverage.
Enjoy with a small bowl of pickled vegetables (tsukemono).
instructions: Pat mackerel fillets dry with paper towels. Score the skin 2-3 times diagonally.
Combine umeboshi paste, sake, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until slightly reduced and glossy. Set aside.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Lightly oil the grates.
Place mackerel fillets skin-side down on the grill. Grill for 4-5 minutes until skin is crisp and slightly charred.
Flip the mackerel. Continue grilling for 3-4 minutes, brushing generously with the umeboshi glaze during the last 2 minutes, until cooked through.
Divide cooked rice among 4 plates. Arrange blanched greens next to the rice.
Carefully transfer one grilled mackerel fillet to each plate. Spoon any remaining glaze over the fish.
Garnish each plate with fresh shiso leaves and a small mound of grated daikon radish.
Sprinkle sansho pepper over the mackerel just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Napa Cabbage and Fermented Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with an earthy, natural tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. Thinly sliced napa cabbage forms the base, its vibrant green providing a fresh backdrop. Julienne carrots add bright orange streaks, while thinly sliced fermented cucumbers, in pale green half-moons, introduce a subtle translucency. Blanched edamame pods are scattered throughout, offering pops of tender green. Thinly sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds are sprinkled on top, adding contrasting color and texture. The dressing lightly coats all ingredients, providing a glossy sheen. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests on the bowl's rim. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, natural lighting highlighting the dish's organic beauty. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone complements the sustainable aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a bowl of plain steamed rice.
Offer small side dishes of other pickled vegetables or kimchi.
Enjoy with a simple clear broth or miso soup.
instructions: Prepare all vegetables: Thinly slice napa cabbage. Julienne carrots. Thinly slice spring onions.
Blanch shelled edamame in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and rinse with cold water.
For the dressing, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, and maple syrup in a small bowl. Whisk until well combined.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sliced napa cabbage, julienned carrots, thinly sliced fermented cucumbers, blanched edamame, and sliced spring onions.
Pour the prepared dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to ensure all components are evenly coated.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the salad.
Serve immediately in individual bowls.
notes: To make fermented cucumbers: Thinly slice cucumbers. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 1 tablespoon of salt in 2 cups of filtered water to create a brine. Pour brine over cucumbers, ensuring they are fully submerged. Cover loosely and let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing fermentation for preservation and focusing on whole, unprocessed ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuna Crudo, Yuzu Yogurt, Crispy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a round, modern, matte white ceramic plate, set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. The composition features very thin slices of deep red sashimi-grade tuna, arranged in a natural, slightly overlapping flow. Small, artfully placed dots and delicate lines of pristine white Yuzu-Greek Yogurt Emulsion are precisely piped around the tuna. A few drops of vibrant emerald-green Shiso Oil are drizzled with intent, creating subtle pooling and sheen. Standing upright, one or two irregular, off-white crispy rice tuile shards add architectural height and textural contrast. The negative space on the plate is abundant, emphasizing the minimalist arrangement. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, lies beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle, intentional shadows that enhance depth and texture. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the sole focal point.
instructions: Prepare Crispy Rice Tuiles: Cook sushi rice according to package directions. Season lightly with salt. Spread cooked rice very thinly (1-2 mm) onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Dehydrate rice in a low oven (approx. 60°C) or dehydrator until completely dry and brittle, about 4-6 hours. Heat neutral oil in a small pot to 180°C. Deep-fry small pieces of dehydrated rice for a few seconds until they puff up and become crisp. Drain immediately on paper towels. Season lightly with fine sea salt. Break into irregular, elegant shards.

Make Yuzu-Greek Yogurt Emulsion: In a small bowl, combine Greek yogurt, fresh yuzu juice, and a pinch of fine sea salt. Whisk vigorously until the mixture is very smooth and slightly aerated. Transfer the emulsion to a small squeeze bottle for precise plating.

Prepare Shiso Oil: Blanch 10-12 shiso leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Squeeze out excess water from the blanched shiso. Blend the shiso leaves with extra virgin olive oil until a vibrant green, smooth oil forms. Strain the oil through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove any solids, yielding a clear, emerald green oil.
Prepare Tuna Crudo: Slice the sashimi-grade tuna loin very thinly against the grain, aiming for slices approximately 3 mm thick. Keep chilled until plating.

Assemble the Dish: On each cold, matte white plate, arrange 3-4 slices of tuna crudo in a natural, slightly overlapping composition. Use the squeeze bottle to place small, deliberate dots or lines of the Yuzu-Greek Yogurt Emulsion next to and around the tuna. Drizzle a few drops of the vibrant Shiso Oil artistically over and around the tuna. Carefully place 1-2 irregular shards of crispy rice tuile upright near the tuna for height and contrasting texture. Garnish each plate with a few delicate micro shiso or micro cilantro leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Pasta with Apple and Chili
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy chicken pasta is centrally plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta, such as fettuccine, is generously coated in a glossy, pale yellow-orange cream sauce. Seared golden-brown chicken chunks, approximately 2-3 cm, are nestled among the pasta, showcasing their crispy exteriors. Bright flecks of finely chopped red chili and fresh green parsley are visible, adding vibrant color and texture. Coarsely grated white apple pieces are interspersed, providing a fresh, crisp contrast. The dish is balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate. A silver fork rests to the right, and a folded white cotton napkin lies to the left. The scene is set on a simple wooden table under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere. The background is subtly blurred.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Finely chop chili, removing seeds for less heat if desired.
Add onion to the same skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened. Add garlic and chili. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in Dijon mustard until well combined. Add heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 100ml pasta water before draining.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Add cooked chicken chunks.
Grate apple coarsely. Add grated apple and grated Parmesan cheese to the pasta. Toss well to combine. Add reserved pasta water if needed to adjust sauce consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Mackerel Nitsuke with Umeboshi and Sansho
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mackerel Nitsuke is presented in a shallow, wide-rimmed Japanese ceramic bowl with a subtle, earthy tone. A thick chunk of pan-simmered mackerel, with its silvery skin lightly scored, rests in the center. The fish is generously coated in a rich, glossy, dark amber sauce that pools attractively around its base. The sauce glistens under natural, even lighting, hinting at its savory depth. Bright red streaks of umeboshi paste are visible within the sauce, adding a vibrant color contrast. Thin, translucent slices of fresh ginger are artfully placed on top of the mackerel, along with a scattering of vibrant green, thinly sliced green onion. A light dusting of finely ground sansho pepper provides a delicate, earthy speckle. The entire plate is visible, showcasing moderate negative space around the dish. Beside the bowl, a small, pristine white ceramic rice bowl holds a mound of fluffy steamed white rice. A pair of elegant wooden chopsticks rests neatly on a chopstick rest next to the rice bowl. A small dish of light pink pickled ginger sits nearby, completing the authentic Japanese setting on a simple wooden table surface with a natural cotton napkin.
instructions: Pat mackerel fillets dry. Score the skin of each fillet 2-3 times.
In a wide, shallow pot, combine sake, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, umeboshi paste, and dashi. Add half of the sliced ginger.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Carefully place mackerel fillets, skin-side up, into the simmering sauce. Ensure fish is mostly submerged.
Cover the fish directly with a small lid (otoshibuta) or a crumpled piece of foil.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes, or until the mackerel is cooked through and flakes easily. Do not overcook.
Gently remove the cooked mackerel fillets and place them into individual serving bowls.
Increase heat to high and reduce the remaining sauce in the pot until it slightly thickens and becomes glossy.
Pour the reduced sauce generously over each mackerel fillet.
Garnish each serving with the remaining fresh ginger slices, a sprinkle of sansho pepper, and thinly sliced green onion. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Yellowfin Tuna with Lemon-Caper Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A thick, pan-seared yellowfin tuna steak, displaying a golden-brown crust and pink interior, rests on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, a smooth mound of pale yellow potato puree is gently mounded. A vibrant, glistening lemon-caper butter sauce, flecked with bright green chopped parsley and dark capers, is spooned generously over the tuna, creating a rich sheen. A fresh lemon wedge accompanies the dish. The natural colors are inviting: deep pink and seared brown tuna, light yellow puree, and vibrant green/yellow sauce. Plating is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a light wooden surface, with a folded light grey cotton napkin nearby. Soft, even natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting textures. The background is simple, suggesting a casual bistro.
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to hot pot. Mash until smooth. Add 50g butter and warm milk. Mix until creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat tuna steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.

Heat olive oil in a large non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place tuna steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove tuna from pan. Set aside on a plate to rest.

Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 50g butter to the same pan. Let it melt and lightly brown, about 1-2 minutes. Add drained capers and juice of one lemon. Stir well. Cook for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Place a generous dollop of potato puree on each plate. Gently place one seared tuna steak next to the puree. Spoon lemon-caper sauce generously over the tuna. Garnish with a fresh lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Forbidden Rice Risotto, Black Garlic Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated portion on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, organic texture. The plate rests on a cool white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, soft overhead lighting casts gentle shadows, highlighting the dish's contours. A perfectly seared chicken breast, its skin a rich, crispy golden-brown, sits as the focal point, presented as a whole piece. Adjacent is an elegant, flowing mound of deep purple-black forbidden rice risotto, its creamy texture visible. A small, artfully placed pool of a rich, creamy, light brown black garlic emulsion adds a contrasting color and sophisticated sheen. Three vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched and quickly seared, are arranged with architectural precision. A delicate sprinkle of bright green microgreens provides a final touch of freshness and color. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist and refined presentation.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal individually. Cook sous-vide at 63°C for 90 minutes. Chill immediately in an ice bath if not serving immediately.
For the forbidden rice, heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan. Sauté diced shallot until translucent. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute.
Add forbidden rice. Stir for 2 minutes until lightly toasted. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until absorbed.
Begin adding hot chicken stock, 150ml at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Continue until rice is creamy and al dente, approximately 30-35 minutes.
Stir in 25g butter and season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the black garlic emulsion, mash black garlic cloves into a paste. In a bowl, whisk egg yolk, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and black garlic paste.
Slowly drizzle neutral oil into the egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly until a thick, emulsified sauce forms. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped tarragon.
Blanch asparagus spears in salted boiling water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Pat dry.

Remove chicken from sous-vide bags. Pat skin very dry. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear flesh-side down for 2 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before plating.
Heat remaining 25g butter in a small pan. Quickly sear blanched asparagus spears for 1-2 minutes until vibrant and tender-crisp.

To plate, spoon a generous, flowing mound of forbidden rice slightly off-center on each plate. Place one seared chicken breast next to the rice. Create a small, artistic pool or swirl of black garlic emulsion beside the chicken. Arrange 3 seared asparagus spears elegantly. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna with Lemon-Herb Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant seared tuna steak rests on a creamy, flowing bed of lemon-herb risotto, presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tuna steak, a thick, whole medallion, exhibits a golden-brown sear on its exterior, contrasting with its vibrant pinkish-red, medium-rare interior. The risotto is a pale yellow, showcasing its creamy, loose consistency, with flecks of green from finely chopped parsley and chives. Beside the tuna, three to four bright green, tender-crisp asparagus spears are neatly arranged. A fresh lemon wedge and a sprinkle of additional chopped herbs provide a fresh garnish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, with balanced elements and moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately.
Pair with a crisp dry white wine.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the risotto.
instructions: Prepare asparagus: Blanch or roast asparagus until tender-crisp. Set aside.
Start risotto: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice: Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at edges.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Add broth: Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladleful to be absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy.

Finish risotto: Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter cubes, grated Parmesan, lemon zest, and half of the lemon juice. Stir in chopped parsley and chives. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid.
Prepare tuna: Pat tuna steaks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.

Sear tuna: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Place tuna steaks in hot pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare (adjust time for desired doneness).
Rest tuna: Remove tuna from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate: Ladle a generous portion of risotto onto each plate. Place a seared tuna steak on top or beside the risotto. Arrange blanched asparagus spears next to the tuna. Garnish with a lemon wedge and extra fresh herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken with Peas
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of creamy garlic chicken with peas is presented on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The chicken, cut into irregular, homely chunks, is coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Vibrant green peas are generously mixed throughout, providing pops of color. The chicken chunks are nestled naturally, some overlapping, with no fanning. A scattering of fresh, roughly chopped green parsley provides a functional, fresh garnish. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen. Standard everyday silverware, a fork and knife, are placed casually beside the plate. Warm, soft lighting from above illuminates the dish, highlighting the creamy texture and natural colors of the ingredients. The background is minimal, hinting at a comfortable home environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes or steamed white rice.
Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides, about 6-8 minutes. Cook to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add frozen green peas. Stir to combine.
Simmer for 3-5 minutes, until chicken is heated through and peas are tender. Sauce will thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Bistec Salteado con Papas y Crema de Ají
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, robust single portion of "Bistec Salteado con Papas y Crema de Ají" is presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. A rustic bed of golden-brown, crispy fried potato batons forms the base. Large, irregular chunks of seared beef sirloin, caramelized to a deep brown, are nestled among the potatoes. Interspersed are tender-crisp, bright green halved green beans and softened, purple-edged julienned red onion strips, all coated in a glossy, savory dark sauce. A generous, creamy drizzle of pale yellow aji mayonnaise cascades over the beef and vegetables. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered artfully as a garnish. The dish exhibits varied textures and rich, earthy colors. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fluffy steamed white rice to absorb the rich sauce.
Offer extra crema de ají (aji mayonnaise) in a small side bowl for dipping.
instructions: Heat 200ml vegetable oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Cut potatoes into 1cm x 1cm x 6cm batons. Fry potato batons in batches until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt.
Pat beef chunks dry. Cut beef sirloin into 3cm chunks. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large wok or heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat. Sear beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pan.
Cut red onion into thick julienne. Add red onion to the same pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened.
Trim and halve green beans. Mince garlic. Add green beans and minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pan. Add soy sauce, red wine vinegar, and 10g aji amarillo paste. Stir quickly to combine. Cook for 1 minute.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with remaining 20g aji amarillo paste. Mix well to create the crema de ají.
To serve, divide crispy potatoes among 4 plates. Spoon beef and vegetable mixture over potatoes. Drizzle generously with crema de ají. Roughly chop fresh cilantro and garnish.
notes: This dish is inspired by traditional Peruvian Lomo Saltado, with green beans and aji mayonnaise as modern additions.
High heat cooking is crucial for proper "salteado" technique, ensuring a smoky flavor and tender beef.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken with Smoky Chocolate Sauce and Savory Custard Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A modern white porcelain dinner plate holds a visually striking main course. A pool of rich, glossy, deep brown smoky chocolate sauce forms the base. Centered on the sauce are thick, golden-seared chicken breast pieces, showcasing a crisp, caramelized exterior. Beside the chicken, a light golden savory egg custard, perfectly molded from its ramekin, sits gracefully. The dish is finished with a scattering of toasted, golden-brown savory crumble, which subtly incorporates colorful flecks from the 100s and 1000s, adding an unexpected visual pop and textural contrast without overwhelming the savory profile. The overall presentation is clean and refined, with moderate negative space, offering a sophisticated yet approachable appearance. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures and warm tones of the dish.
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, heavy cream, Parmesan, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Pour mixture into 4 small oven-safe ramekins (approx. 150ml capacity).

Place ramekins in a baking dish. Fill baking dish with hot water halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Bake at 160°C for 25-30 minutes, or until set but slightly wobbly. Remove from water bath. Let cool slightly.
In a small bowl, combine breadcrumbs, melted butter, 100s and 1000s, dried parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Spread mixture on a small baking sheet.
Bake at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Watch carefully. Remove from oven.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium. Add butter, diced onion, and a pinch of salt. Sauté until onion softens, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits.
Stir in chopped dark chocolate and sugar until chocolate melts and sauce is smooth. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon smoky chocolate sauce onto the center of each plate. Slice each chicken breast into thick chunks or keep whole. Place chicken over the sauce.
Gently invert each savory custard onto the plate next to the chicken. Sprinkle the savory crumble over the chicken and custard. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Seared Beef with Tomato-Onion Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A thick, perfectly seared beef sirloin steak, cooked to a juicy medium-rare, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The steak exhibits a rich, dark brown crust from pan-searing. A vibrant, reddish-orange tomato-onion reduction, thick and glossy, is generously spooned beneath and partially over the beef. Visible within the sauce are soft, caramelized pieces of diced onion. Delicate, creamy shavings of Parmesan cheese are scattered artfully over the beef and sauce. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley adds a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The presentation is organized yet organic, with ample negative space. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and colors.
instructions: Pat beef steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.
Sear steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until a deep brown crust forms. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove steaks from pan. Place on a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the same pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and hot sauce. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in butter until melted and incorporated, making the sauce glossy. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
To serve, spoon a generous amount of tomato-onion reduction onto each plate. Place one seared beef steak on top of the sauce.
Garnish with parmesan shavings and chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.
Allowing the beef to rest is crucial for tenderness and juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Filet, Forest Mushroom Puree, Asparagus, Mustard Jus
recipes.visual_description: A meticulously composed single portion of seared beef filet on a large, pristine white bone china plate. The beef, cut into two thick, perfectly seared medallions with a rosy medium-rare interior, is positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent to the beef, a smooth, dark forest mushroom puree forms an elegant quenelle. Three vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched to retain their crispness, are artfully arranged parallel to each other, adding a linear element. A small, neatly folded parcel of emerald green Swiss chard provides a subtle textural and color contrast. A glossy, amber-hued mustard jus is carefully spooned in an organic curve around the main components, catching the light. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the precision and minimalism of the plating. A single delicate sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the beef. The scene is set on a premium grey veined marble surface with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's contours against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Season beef filets generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear beef filets 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Transfer beef to a wire rack. Rest for 10 minutes.
Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic and shallot.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté minced shallot and garlic until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until tender and liquid evaporates.
Transfer cooked mushrooms to a blender. Add 30g unsalted butter and fresh thyme. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Trim tough ends from asparagus spears.
Blanch asparagus in salted boiling water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well.
Separate Swiss chard leaves from stems. Blanch leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds. Shock in ice bath. Squeeze out excess water.
Roll or fold blanched chard leaves into small, neat bundles or rectangles. Gently warm with a knob of butter before plating.
Deglaze the pan with beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Whisk in Dijon mustard and remaining 30g unsalted butter until the jus is emulsified and glossy. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice each beef filet into two thick, even pieces.
Place the beef pieces slightly off-center on a large plate.
Spoon a quenelle of the forest mushroom puree beside the beef.
Arrange three blanched asparagus spears artfully on the plate.
Carefully place the Swiss chard element near the other components.
Spoon the mustard jus in an organic curve around the plated elements.
Garnish with a small, delicate sprig of fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken & Mushroom Bites
recipes.visual_description: A homely, close-up view of several irregularly shaped, golden-brown chicken and mushroom bites, approximately 4-5 cm in diameter, casually piled on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. The bites show flecks of red chili and finely diced mushrooms. Small, vibrant green broccoli florets are loosely arranged alongside the bites, some touching, some slightly overlapping. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley rests over the bites. The plate sits on a well-used, slightly worn wooden dining table. A simple, light-colored cloth napkin is casually placed to the side. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen, casting soft shadows. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere without distraction, possibly a blurred view of a water glass or a salt shaker. The overall presentation is unpretentious, comforting, and perfectly suited for a casual home snack.
instructions: Finely dice mushrooms and onion. Mince garlic.
Cut broccoli into small florets.
In a large bowl, combine chicken mince, diced mushrooms, diced onion, minced garlic, dried chili flakes, egg, breadcrumbs, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form the mixture into small, irregular bite-sized patties or nuggets.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add chicken bites to the pan in batches. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While bites are cooking, steam or boil broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley.
Serve chicken and mushroom bites hot alongside steamed broccoli. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Tofu Medallions with Wood Ear Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared golden-brown tofu medallion is positioned off-center in a deep, elegant white bone china bowl. The tofu, precisely cut into a thick round, features a crisp exterior and a tender, creamy interior. Adjacent to the tofu, a small, artful cluster of glossy, dark wood ear mushroom pieces, precisely julienned, adds a contrasting texture and deep earthy tone. The bowl is filled with a crystal-clear, amber-hued wood ear mushroom consommé, which subtly envelops the components. A single, delicately crispy curry leaf, vibrant green, is perched atop the tofu or beside the mushroom, providing a precise pop of color and a hint of aromatic spice. The composition is highly minimalist, with abundant negative space showcasing the purity of each element. The setting features a polished grey veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and a single, elegant silver spoon. Dramatic professional lighting creates subtle shadows, emphasizing the dish's refined simplicity.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut into four 2cm thick medallions. Whisk 15ml soy sauce with a pinch of salt and white pepper. Marinate tofu medallions for 15 minutes.
Rehydrate dried wood ear mushrooms in warm water for 30 minutes. Drain, rinse thoroughly, and trim tough bases. Reserve 30g for braising, finely julienne the remaining 20g for the consommé.

In a large pot, combine vegetable stock, ginger, garlic, shallots, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, cloves, black peppercorns, and the julienned 20g wood ear mushrooms. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes.

Strain the stock through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Return liquid to a clean pot. Whisk egg whites until foamy. Add egg whites to the cool stock. Slowly bring to a simmer over medium-low heat without stirring, allowing a 'raft' to form. Gently simmer for 15 minutes.

Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a damp cheesecloth, avoiding disturbing the raft. Season consommé with 15ml soy sauce, salt, and white pepper to taste. Keep warm.
In a small pan, heat a touch of oil. Add the reserved 30g wood ear mushrooms. Sauté briefly. Add 50ml of the finished consommé. Simmer for 5 minutes until tender and glossy.
Heat neutral oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear tofu medallions for 4 minutes per side, until golden-brown and crisp.
In a small, dry pan, gently toast curry leaves over low heat until brittle and fragrant. Be careful not to burn.

Place one seared tofu medallion off-center in each deep serving bowl. Arrange a small, artful cluster of braised wood ear mushrooms next to the tofu. Carefully pour the hot, clear consommé around the tofu and mushrooms. Garnish each dish with one or two crispy curry leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: While soy sauce is not a traditional staple in Sri Lankan cuisine, a minimal amount is used here to provide a subtle umami depth in this modern, refined interpretation.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single vibrant Mexican stuffed bell pepper sits centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The bell pepper half, slightly softened yet holding its shape, showcases its rich color – perhaps a deep red or sunny yellow. It is generously filled with a hearty, savory mixture. Visible elements of the filling include golden corn kernels, dark black beans, small diced red tomatoes, and finely diced orange carrots, all bound together with seasoned rice. A light golden-brown layer of melted Monterey Jack cheese, if used, bubbles gently on top. A sprinkle of bright green, chopped fresh cilantro contrasts beautifully with the warm tones of the filling. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting and authentic casual dining presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Provide a side of salsa roja or crema (Mexican sour cream).
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced carrot. Cook 3 minutes more.
Stir in diced tomatoes, cooked rice, black beans, corn, chili powder, cumin, and oregano.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, until liquid is mostly absorbed.
Season filling with salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon filling evenly into bell pepper halves.
Cover baking dish loosely with foil.
Bake 30 minutes. Remove foil.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over peppers, if using.
Bake uncovered 10-15 minutes more, until peppers are tender and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Parmesan Beef & Roasted Vegetable Stack
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust portion of Parmesan Beef & Roasted Vegetable Stack is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The stack stands tall, showcasing distinct, well-defined layers: deep purple roasted eggplant rounds, rich reddish-brown minced beef ragu, vibrant red and yellow roasted bell pepper strips, and dark cremini mushroom quarters. A generous, golden-brown crust of melted, bubbly Parmesan cheese crowns the top. Bright green fresh basil leaves, torn, are scattered over the top. The elements are composed centrally, leaving moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to sop up the savory sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a robust red wine like Chianti or Montepulciano.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Slice eggplants into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Quarter mushrooms.
Toss eggplant and bell pepper with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred.
While vegetables roast, heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add minced beef. Brown beef, breaking it apart. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced chili (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape bottom of pot. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Stir in tomato passata, dried oregano, 5g chopped fresh basil, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish or individual oven-safe dishes.

Begin layering: Place a layer of roasted eggplant at the bottom. Top with a layer of beef ragu. Add a layer of roasted bell peppers, then scatter some quartered mushrooms and cherry tomatoes. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan.
Repeat layering until all ingredients are used, ending with a generous layer of Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is golden and bubbly, and the stack is heated through.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the beef ragu ahead of time.
Adjust chili quantity to preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Bell Pepper Basil Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Chicken and Bell Pepper Basil Noodles sits in a rustic, slightly irregular ceramic bowl, showcasing a medley of colors and textures. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed with vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, soft, sliced brown mushrooms, and translucent flat rice noodles. The fresh, dark green basil leaves are visibly tossed throughout, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is casual and natural, with ingredients overlapping and some noodles spilling slightly over the bowl's edge, as if just served from a family meal. The bowl rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. Adjacent to the bowl, a pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests casually. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, creating a cozy and lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of chili oil or sriracha on the side for those who prefer extra heat.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
instructions: In a bowl, toss chicken chunks with 15 ml soy sauce and cornstarch. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, water, and chili flakes (if using).

Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add chicken. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.

Add remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add red and yellow bell pepper strips. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until crisp-tender. Add sliced mushrooms. Stir-fry for another 2 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add cooked noodles and the prepared sauce. Toss everything together for 1-2 minutes until well combined and heated through.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh basil leaves until just wilted.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust spice level by varying chili flakes.
Ensure noodles are not overcooked; they should be firm enough to stir-fry without breaking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Champiñones Picante
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo con Champiñones Picante is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are nestled in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. The sauce, vibrant red from crushed tomatoes and rehydrated Guajillo chilies, is studded with earthy sliced Cremini mushrooms, diced red bell pepper, and small cubes of Spanish chorizo. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a bright green contrast. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing the sauce to flow around the chicken and vegetables. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan rústico) for dipping.
Serve alongside simple saffron rice.
instructions: Rehydrate Guajillo chilies: Place chilies in hot water for 20 minutes. Remove stems and seeds. Chop finely.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced chorizo to the pan. Cook until crispy. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Stir in chopped rehydrated chilies, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring sauce to a simmer. Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Add cooked chorizo.
Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Uncover and simmer 5-10 minutes more to slightly thicken sauce, if needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best flavor, use good quality Spanish chorizo.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Green Pea & Celery Soup with Beer-Braised Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of soup is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl in an earth tone. The soup is a vibrant, natural green, smooth and flowing. A small, intentional dollop of glistening, dark brown beer-braised onions rests off-center on the soup surface. A few fresh, bright green celery leaves are placed delicately beside the onions, offering a contrasting fresh element. The setting features a light reclaimed wood table surface and an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. The background is minimalist with soft natural lighting, showcasing the dish as the main subject. This clean, uncluttered scene highlights the pure beauty of each ingredient with a simple, clean composition.
instructions: Prepare fermented pea and celery base: Blend 250g green peas with 2 celery stalks and enough water to create a thick slurry. Add 2% salt by weight of the slurry. Transfer to a clean jar. Seal. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy.

Cook beer-braised onions: Thinly slice onions. Heat olive oil in a pot. Add sliced onions. Cook over medium-low heat until softened, about 10 minutes. Pour in dark beer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until onions are very tender and beer has mostly evaporated, about 20-30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Make soup base: In a large pot, combine chicken stock, remaining 250g green peas, and 2 chopped celery stalks. Bring to a simmer. Cook until peas and celery are tender, about 10-15 minutes.

Combine and blend soup: Add the fermented pea and celery mixture to the soup base. Stir well. Carefully blend the soup until smooth using an immersion blender or regular blender. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for extra smoothness, if desired.

Season and serve: Return soup to pot. Gently reheat. Stir in verjus. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with a spoonful of beer-braised onions and a few fresh inner celery leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Roasted Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a rustic, everyday ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, natural texture, typical of a home kitchen. A single, modest individual portion of spaghetti is twirled neatly onto the plate, coated generously in a vibrant, creamy, reddish-orange roasted bell pepper sauce. The sauce has a smooth, slightly textured consistency, clinging well to the pasta strands. Bits of finely sliced red chili are visible, providing small pops of darker red against the sauce. A few torn fresh green basil leaves are casually scattered over the top, adding a fresh, aromatic contrast. The overall arrangement is natural and organic, with the pasta forming a gentle mound. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. In the background, a simple cloth napkin is casually draped, and a fork with a natural handle rests beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. The scene evokes a comfortable, lived-in family dining atmosphere, focusing entirely on the appetizing, hearty pasta dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve and deseed bell peppers. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skins are charred and soft.
Remove peppers from oven. Place in a bowl. Cover tightly with cling film for 10 minutes to steam.
Once cool enough, peel skins from roasted peppers. Discard skins. Roughly chop the roasted pepper flesh.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and finely sliced chili to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped roasted bell peppers and crushed tomatoes to the pan. Stir well. Add vegetable broth.
Simmer the sauce for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until smooth. If too thick, add a little reserved pasta water to reach desired consistency.
Return the blended sauce to the pan. Add the drained pasta. Toss well to coat. Add more reserved pasta water if needed to loosen sauce.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil and a sprinkle of Parmesan or nutritional yeast if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim, centered on a rustic wooden dining table. The dish features tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (approximately 3 cm) mixed with soft, slightly browned potato cubes (2 cm). A vibrant orange-red hot sauce lightly coats the ingredients, peeking through the generous layer of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese that forms a golden crust over the top. Some cheese pulls are visible, indicating its gooey texture. A few chopped green chives are scattered over the melted cheese, adding a fresh color contrast. The overall arrangement is natural and comforting, as if plated directly from the baking dish. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of coleslaw or a simple green salad.
Offer extra hot sauce on the side for those who prefer more heat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine chicken chunks and potato cubes.
Add olive oil, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread the chicken and potato mixture in a single layer in a large baking dish (approx. 30x20 cm).
Bake for 25 minutes.
Remove dish from oven. Stir the chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven and bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Remove dish from oven. Pour hot sauce over the mixture and toss gently to coat.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Return to oven and bake for 5-7 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with chopped chives, if desired.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken with Bell Peppers, Mushrooms, and Mozzarella Rice
