Roast bell peppers for 25-30 minutes. Skins should be charred and flesh soft. Remove from oven. Place in a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap for 10 minutes.
Peel skins from bell peppers. Discard skins. Slice bell pepper flesh into thick strips or large chunks. Set aside.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add red onion to skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and chili powder. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pitted cherries to skillet. Cook 3-5 minutes, mashing some cherries with a spoon.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Add dark chocolate. Stir until melted and smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.
Transfer sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until smooth. Return sauce to skillet.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Add roasted bell pepper strips.
Add grated cheddar cheese. Stir constantly until cheese melts and coats pasta. Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Turkey Medallions with Mediterranean Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Turkey Medallions is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a light wooden table surface. Two golden-brown, pan-seared turkey medallions, left as whole pieces, are positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent to the turkey, a vibrant Mediterranean relish, featuring halved bright red cherry tomatoes, dark Kalamata olive halves, and finely diced red onion, is spooned in an organic pile. The relish offers a burst of color and a mix of soft and firm textures. Beside the relish, quartered hard-boiled eggs with their distinct yellow yolks and white whites are arranged, contrasting with cubes of creamy green avocado and crisp diced cucumber. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens over the components. Fresh green chopped parsley and basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding freshness and a pop of color. A folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh ingredients and refined presentation.
instructions: Hard boil eggs. Cool completely. Peel. Quarter. Set aside.
Prepare turkey. Pat turkey medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Sear turkey. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear turkey medallions 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove from pan. Rest 5 minutes.

Make relish. In a bowl, combine halved cherry tomatoes, halved olives, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, 30ml olive oil, and red wine vinegar. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in half the chopped parsley.
Prepare salad. In a separate bowl, gently combine diced cucumber and diced avocado. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Plate dish. Place two turkey medallions on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of Mediterranean relish beside turkey. Arrange hard-boiled egg quarters and avocado-cucumber salad on the plate. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Style Braised Pork with Tomato and Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Greek Style Braised Pork is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tender pork shoulder chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are deep brown from searing and submerged in a rich, rustic tomato-oregano sauce. The sauce is a vibrant deep red, flecked with softened diced onions and hints of green from dried oregano. A scattering of fresh bright green chopped parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The dish has a comforting, hearty appearance with visible texture from the braised pork and chunky sauce. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and depth of color. A small, traditional ceramic bowl with a side of fluffy white rice or orzo pasta is placed next to the main plate. A simple, sturdy fork and knife rest beside the plate, ready for dining. The overall scene is clean, inviting, and authentically Greek.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with orzo pasta (Kritharaki), rice, or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
A side of Greek salad (Horiatiki Salata) complements the richness.
Optionally, sprinkle with crumbled feta cheese before serving.
instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks, 4-5 cm, in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, bay leaves, and broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until pork is very tender.
Stir occasionally. If sauce becomes too thick, add a little more broth or water.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, braise the pork for at least 2 hours.
This dish tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Ragu Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, homely scene featuring 8-12 Pork Ragu Crostini arranged casually on a light-colored, well-used wooden dining table. The crostini are placed on a simple, round ceramic platter with natural imperfections, allowing for some negative space. Each crostini features a golden-brown, toasted baguette slice, generously topped with rich, deep red pork ragu. The ragu showcases tender, shredded pork chunks, diced tomatoes, and flecks of green herbs. A sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese adds a light contrast. Fresh green basil chiffonade is scattered over the ragu. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. A casually folded, plain linen cloth napkin is placed beside the platter. The focus is entirely on the inviting, comfort-food appearance of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of an antipasto spread
Pair with a glass of red wine
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until browned. Remove pork.
Dice the onion. Mince the garlic cloves. Add onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared pork to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until pork is very tender and shreds easily.
Remove pork from pot. Shred pork using two forks. Return shredded pork to the sauce. Stir well to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Toast baguette slices in a toaster or oven until golden and crisp.
Spoon a generous amount of pork ragu onto each toasted baguette slice. Arrange on a serving platter.
Chiffonade fresh basil leaves. Garnish crostini with fresh basil and optional grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: The pork ragu can be prepared a day in advance and reheated gently before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sirloin Steak Frites with Burger Aioli
recipes.visual_description: A single seared beef sirloin steak, cooked to a rich brown exterior and tender interior, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The steak is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. Beside it, a generous pile of golden, crispy frites, cut into perfect batons, is neatly arranged. A small, creamy dollop of pale orange burger aioli is placed elegantly on the plate near the frites. The dish is garnished with a light sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley over both the steak and frites. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing a refined casual dining presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp green salad with a vinaigrette dressing.
Offer additional quick-pickled gherkins or red onions on the side.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 1 cm x 1 cm batons for frites. Rinse in cold water until clear. Pat very dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 160°C. Blanch frites in batches for 5-7 minutes until tender but not browned. Remove. Drain on paper towels. Increase oil temperature to 190°C.
While frites blanch, prepare burger aioli. Mince garlic and shallot very finely. Chop parsley finely.
In a bowl, combine mayonnaise, ketchup, dill pickle relish, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, minced garlic, and minced shallot. Stir well. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside.
Season sirloin steaks generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat a large cast-iron or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Add olive oil until shimmering.
Sear steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Add butter to the pan during the last minute. Baste steaks with melted butter.
Remove steaks from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5-7 minutes.
Fry blanched frites in batches at 190°C for 2-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove. Drain well. Season immediately with salt.
Slice rested steaks into thick chunks, or serve whole. Do not fan slices.
Plate each steak alongside a mound of crispy frites. Place a dollop or small ramekin of burger aioli next to the frites. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley over the steak and frites.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork & Tomato Bruschetta Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant Pork & Tomato Bruschetta Bites are artfully arranged on a sleek, dark slate serving platter. Each bite features a crisp, golden-brown toasted baguette slice, topped first with a generous mound of finely diced, savory cooked pork. The pork is seasoned and browned, offering a rich, umami base. Crowning the pork is a vibrant, fresh mixture of small-cubed ripe red tomatoes, flecked with bright green chopped oregano and basil. A thin, glossy drizzle of dark balsamic glaze elegantly zigzags across the top of each bite, adding a touch of sophisticated sheen. Scattered fresh basil leaves provide a final pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is clean and professional, with consistent spacing between each canape. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, with natural, even lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors of the ingredients. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, showcasing the dish as the main subject.
instructions: Finely dice the red onion and mince the garlic.
Heat 15 ml of olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion and sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground pork to the pan. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Drain any excess fat.
Season the cooked pork with salt and black pepper. Set aside.
Dice the ripe plum tomatoes into small cubes. Roughly chop fresh oregano and fresh basil.
In a small bowl, combine diced tomatoes, chopped oregano, and half of the chopped basil. Drizzle with 5 ml of olive oil. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Stir gently.
Slice the baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Lightly brush both sides of each slice with the remaining 10 ml of olive oil.
Toast baguette slices in a dry pan or under a broiler until golden and crisp, about 2-3 minutes per side. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
To assemble, spoon a small portion of the cooked pork onto each toasted baguette slice.
Top the pork with a spoonful of the fresh tomato mixture.
Arrange the assembled bruschetta bites on a serving platter.
Drizzle a thin line of balsamic glaze over each bruschetta bite.
Garnish with the remaining fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: White Bean and Rosemary Pizza
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, round pizza rests on a simple white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a golden-brown, slightly blistered crust. The surface is topped with melted, creamy mozzarella cheese, revealing patches of the subtly sauced crust beneath. Scattered generously across the cheese are tender, ivory-colored whole white beans, interspersed with vibrant green fresh rosemary leaves and thinly sliced crimson red onion crescents. A few halved, bright red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color. A light drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on the ingredients. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with ample negative space on the plate. The background features a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin, illuminated by natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer a glass of light-bodied red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C. Place a pizza stone or baking sheet in the oven to heat.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans. Pat dry.
Finely chop garlic. Remove rosemary leaves from stems; chop finely.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add garlic and half the rosemary. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add drained beans to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring gently. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Thinly slice red onion into crescents. Halve cherry tomatoes.
On a lightly floured surface, stretch or roll pizza dough into a 30 cm round.
Carefully transfer dough to the hot pizza stone or baking sheet.
Drizzle remaining 30 ml olive oil over the dough. Spread evenly.
Scatter mozzarella pieces over the dough. Distribute bean mixture over the cheese.
Arrange red onion slices and cherry tomato halves on top.
Sprinkle with remaining fresh rosemary.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 2 minutes before slicing and serving.
notes: For a crispier crust, ensure your oven and pizza stone/baking sheet are fully preheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Brown Rice Risotto with Roasted Tomatoes, Leeks, and Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, rich Brown Rice Risotto is presented in a wide, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a fluid, flowing consistency. The nutty brown rice grains are tender, interspersed with soft, golden sautéed leeks and vibrant red, slightly blistered roasted cherry tomatoes. Nestled atop the risotto are two thick, golden-brown medallions of seared chicken breast, displaying a perfectly cooked interior. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped basil, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a standard fork and knife and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and appealing colors. The background is clean and subtly blurred, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple green salad with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the creamy risotto.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.quantity: 30ml, plus more for roasting and searing

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Trim leeks. Slice white and light green parts into 1 cm thick rounds. Wash thoroughly to remove dirt. Drain well.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced leeks. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until very soft and lightly golden. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a separate large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Let rest for 5 minutes. Slice thickly into medallions.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt 30g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook for 5 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add brown rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains. If using, pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Add one ladleful of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir constantly until broth is almost fully absorbed. Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding more. This process will take 30-40 minutes for brown rice.
When rice is al dente and creamy, stir in roasted tomatoes and sautéed leeks. Remove pot from heat.
Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute until the risotto is creamy and fluid (mantecatura). Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve risotto immediately in wide, shallow bowls. Top each portion with thick slices of seared chicken. Garnish generously with fresh chopped basil.
notes: Brown rice takes longer to cook than Arborio rice for risotto; adjust cooking time accordingly.
Maintain a fluid, creamy consistency; risotto should not be dry or stiff.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey Pineapple Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Honey Pineapple Chicken Stir-fry is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl. Cubed chicken pieces, cooked until golden-brown, are mixed with vibrant yellow pineapple chunks, all coated in a glossy, rich amber sauce. The chicken and pineapple are casually arranged, naturally overlapping, with some pieces visibly seared. Bright green sliced spring onions are sprinkled over the top, adding a fresh contrast. The dish is served over a bed of fluffy white steamed rice, filling the bowl adequately but not overflowing. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl. Lighting is warm and cozy, like natural light from a kitchen window. The scene is uncluttered, showcasing the hearty, comforting home-style meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with hot steamed white rice.
Offer a small side of pickled vegetables for a refreshing contrast.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Cut fresh pineapple into 2 cm chunks.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Set aside.
In a separate small bowl, combine cornstarch and water to make a slurry. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes to the hot wok. Cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). This takes about 5-7 minutes.
Add pineapple chunks to the wok with the cooked chicken. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the chicken and pineapple. Bring to a simmer.
Stir the cornstarch slurry again, then slowly pour into the simmering sauce while stirring constantly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken and pineapple.
Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil.
Garnish with sliced spring onions. Serve immediately over steamed white rice.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty British Sausage and Root Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: The stew is presented in a deep, rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl, generously filled. The rich, savory stew base is a deep mahogany, studded with vibrant green peas, bright orange diced carrots and squash, quartered brown mushrooms, and dark red kidney beans. Prominently featured are substantial, golden-brown seared sausage chunks. A small, creamy dollop of mayonnaise rests delicately on one side of the stew, contrasting with the rich tones. A generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese melts slightly into the surface. A fresh, upright cluster of vibrant green sunflower sprouts provides a final height and freshness. The bowl is centered on a simple white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a warm wooden table. A folded cotton napkin sits to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's hearty texture and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a pint of traditional British ale
instructions: Remove sausage meat from casings. Break into rough 2cm chunks.
Dice carrots, celery, and onion into 1cm pieces. Peel and dice squash into 2cm cubes. Quarter mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Brown thoroughly on all sides. Remove sausage from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook 8 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic, dried chili flakes, quartered mushrooms, and diced squash. Cook 5 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 1 minute. Pour in beer and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add lentils and beef stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 25 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
Return browned sausage chunks to the pot. Add drained kidney beans and frozen green peas. Simmer uncovered 5-7 minutes, until peas are tender and flavors meld. Ensure sausage is cooked through.
Season stew with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Ladle stew into serving bowls. Top each serving with a dollop of mayonnaise, a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese, and a small cluster of fresh sunflower sprouts.

recipes.recipe_name: Southern-Style Kohlrabi and Collard Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, dark green stew fills a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. Large pieces of tender, deep green collard greens are prominent, intertwined with soft, pale green kohlrabi cubes and bright red bell pepper dice. The stew has a rich, slightly thick, reddish-brown broth, indicating a long simmer. A generous scattering of fresh, thinly sliced green scallion rings garnishes the top, adding a pop of vibrant color. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, next to a casually folded cloth napkin. The setting is warm and inviting, illuminated by soft, natural kitchen light, evoking a homely family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot cornbread.
Offer a bottle of hot sauce on the side.

ingredients.name: Kohlrabi
ingredients.quantity: 2 large, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Collard greens
ingredients.quantity: 500g, tough stems removed, chopped into 2-3 cm pieces

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1 large, cored, seeded, and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.quantity: 4, thinly sliced (separate white and green parts)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add diced bell pepper and white parts of scallions. Cook 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced kohlrabi, chopped collard greens, diced tomatoes with their juice, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover.
Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until kohlrabi is tender and collards are very soft. Stir occasionally.
Stir in apple cider vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish each serving with green parts of sliced scallions.
notes: For extra depth, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the spices.
A small amount of liquid smoke can enhance the smoky flavor if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Kohlrabi & Roasted Bell Pepper Medley
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic and natural presentation of vibrant vegetables on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Thinly sliced, pale green kohlrabi discs are arranged in a clean, slightly overlapping pattern, showcasing their delicate texture. Beside them, roasted bell pepper wedges in rich red and yellow hues display tender, slightly caramelized edges. Crispy, deep green collard leaf pieces are scattered organically, adding textural contrast. A luminous, verdant scallion oil is generously drizzled over the components, with finely sliced fresh green scallions providing a final, bright garnish. The composition emphasizes natural forms and colors, with ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light reclaimed wood surface and an undyed linen napkin, under soft natural light.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Kohlrabi: (Note: This step requires pre-preparation). Peel one kohlrabi. Slice into 3 mm thick rounds or 5 cm long matchsticks. Dissolve 20g pickling salt in 1 litre non-chlorinated water to make a 2% brine. Submerge kohlrabi in brine in a clean jar. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days until tangy and slightly effervescent. Store in refrigerator.

Roast Bell Peppers: Preheat oven to 200°C. Core and deseed both bell peppers. Cut each into 8-10 large wedges. Toss bell pepper wedges with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of sea salt, and black pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and edges are slightly charred.
Prepare Kohlrabi Discs: Peel the second kohlrabi. Slice into very thin, uniform discs (1-2 mm thick) using a mandoline if possible.

Crisp Collard Greens: Wash collard greens thoroughly. Remove tough stems. Tear leaves into large, irregular pieces. Toss collard green pieces with 15 ml olive oil and a pinch of sea salt. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Bake at 180°C for 8-12 minutes, or until crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Make Scallion Oil: Wash scallions. Separate white and green parts. Finely chop the white and light green parts. Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add chopped white and light green scallion parts. Cook gently for 5 minutes until fragrant, without browning. Remove from heat. Let steep for 10 minutes. Strain if desired for a clearer oil, or leave scallion pieces in.

Assemble Dish: Arrange thin kohlrabi discs artfully on each plate. Place roasted bell pepper wedges alongside. Scatter crispy collard greens over the plate. Drizzle generously with scallion oil. Finely slice the remaining green parts of the scallions for garnish. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe highlights zero-waste by encouraging the use of kohlrabi peels and bell pepper cores for vegetable stock. Collard green stems can be finely chopped and added to roasted vegetables for another dish, or used in stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto with Butternut Squash, Leek, and Pancetta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Risotto with Butternut Squash, Leek, and Pancetta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, positioned centrally on a simple wooden table surface. The risotto is fluid and naturally spread, not formed into a ring. Its rich, creamy texture is evident, with the vibrant orange of tender, roasted butternut squash cubes interspersed throughout. Thinly sliced, softened leek pieces provide subtle green accents, while small, deep red cherry tomato halves add pops of color. Crispy, golden-brown diced pancetta is sprinkled over the top, offering a textural contrast. The dish is garnished with a generous scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley and delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a cotton napkin beside the plate and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures against a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background, creating an authentic Italian casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed hot and creamy.
Accompany with a crisp green salad dressed with a simple vinaigrette.
Pair with a dry, crisp white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Soave.
instructions: Peel butternut squash. Cut into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Set aside.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pot.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add thinly sliced leek. Cook for another 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until the edges of the grains are translucent. This is tostatura.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed. This deglazes the pot.

Begin adding hot stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladleful to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is al dente and creamy. Maintain a fluid consistency.
Stir in roasted butternut squash cubes and halved cherry tomatoes during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until creamy and emulsified. This is mantecatura. Add crispy pancetta.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and additional shaved Parmesan.
notes: Use high-quality Arborio rice for best results.
Keep the stock hot throughout the cooking process to maintain the risotto's temperature and creamy texture.
Constant stirring is key for releasing the starch from the rice, which creates the creamy consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Butternut Squash and Shrimp Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Roasted Butternut Squash and Shrimp Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Rigatoni pasta forms a neat base, lightly coated in a shimmering, light sauce. Generous 2 cm cubes of roasted butternut squash, with subtly caramelized edges, are interspersed. Plump, whole pan-seared shrimp, displaying a rosy pink hue, are arranged naturally atop the pasta. Vibrant green torn basil leaves are scattered over the dish. Colors are natural: warm orange, rosy pink, golden pasta, fresh green. Textures show tender squash, succulent shrimp, and al dente pasta. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with standard silver flatware. A folded cotton napkin sits beside. Natural, even lighting highlights the food. The background suggests a modern bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the light sauce.

ingredients.name: Butternut squash, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
Dry white wine or vegetable broth

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss butternut squash cubes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Turn halfway through.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Pour in white wine or vegetable broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Let liquid reduce slightly, about 1 minute.
Add cooked pasta, roasted squash, and half of the torn basil to the skillet. Toss gently to combine. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to create a light sauce consistency.
Season with additional salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Use fresh, high-quality shrimp for best flavor and texture.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Truffle & Arbequina Olive Oil Gâteau
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably cut slice of the Chocolate Truffle & Arbequina Olive Oil Gâteau is presented on a pristine, elegant porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice reveals distinct, architectural layers: a dark, moist black truffle chocolate sponge base, followed by a creamy, rich Arbequina olive oil ganache, and topped with a light, airy orange blossom mousse. The entire slice is enrobed in a glossy, reflective black truffle mirror glaze, showcasing its smooth, even surface. A thin, precisely cut strip of vibrant candied orange peel rests delicately beside the slice, complementing the dark hues. A slender, artfully angled dark chocolate shard stands upright, adding a refined textural contrast. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting the dessert as a sculptural centerpiece. The setting is a pristine white marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in the background. Dramatic, professional lighting creates subtle shadows, emphasizing the dessert's sophisticated textures and forms, capturing a sense of minimalist luxury.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small cup of strong, dark Spanish coffee or a chilled glass of Pedro Ximénez sherry.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 15 cm round cake pan.
Melt 100g dark chocolate and butter together. Stir until smooth.
Whisk 100g sugar and eggs until pale and fluffy.
Fold melted chocolate mixture into egg mixture.
Sift flour and cocoa powder. Fold into batter until just combined.
Grate 5g fresh black truffle into the batter. Mix gently.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake 25-30 minutes. Cool completely.

For Olive Oil Ganache: Melt remaining 100g dark chocolate. Heat 50ml heavy cream until simmering. Pour hot cream over chocolate. Emulsify with a whisk. Stir in Arbequina olive oil. Grate 3g fresh black truffle into ganache. Chill until firm but spreadable.

For Orange Blossom Mousse: Bloom gelatin in cold water. Heat 100ml heavy cream. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Dissolve gelatin in hot cream. Whip remaining 150ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold gelatin mixture and orange blossom water into whipped cream.

For Truffle Glaze: Bloom remaining gelatin. Heat 50ml heavy cream, glucose, and condensed milk. Remove from heat. Stir in melted 50g dark chocolate and white food coloring. Stir in 2g grated fresh black truffle. Stir until smooth. Strain. Cool to 35°C.

To assemble: Slice cooled cake horizontally into two layers. Place one layer on a serving plate. Spread olive oil ganache evenly. Top with second cake layer. Spread orange blossom mousse over top. Chill 2 hours.
Pour truffle glaze over chilled cake, ensuring full coverage. Chill 30 minutes to set glaze.
Garnish with candied orange peel and a delicate chocolate shard before serving.
notes: Use a high-quality fresh black truffle for optimal aroma and flavor.
Ensure all components are at the correct temperature for precise assembly and glazing.
For best results, prepare the day before serving to allow flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Forestière
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken Forestière is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, cut into thick, rustic chunks, is nestled within a rich, off-white creamy sauce. The sauce is generously studded with browned, rustic-cut mushroom slices and finely diced onion, with visible flecks of fresh thyme and rosemary. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the dish. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin, and classic French flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an authentic bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
Pair with simple buttered egg noodles or roasted potatoes
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté 5-7 minutes until deeply browned and moisture has evaporated.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, thyme sprigs, rosemary sprigs, and cayenne pepper. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 10-12 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pan. Stir grated Parmesan cheese into the sauce until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Remove herb sprigs.
Slice chicken into thick, rustic chunks. Serve chicken with the creamy mushroom sauce spooned generously over it.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C internal temperature.
Adjust cayenne pepper to taste for desired heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Ahi Tuna, Artichoke Puree, Tomato-Olive Confit, Pasta Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of seared Ahi tuna is the focal point, presented as a thick, pristine slab with a subtle rosy-red interior and a golden-brown sear. It rests gracefully upon a smooth, verdant swirl of artichoke puree, its creamy texture visible. Around the base of the tuna, a vibrant confit of halved cherry tomatoes and finely sliced Kalamata olives is artfully placed, offering bursts of deep red and dark purple. A delicate, golden-brown pasta crisp stands elegantly upright, providing a contrasting architectural element. The plate, made of expensive bone china with a subtle pattern, is white Carrara marble. A few drops of brilliant green basil oil are meticulously dotted around the composition, adding aromatic and visual punctuation. Ample negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated simplicity. The setting features a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural qualities against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a sophisticated standalone main course in a fine-dining setting.
instructions: Prepare Artichoke Puree: Drain artichoke hearts. Sauté 2 minced garlic cloves in 15 ml olive oil. Add artichoke hearts. Cook 5 minutes. Add 100 ml water. Simmer until tender. Blend with 50 grams butter until silky smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Tomato-Olive Confit: Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice Kalamata olives. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Combine tomatoes, olives, minced garlic in a small saucepan. Cover with 100 ml extra virgin olive oil. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes. Tomatoes should be soft but retain shape. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Pasta Crisps: Cut fresh pasta sheets into desired shapes (e.g., 5 cm x 10 cm rectangles). Heat 50 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry pasta pieces until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Prepare Basil Oil: Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 50 ml extra virgin olive oil until smooth. Pass through a fine mesh sieve for a clear oil. Discard solids.

Sear Ahi Tuna: Pat tuna loin dry. Cut into 4 thick, equal portions. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until smoking. Add 15 ml olive oil. Sear tuna portions 60-90 seconds per side for rare internal temperature. Adjust cooking time for desired doneness. Rest tuna 2 minutes.

Plate the Dish: Spoon a swirl of artichoke puree onto the center of each plate. Place one seared tuna portion atop the puree. Artistically arrange a spoonful of tomato-olive confit around the tuna. Stand one pasta crisp vertically on the plate. Drizzle basil oil around the dish. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure Ahi tuna is sashimi-grade for optimal quality and texture.
Achieve a fluid consistency for the artichoke puree; adjust liquid as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Watermelon and Feta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Watermelon and Feta Salad is plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of colors and textures. Large, juicy 2cm diced watermelon cubes form the base, interspersed with smaller, crisp 1cm diced cucumber pieces. Very thinly sliced red onion rings add a delicate purple hue. Crumbled feta cheese, stark white and creamy, is scattered generously over the top, contrasting with the dark, halved Kalamata olives. Freshly chopped bright green mint leaves are sprinkled throughout, adding an aromatic pop. A light balsamic vinaigrette subtly glistens on the ingredients. The arrangement is natural and slightly mounded, allowing negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or grilled halloumi cheese.
instructions: Dice watermelon into 2cm cubes. Place in a large bowl.
Deseed cucumber. Dice into 1cm cubes. Add to bowl.
Very thinly slice red onion. Add to bowl.
Pit and halve Kalamata olives. Add to bowl.
Finely chop fresh mint. Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
Pour dressing over the watermelon, cucumber, onion, and olives. Gently toss to combine.
Crumble feta cheese over the salad. Gently fold in the chopped mint.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef and Beer Stew with Chili Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rich Braised Beef and Beer Stew is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. Generous chunks of tender, dark brown braised beef are nestled among soft, light brown potato pieces, all coated in a glossy, deep amber-brown sauce. A few vibrant slivers of red chili are visible, providing a subtle color contrast. The stew has a natural, organic flow, showing its hearty texture. It is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley, adding freshness and color. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware, a fork and spoon, are placed neatly beside the bowl on a folded cotton napkin. The setting features natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the rich sauce

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 grams, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, sliced red chili, and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low.
Braise for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add potato chunks to the pot. Continue to braise for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Rosemary Chicken with Mushrooms and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to tender perfection, anchors the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously draped with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce, featuring thinly sliced cremini mushrooms and finely chopped fresh rosemary. The sauce, glistening with a hint of butter, pools invitingly around the chicken. A scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese adorns the top, adding a delicate pale yellow hue and textural contrast. The earthy browns of the mushrooms, vibrant green of the rosemary, and crisp golden-brown of the chicken create a harmonious color palette. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 50g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Add diced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine (if using). Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in chicken broth and double cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add chopped rosemary. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return cooked chicken breasts to the pan. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Serve immediately, garnished with extra grated Parmesan and a fresh rosemary sprig.
notes: For enhanced flavor, use a mix of wild mushrooms like shiitake or oyster alongside cremini.
Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Tomato Garlic Pasta with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of pasta with a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce is artfully coiled on an off-white, rustic ceramic plate. The pasta strands are glistening, thoroughly coated in the rustic sauce. Small, irregular pieces of softened diced tomato and onion are visible within the sauce, along with flecks of dried oregano. A scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly coats the top, with a few fresh basil leaves torn and casually placed for color and aroma. The dish is presented on a worn, dark wooden dining table. A simple linen napkin is folded next to the plate. A traditional Italian fork and spoon rest beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add diced tomatoes. Stir well.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer sauce for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sauce should thicken slightly.
While sauce simmers, add pasta to boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 120ml pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta directly to the sauce.
Add reserved pasta water and half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Toss well to combine.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing sauce to coat pasta.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust sauce consistency with pasta water as needed.
Use good quality canned tomatoes for best flavor if fresh are not in season.

recipes.recipe_name: Harissa Shrimp & Fermented Fennel Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Harissa Shrimp & Fermented Fennel Pasta is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The seared shrimp, vibrant orange-pink, are interspersed throughout the pasta, which is a neutral beige. Thinly sliced, tender-crisp fresh fennel and translucent, pale slivers of fermented fennel are visible, adding texture and subtle color variations. Bright green chopped parsley and delicate fennel fronds are sprinkled over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. A light, creamy lemon-yogurt sauce lightly coats the ingredients, ensuring a cohesive look without being overly saucy. The arrangement is natural and unforced, highlighting each ingredient's individual beauty with ample negative space on the plate. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating gentle shadows. A hint of green from a minimalist plant in the background suggests an eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Fennel: Thinly slice one fennel bulb. Combine with 20g non-iodized salt per liter of water. Submerge in a clean jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy. Refrigerate.
Cook pasta: Boil salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Prepare shrimp: Pat shrimp dry. In a bowl, combine shrimp with 1 tablespoon harissa, lemon zest, 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.

Sauté fresh fennel: Thinly slice the second fennel bulb. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add sliced fennel. Sauté until tender-crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Remove fennel from pan. Set aside.

Cook shrimp: Add 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same pan. Increase heat to medium-high. Add marinated shrimp in a single layer. Cook 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from pan. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.

Make sauce: Reduce heat to low. Add minced garlic and chili flakes (if using) to the pan. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in remaining 1 tablespoon harissa. Add yogurt, lemon juice, and reserved pasta water. Whisk until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Combine ingredients: Add cooked pasta, sautéed fresh fennel, fermented fennel, and cooked shrimp to the pan with the sauce. Toss to combine. Ensure everything is well coated.
Finish: Stir in chopped parsley and chopped fennel fronds. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing the entire fennel bulb, including fronds. Consider using fennel cores and lemon rinds for homemade vegetable stock or cleaning solutions.

The fermented fennel component requires preparation 3-5 days in advance. Alternatively, a quick pickle can be made by brining thinly sliced fennel in a hot solution of water, vinegar, salt, and sugar for at least 30 minutes, though true fermentation offers deeper flavor and probiotic benefits.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Crispy Pancetta, Broccoli Rabe, and Spinach
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of Orecchiette with Crispy Pancetta, Broccoli Rabe, and Spinach is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl. The small, ear-shaped orecchiette pasta is mixed with vibrant green, sautéed broccoli rabe florets and leaves, and wilted spinach. Small, golden-brown crispy pancetta cubes are scattered throughout, adding texture and savory notes. The dish has a natural, slightly rustic appearance, with components touching and overlapping. The pasta is lightly coated in a glistening, subtle sauce from the cooking liquid. The colors are natural, showing the deep greens of the vegetables against the pale pasta and golden pancetta. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the bowl. A casually folded plain cloth napkin is nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. The background shows a hint of a lived-in family dining area with minimal, unfocused clutter, reinforcing a homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Trim tough ends from broccoli rabe. Cut into 5 cm pieces. Wash thoroughly.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli rabe. Blanch for 2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well.
Add orecchiette to the boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, dice pancetta into small cubes.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Leave rendered fat in the skillet.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes to the skillet with pancetta fat. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add blanched broccoli rabe to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes. Add fresh spinach. Cook until wilted.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with vegetables. Add crispy pancetta. Toss to combine.
Add reserved pasta water gradually, if needed, to create a light sauce. Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.
Broccoli rabe can be bitter; blanching helps to mellow its flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Harissa Shrimp with Fermented Fennel & Lemon Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone, showcasing its natural texture. A bed of gently sautéed, thinly sliced fresh fennel forms a natural base. Scattered over the fennel are 4-5 seared harissa shrimp, their vibrant orange-red hue contrasting with the pale fennel. Alongside, a small, organic cluster of translucent, thinly sliced fermented fennel adds a delicate, slightly pickled visual element. A generous, fluid drizzle of creamy, off-white lemon-parsley yogurt cascades naturally over parts of the shrimp and fennel. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley and a few delicate, feathery fennel fronds are placed sparingly on and around the dish. The arrangement is minimalist and unforced, allowing ample white space. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly folded beside the plate. Lighting is soft, natural, and diffused. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green from a potted plant.

ingredients.name: Large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Prepare Fermented Fennel: Thinly slice 1 fennel bulb. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 1 tsp salt in 250ml water. Pour brine over fennel to cover. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Prepare Lemon-Parsley Yogurt: In a small bowl, combine yogurt, half the chopped parsley, lemon zest, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Season with salt. Stir well. Set aside.
Prepare Harissa Shrimp: In a bowl, toss shrimp with harissa paste, 1 tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Marinate 10 minutes.
Cook Fennel: Thinly slice the remaining fresh fennel bulb. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced fresh fennel. Sauté 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Remove from pan.

Cook Shrimp: Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan. Increase heat to high. Add shrimp in a single layer. Sear 1-2 minutes per side until pink and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.

Assemble: Arrange sautéed fresh fennel on plates. Top with cooked harissa shrimp. Spoon fermented fennel alongside. Drizzle generously with lemon-parsley yogurt. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and fennel fronds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes with Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of roasted chicken and vegetables is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic dinner plate with a subtle rim. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, characteristic of a family kitchen. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is the centerpiece, placed slightly off-center. Alongside it are several thick-cut, golden-brown potato wedges, some showing their fluffy interior where slightly split, others with dark roasted edges. Scattered around the chicken and potatoes are bright green broccoli florets, some lightly charred at the edges, maintaining their shape and vibrant color. The chicken is cooked whole, not sliced. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and unfussy, as if served directly from the baking tray to the plate. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone and a basic fork and knife rest beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere with a hint of natural kitchen clutter in the background, like a salt and pepper shaker or a wooden cutting board, slightly out of focus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges.
Wash broccoli. Cut broccoli into small florets.
Peel and mince garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, 30ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, 3g rosemary, 3g thyme, 3g salt, and 1g black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange seasoned potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken with remaining 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, 2g rosemary, 2g thyme, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Place seasoned chicken thighs on the same baking tray with the potatoes, ensuring skin side is up.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove tray from oven. Add broccoli florets to the tray, tossing gently with some of the pan drippings. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Return tray to oven. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through, potatoes are tender and golden, and broccoli is crisp-tender.
Check chicken internal temperature with a meat thermometer. It must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Birria-Style Beef Quesatacos
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-crisp Birria-Style Beef Quesatacos are artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, slightly overlapping. The tortillas exhibit a deep orange-red hue from their consomé dip, with perfectly browned, slightly charred edges that highlight their crisp texture. Shredded, tender braised beef, rich and savory, peeks from within the folded tortillas, along with streaks of melted, slightly browned Oaxaca cheese. Beside the quesatacos, a small, vibrant red-orange ceramic bowl holds the rich consomé for dipping. A fresh, bright corn salsa, featuring vibrant yellow corn kernels, finely diced red onion, and verdant green cilantro, forms a small, neat mound beside the tacos. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro and finely diced white onion over the tacos, and a bright green lime wedge rests beside the consomé bowl. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting that enhances the dish's inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of the rich consomé for dipping
Garnish with fresh lime wedges
Top with finely diced white onion and fresh cilantro
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Season beef chunks with salt and pepper. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Place dried guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles in a bowl. Cover with boiling water. Let steep for 15 minutes until softened.
In the same pot, add chopped onion, garlic, and quartered tomatoes. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.

Drain softened chiles. Transfer chiles, sautéed vegetables, cumin, oregano, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, and cayenne pepper (if using) to a blender. Add 250 ml of beef broth and apple cider vinegar. Blend until a smooth adobo paste forms. Add more broth if needed to blend.
Return seared beef to the Dutch oven. Pour the adobo paste over the beef. Add remaining 500 ml beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef using two forks. Strain the braising liquid (consomé) through a fine-mesh sieve into a separate bowl, discarding solids. Skim excess fat from the consomé.
In a medium bowl, combine fresh corn kernels, half of the chopped cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt.
Heat a large griddle or non-stick pan over medium heat. Dip each corn tortilla briefly into the strained consomé, coating both sides.
Place dipped tortilla on the hot griddle. Sprinkle shredded Oaxaca cheese on one half of the tortilla. Add a generous portion of shredded beef over the cheese.

Once the cheese starts to melt and the tortilla crisps, fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling to form a taco. Press gently with a spatula. Cook until golden brown and crispy on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Repeat with remaining tortillas, cheese, and beef.

Serve Birria-Style Beef Quesatacos immediately with a small bowl of the reserved consomé for dipping, a side of the fresh corn salsa, remaining chopped cilantro, finely diced white onion, and lime wedges.
notes: For a spicier adobo, increase the number of arbol chiles or add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
The consomé is essential for dipping and adds immense flavor. Do not discard it.
Oaxaca cheese is traditional, but Monterey Jack or a good melting mozzarella can be substituted.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Tinga
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork Tinga is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The shredded pork, richly coated in a vibrant reddish-brown, smoky chipotle-tomato sauce, forms a generous, organic mound. Visible within the sauce are soft, diced white onion and red bell pepper cubes, adding subtle textural contrast. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green cilantro and a small scattering of finely diced white onion, providing a fresh, bright counterpoint to the savory tinga. A single lime wedge rests neatly beside the main dish, ready to be squeezed. The plate sits on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. Adjacent to the plate, a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas is presented in a traditional, earthy-toned woven tortilla warmer or basket. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's inviting colors and textures, creating a casual yet professional restaurant aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with warm corn tortillas for making tacos or tostadas.
Offer lime wedges for a squeeze of fresh acidity.
Accompany with traditional Mexican rice and refried beans.
Provide a side of crumbled cotija cheese or a drizzle of crema for added richness.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Place pork in a large pot. Cover with water. Add half an onion and the bay leaf. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 1.5 to 2 hours. Skim any foam. Remove pork. Shred pork using two forks. Set aside.
While pork cooks, prepare sauce. Roughly chop tomatoes. Roughly chop one onion. Peel garlic cloves.
In a blender, combine chopped tomatoes, half of the chopped onion, garlic cloves, chipotle chilies, and chicken broth. Blend until smooth.
Dice the remaining half onion into small cubes. Dice the red bell pepper into small cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour the blended sauce into the skillet with the sautéed vegetables. Add dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.

Add the shredded pork to the sauce. Stir well to coat. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Finely chop fresh cilantro for garnish. Cut lime into wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Bacon Ragu with Pappardelle and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef and Bacon Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. Wide, golden pappardelle ribbons are loosely swirled, forming a generous base. A hearty scoop of rich, dark reddish-brown ragu is spooned over the pasta, showcasing tender, slow-braised beef chunks, crispy diced bacon, and halved, earthy brown mushrooms. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley contrasts the deep colors of the ragu, with a generous dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese over top. The dish is centered on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the rich sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 2-3 cm cubes. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces.
Finely dice onion and mince garlic.
Clean mushrooms and halve them.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add bacon to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and halved mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, and coffee. Add a pinch of salt and pepper.
Bring ragu to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove lid for the last 30 minutes of cooking to allow ragu to thicken.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
While ragu finishes, cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Toss cooked pappardelle with a generous amount of ragu. Serve immediately.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup with Crispy Sage and Garlic Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A warm, inviting starter portion of creamy, vibrant orange butternut squash soup rests in a clean white porcelain bowl. The soup's surface is smooth, with a subtle sheen. Scattered across the surface are golden-brown, small cubed garlic croutons, their edges crisp. A few deep green, crispy fried sage leaves are artfully placed, providing a contrasting color and texture. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center on a simple, rustic wooden table surface. Beside the bowl, a white cotton napkin is neatly folded, and a traditional silver soup spoon is placed to the right. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, hinting at a casual yet refined atmosphere. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich color and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Offer a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil at the table
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel butternut squash. Deseed. Cut into 2.5 cm cubes. Roughly chop onion. Leave garlic cloves unpeeled.
Toss squash, onion, and unpeeled garlic with 1 tablespoon olive oil on a baking tray. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes until squash is tender and lightly caramelized.
Remove garlic from skins. Discard skins.
Transfer roasted squash, onion, and peeled garlic to a large pot. Add chicken stock.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Carefully blend soup until smooth using an immersion blender or standing blender. If using standing blender, blend in batches.
Stir in cream. Reheat gently. Adjust seasoning.

For croutons: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Remove crusts from bread. Cut into 1 cm cubes. Mince 1 garlic clove. Add bread cubes and minced garlic to pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Remove croutons.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same pan. Add sage leaves. Fry briefly until crispy. Remove.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with garlic croutons and crispy sage leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Guisado con Tomillo y Cebolla
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic Mexican Pollo Guisado is presented on a simple, slightly chipped, terracotta-colored ceramic plate. A single portion of two braised chicken thighs, still on the bone, sits centrally. The chicken is deeply browned from searing, now richly coated in a thick, reddish-brown sauce. The sauce is flecked with soft, translucent slices of caramelized onion and hints of dark red from the rehydrated chilies. A few vibrant green fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the chicken, providing a subtle color contrast. The chicken itself is tender, almost falling off the bone, with its natural textures visible. Alongside the chicken, a modest mound of fluffy, orange-tinted Mexican red rice is spooned. Two warm, soft corn tortillas are casually folded and placed beside the chicken. The entire plate rests on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, showing natural grain. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping up the sauce.
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice (Arroz Rojo).
Offer refried beans (Frijoles Refritos) as an additional side.
Serve with a simple fresh salsa or pickled jalapeños.
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy. About 5-7 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
While onions cook, rehydrate dried chilies. Place ancho and guajillo chilies in a heatproof bowl. Pour hot water over them to cover. Let soak for 20 minutes until softened.

Drain rehydrated chilies. Transfer to a blender. Add 100 ml of chicken broth. Blend until smooth. Strain chili mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into the pot with onions, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.
Add diced tomatoes, remaining chicken broth, fresh thyme sprigs, and fresh savory sprigs to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove thyme and savory sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot.
notes: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs add more flavor and moisture. Remove skin before serving if preferred.
For a spicier dish, add a dried chile de árbol or a pinch of cayenne pepper to the sauce.
traditional_techniques: Rehydrating and blending dried chiles for sauce base

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs are nestled amidst a rustic stew of vibrant red and yellow bell pepper chunks, diced tomatoes, and translucent onion pieces. The seared chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender meat. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to ingredients. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is organic, with moderate negative space. Chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. The plate rests on a light wooden table, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and silver flatware. A rustic ceramic bowl of crusty bread and a simple green salad are nearby, completing the casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Simple green salad

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks
Yellow bell pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper chunks. Cook for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken stock, oregano, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 30-40 minutes. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Sustentable con Mole de Maíz Fermentado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken with Fermented Corn & Onion Mole is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in earthy cream. A generous pool of rich, dark amber mole, flecked with subtle textures, forms the base. Nestled within the mole is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh, its seared skin deeply golden and crisp, contrasting with the soft, simmering sauce. The chicken is not sliced. Bright magenta pickled red onion slivers are artfully scattered over and around the chicken, providing a vibrant pop of color and sharp contrast. Fresh green cilantro sprigs and a sprinkle of toasted pepitas add natural garnish. The composition emphasizes natural forms and ample negative space. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a small stack of warm corn tortillas in a simple basket and a small bowl of traditional escabeche. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors. An undyed linen napkin completes the eco-conscious setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Small side dish of escabeche (pickled vegetables)
Agua fresca

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, bell pepper tops, celery ends, onion skins)

instructions: Thinly slice half of the red onion. Place in a jar. Heat 120ml apple cider vinegar, 120ml water, and a pinch of salt until warm. Pour over sliced onions. Seal jar. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 200°C. On a baking sheet, toss the remaining half red onion (quartered), destemmed and deseeded Ancho chiles, destemmed and deseeded Guajillo chiles, unpeeled garlic cloves, halved tomato, and vegetable scraps with 1 tbsp olive oil. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly charred.

Remove stems from chiles. Peel garlic. Transfer roasted vegetables, chiles, garlic, and tomato to a blender. Add fermented corn masa and 120ml water. Blend until smooth. Add more water if needed for desired consistency. Season with salt.

Pat chicken dry. Season with salt, black pepper, chopped fresh thyme, and savory. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Pour mole over chicken in the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pan. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

Remove chicken from mole. Spoon mole onto plates. Place chicken on top of the mole. Garnish with pickled red onion slivers, fresh cilantro sprigs, and toasted pepitas. Serve immediately with warm corn tortillas.
notes: This recipe utilizes lacto-fermentation for the corn masa and pickled onions, enhancing flavor depth and aiding preservation.
Vegetable scraps are incorporated into the mole base, minimizing food waste.
The dish celebrates seasonal, local ingredients and sustainable cooking practices.
